Announcements
Participate in this study and earn 300 HKD! :) English learning from computer-mediated English reading  - Department of English
From: Jookyoung Jung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jookyoungjung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Participate in this study and earn 300 HKD! :)
English learning from computer-mediated English reading
Hello! I am Jookyoung Jung, Associate Professor at the Department of English. I'd like to invite you to a study that examines the relationship between computer-mediated English reading and English learning.
If you decide to participate, I will ask you to take part in three experimental sessions.
In Session 1, we will ask you to complete a brief questionnaire about yourself. Next, you will take English proficiency tests that measure your grammar and vocabulary.
In Session 2, you will read English texts while your eye movements are recorded using an eye-tracker.
In Session 3, you will take a series of memory tasks.
In return for your participation, I am able to offer you 300 HKD at the end of the 3rd session.
If you meet the criteria below, please join our study!
Your age is 18 years or older.
Chinese is your first language, and English is your second language.
Your English score (no lower, no higher!!): DSE English: 4-5; IELTS: 5.5-6.5; TOEFL iBT: 75-95; Cambridge English Scale: 160-180
If you want to participate in this study, please complete this online survey so that we can contact you and schedule your sessions.
Link:
https://forms.gle/9NyVzTHPBvW7wgHz6
If you have any queries about the study, please feel free to contact our team at tobiiproject2021@gmail.com. I would be very grateful if you would agree to take part! :-)
Jookyoung Jung

Chinese University of Hong Kong

title: Go Green Carnival (with Free Reuse Items Available ) 「綠」續園遊會（可免費領取重用物品）
bodyText:

Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/09/04
»
Events / Activities
Go Green Carnival (with Free Reuse Items Available ) 「綠」續園遊會（可免費領取重用物品） - Chung Chi College
From: Steven Hung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
stevenhung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【「綠」續園遊會】
同學剛剛入宿，需要些家品，但不想專程添置，可以怎辦？
為了提高同學對環保回收及減少碳排放的認識，並為年中退宿回收所得物品尋找新歸宿，學院環境及可持續發展委員會將聯同綠在沙田舉行「『綠』續園遊會」，從而善用資源，延續環保精神：
日期：9
月10
日（四）        |
時間：11:00 – 17:00
地點：龔約翰學生中心LG4
活動室
園遊會分成四大區域，包括—
入宿寶物市集：
衣架？二手衫？刀叉杯碗碟？收納用品？這裡應有盡有！市集上的物品主要來自五月份退宿回收所得，有待你慧眼「尋寶」，免費取用。
減碳挑戰站：
現場特設「碳足跡小挑戰」，挑戰者一邊手捧與生活碳排放量等重的箱子，一邊參與Kahoot! 問答，爭取登上龍虎榜！
一擊即中回收球：
生活中哪些物資可以回收？在這個遊戲，參與者以投球判斷各類回收品，兩者都看得準並不容易。
流水式工作坊X2
：
場內更有專人教授綠色手作—天然防蚊液適用於中大多山多水的環境；而扭蛋殼多肉盆栽「的骰」易養，放在宿舍或辦公室皆適合！
記得9月10日11:00，龔約翰LG4見！
【Go Green Carnival】
Just moved into the student hostel and need some household items, but do not want to buy something brand new — then what next?
To raise students’ awareness of recycling materials and reducing carbon emissions, and to find new owners for items collected during the mid-year Hostel Checkout Recycling, the College Environment and Sustainable Development Committee will co-organise with Green@ShaTin the “Go Green Carnival” to make good use of resources and extend the spirit of environmental protection:
Date: 10 September (Thursday)            |         Time: 11:00-17:00
Venue: KSC LG4 Activity Room, Chung Chi College
The Carnival is composed of four sections, including—
Free Reuse Market:
Hangers? Clothes? Cutlery, cups, and dinnerware? Storage items? There are always things for everyone! Most of them come from the Hostel Checkout Recycling collections in May.
Low-Carbon Challenge:
Challengers are invited to bear weight equivalent to carbon emissions in living, and at the same time take part in Kahoot! quizzes to compete in the leaderboard!
Eco Ball Tossing:
Participants will judge different recyclable items by throwing balls — getting both right is not as easy as it sounds.
Ongoing workshop x2:
Participants will be instructed in two DIY workshops — making natural bug spray suited to the CUHK environment and planting succulents in capsules that are easy to care for in hostels and offices.
Remember 11 am on 10 September. See you at KSC LG4!

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

We are now inviting Hong Kong young adults to participate in a bereavement survey, titled “Trajectories of grief outcomes and the associated psychosocial predictors among recently bereaved young adults in Hong Kong: A retrospective longitudinal mixed-methods approach”. Participants will receive up to HK$300 coupons upon completion.
Participant Inclusion Criteria:
Local young adults aged 18 to 29 residing in Hong Kong.
Have experienced the death of a close friend/relative or an important person within the past 18 months.
Able to read Chinese and communicate in Cantonese.
1) Baseline Questionnaire
- After signing the consent form, participants will complete a 20-minute baseline questionnaire.
- The questionnaire will include questions about grieving process in response to the death of a loved one or significant person, and attitudes toward death
- Participants will receive HK$100 coupons for completing the baseline questionnaire.
2) First Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months later, participants who have completed the baseline questionnaire will be invited to complete a follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the first follow-up questionnaire will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
3) Second Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months after the first follow-up questionnaire, participants who have completed the first follow-up questionnaire will be invited to complete a second follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the second follow-up questionnaire after will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
Participation in this study is voluntary. The study data will be kept confidential and no one other than the researchers will have access to the questionnaire information or audio recordings completed by the participants. This study has been approved by The Joint CUHK-NTEC CREC (CREC-2025.748) and the Survey and Behavioral Research Ethics Committee of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (SBRE‐24‐0378).
Please use the following link to fill out the consent form and questionnaire. Upon completion, you will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4SbSwIIE6shc67I
You are welcome to recommend this recruitment information to qualified young adults in Hong Kong.
For enquiries, please contact Dr. Ling
E-mail: haofengling@cuhk.edu.hk
WhatsApp: 44643831

NEWLY LAUNCHED! - UGEB2996 Getting to Know Speech and Language Impairment and the Role of Speech Therapist (Fully Online & Asynchronous Learning) 全新推出！UGEB2996 初探言語障礙與言語治療師角色 (全網上非同步學習) - Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: CHEUK KIT CHING

🆕
全新推出！
你是否曾遇過有溝通困難的人士，卻不知道如何與他們互動？你是否想了解言語障礙如何影響一個人的學習、社交及日常生活？
本課程將介紹言語及語言障礙（Speech and Language Impairment）的基本知識，以及言語治療師在支援有溝通需要人士方面的重要角色。課程透過由經驗言語治療師及教授團隊預備的動畫教學、模擬及真實臨床資料、及互動學習活動，幫助同學認識言語及語言障礙的影響，同時培養尊重、同理心及共融價值觀。
課程特色
自主安排學習時間，按個人進度完成課程
互動學習模式
真實及模擬臨床資料
提升對特殊教育需要（SEN）的認識
培養同理心、尊重與共融精神 適合任何學科背景同學修讀

課程編號：
UGEB2996

課程名稱：
初探言語障礙與言語治療師角色

授課模式：
網上非同步學習（Online Asynchronous）

學分：
1 學分
NEWLY LAUNCHED!
Have you ever wondered how communication disorders affect a person's daily life and learning? Would you like to understand the role of Speech Therapists and learn how to communicate more effectively with individuals with communication needs?
This course introduces the fundamentals of Speech and Language Disorders (types of Special Educational Needs), and the important role of the Speech Therapist in supporting individuals with such communication needs. Through animated tutorials by our experienced team of Speech Therapists and Professors, the use of simulated and/or real clinical data, and interactive learning activities, students will gain both knowledge and awareness of the impact of Speech and Language Disorders, whilst developing empathy, respect and inclusive values.
Course Highlights
Flexible self-paced online learning
Interactive learning activities
Real and simulated clinical data
Enhance awareness of Special Educational Needs (SEN)
Foster empathy, respect, and inclusion

Course Code:
UGEB2996

Course Title:
Getting to Know Speech and Language Impairment and the Role of Speech Therapist

Mode:
Online Asynchronous

Credits:
1 Unit

NEWLY LAUNCHED! - UGEB2996 Getting to Know Speech and Language Impairment and the Role of Speech Therapist (Fully Online & Asynchronous Learning) 全新推出！UGEB2996 初探言語障礙與言語治療師角色 (全網上非同步學習) - Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: CHEUK KIT CHING
cynthiacheuk@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
🆕
全新推出！
你是否曾遇過有溝通困難的人士，卻不知道如何與他們互動？你是否想了解言語障礙如何影響一個人的學習、社交及日常生活？
本課程將介紹言語及語言障礙（Speech and Language Impairment）的基本知識，以及言語治療師在支援有溝通需要人士方面的重要角色。課程透過由經驗言語治療師及教授團隊預備的動畫教學、模擬及真實臨床資料、及互動學習活動，幫助同學認識言語及語言障礙的影響，同時培養尊重、同理心及共融價值觀。
課程特色
自主安排學習時間，按個人進度完成課程
互動學習模式
真實及模擬臨床資料
提升對特殊教育需要（SEN）的認識
培養同理心、尊重與共融精神 適合任何學科背景同學修讀

課程編號：
UGEB2996

課程名稱：
初探言語障礙與言語治療師角色

授課模式：
網上非同步學習（Online Asynchronous）

學分：
1 學分
NEWLY LAUNCHED!
Have you ever wondered how communication disorders affect a person's daily life and learning? Would you like to understand the role of Speech Therapists and learn how to communicate more effectively with individuals with communication needs?
This course introduces the fundamentals of Speech and Language Disorders (types of Special Educational Needs), and the important role of the Speech Therapist in supporting individuals with such communication needs. Through animated tutorials by our experienced team of Speech Therapists and Professors, the use of simulated and/or real clinical data, and interactive learning activities, students will gain both knowledge and awareness of the impact of Speech and Language Disorders, whilst developing empathy, respect and inclusive values.
Course Highlights
Flexible self-paced online learning
Interactive learning activities
Real and simulated clinical data
Enhance awareness of Special Educational Needs (SEN)
Foster empathy, respect, and inclusion

Course Code:
UGEB2996

Course Title:
Getting to Know Speech and Language Impairment and the Role of Speech Therapist

Mode:
Online Asynchronous

Credits:
1 Unit

title: Sustainable Development Goals × General Education (SDG Study Scheme) – Start Your Sustainability Journey in the new academic year!

Announcements
Sustainable Development Goals × General Education (SDG Study Scheme) – Start Your Sustainability Journey in the new academic year!   - Office of University General Education
From: Office of University General Education
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
sdg-ouge@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

SDG Study Scheme
– Learn. Act. Achieve
Are you passionate about sustainability and making a real impact?
Join the
SDG Study Scheme
by the Office of University General Education (OUGE) – a unique opportunity to integrate the
United Nations’ 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
into your General Education journey at CUHK!

Why Join?
The SDG Study Scheme empowers you with essential knowledge and practical experience for tackling the challenges of tomorrow. This is your chance to showcase your sustainability competency and potential! Let’s be part of a community striving for a better future together!

What’s in the Scheme?
The SDG Study Scheme comprises three components, combining knowledge-based learning with experiential learning:
1.
Understand SDGs with a global vision
Finish the short online introductory course -
How to Achieve the SDGs
by the SDG Academy, and
pass
a
short
quiz
on the
SDG Community Blackboard site
.
2.
Equip yourself with SDG-related k
nowledge
Take
two to three
SDG-GE
(General Education) courses
, each carrying at least 2 units
:
Students admitted in
2021-22
: take at least
3
SDG-GE courses
Students admitted in
2022-23 or after
: take at least
2
SDG-GE courses
3.
Take action to help the communities
Complete one of the following action items:
one
SDG-SE (Social Engagement) course
of at least 2 units
; or
at least 26 hours
of co-curricular
Volunteer Activity (SDG-VA)
.
Learn more:
https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/sdg-study-scheme-overview/

Certification
Upon completing the Scheme, you will be awarded the
SDG Explorer Certificate
to recognize your achievements in both SDG knowledge and community engagement.
Apply for your certificate here:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=12998341

Actions to take!
1. Join the SDG Community!
Join the SDG Community to connect with like-minded students and receive updates on SDG-related activities and the SDG Study Scheme.
Sign up here:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=10231196
2. Enroll in SDG courses in Term 1!
Take your GE studies further – enroll in courses labelled with SDGs.
These courses not only enrich your sustainability competency but also empower you to engage with global and local sustainability challenges through meaningful learning and actions.
Browse the list of SDG-related GE courses offered in Term 1 and enroll early:
https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/wp-content/uploads/learning/2627T1_SDG-Class-Offerings.pdf
3. Follow us on Instagram and share with your friends!
Connect with us on Instagram at @
sdg_ge_cuhk
and scan the QR code below to follow us.

Enquiry
Email us at:
sdg-ouge@cuhk.edu.hk

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Temporary Closure of Open Space Staff Carpark Adjacent to Exit A of University Station
(Between 15 Sep and 31 Dec 2026)
To facilitate large scale lifting works for the construction of ‘Chung Chi College Project E Twin Building’, the open space staff carpark adjacent to Exit A of University Station will be temporarily closed between 15 Sep and 31 Dec 2026.  During this period, staff parking is available at the open space carparks adjacent to Exit D of University Station and outside Shanghai Fraternity Association. The paid shuttle light bus stop will be temporarily relocated to nearby No. 2 school bus stop at Station Piazza. For details, please refer to the attached layout plan.  Any inconvenience caused is apologized.

bodyText:

Events / Activities
Soi Cheang: Director's Talk 鄭保瑞導演講座：電影係我條命，咁…… - CUHK Library
From: The Chinese University of Hong Kong Library
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
liblc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Award-winning film director Soi Cheang comes to CUHK to share his personal journey of growing up, entering the film industry, and his creative experiences. The director once said that if cinema were taken away from his life, he would feel hollow. With over 30 years of experience behind the camera, his wealth of insights and behind-the-scenes stories will inspire anyone who loves film, and offer a fresh perspective on life and the art of cinema.
Date:
29 September 2026 (Tuesday)
Time:
2:30 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.
Speaker:
Mr. Soi Cheang, Hong Kong Film Award-winning Director
Guest Moderator:
Professor Fung Ying Him, Dean of the Faculty of Social Science
Language:
Cantonese
Venue:
VR Zone, Learning Garden, LG/F, University Library
Target Audience:
CUHK students and staff (a limited number of seats reserved for alumni)
Fee:
Free of charge. Registration is on a first-come, first-served basis.
Registration:
CUHK Students and Staff:
https://webapp.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/ras/restricted/event?id=112505
CUHK Alumni:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13738165
Co-organisers:
University Library
Independent Learning Centre
Office of Student Affairs
Faculty of Social Science
日期：
2026年9月29日（星期二）
時間：
下午二時三十分至四時
講者：
金像導演鄭保瑞先生
嘉賓主持：
社會科學院院長馮應謙教授
語言：
粵語
地點：
大學圖書館地庫進學園 虛擬實境空間
對象：
中大學生及教職員 (預留少量名額予校友)
費用：
免費參加，先到先得
活動簡介：
金像導演鄭保瑞親臨中大校園，與師生分享成長、入行及創作經歷。導演說過，如果將電影從他的生命裡抹掉，他將變成一片空白。從事電影行業超過30年，他豐富的幕後歷練與創作心得必能喚起大家對人生的體悟，並為每個熱愛電影的人帶來新的觀影視角。
講者簡介：
鄭保瑞，香港電影導演、監製、編劇、演員，以動作、驚慄風格見長，主要作品有《意外》、《車手》、《殺破狼II》、在法國票房理想的《智齒》、榮獲金像獎最佳導演獎的《命案》和《九龍城寨之圍城》。

金像導演鄭保瑞親臨中大校園，與師生分享成長、入行及創作經歷。導演說過，如果將電影從他的生命裡抹掉，他將變成一片空白。從事電影行業超過30年，他豐富的幕後歷練與創作心得必能喚起大家對人生的體悟，並為每個熱愛電影的人帶來新的觀影視角。
講者簡介：
鄭保瑞，香港電影導演、監製、編劇、演員，以動作、驚慄風格見長，主要作品有《意外》、《車手》、《殺破狼II》、在法國票房理想的《智齒》、榮獲金像獎最佳導演獎的《命案》和《九龍城寨之圍城》。

Undergraduate students wanted for a FYP survey analysing whether CUHK canteens can handle the demands in the future  - Chung Chi College
From: Chiu Kwok Shing, with endorsement of the course supervisor Dr. Ng Chi Kong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155212981@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Hello, we are students from GECC4130. We noticed that there are quite some
changes for student canteens in CUHK over the years, and wondered whether
the current situation could meet the future demand. As Chung Chi College,
Wu Yee Sun College, and Shaw College are building additional hostels
currently, and there will be one more postgraduate student hostel, we are
afraid that more students living on campus will overwhelm the student
canteens. Therefore, we would like to collect data about the general
experience of undergraduate students at university outlets as well as how
additional hostels may affect the demand for CUHK canteen services.
If you find our study meaningful or would like to share your
experience/opinion with us to let more people know how the catering
services in CUHK are doing, we would be grateful that you could spend some
time taking the following survey:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cAuL2gHWQdbgGyO
If you have any questions, please don't hesitate to contact
1155212981@link.cuhk.edu.hk (Ken). Thank you!

From: Lewina Lee

nac@cuhk.edu.hk

二
○
二六至二七年度「新亞書院文化講座」第一講
「新亞書院文化講座」由香港中文大學新亞書院與新亞書院校友會合辦、新亞中學協辦，每年舉辦兩至三次講座。本年度第一場講座將於二Ｏ二六年九月十九日舉行，主講嘉賓為張倩儀博士。講座詳情如下：
講題：絲路上不容錯過的訊息
講者：張倩儀博士 (中大校友，文化學者、出版人及遊記作家)
主持：陳柏嘉博士 (香港中文大學新亞書院文化講座委員會成員、香港中文大學自學中心講師)
日期：二Ｏ二六年九月十九日 ( 星期六 )
時間：下午四時正
地點：香港九龍土瓜灣農圃道六號新亞中學禮堂 ( 經合一道校門進入 )
截止日期：九月十六日 ( 星期三 )
網上報名：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13740249
講座內容摘要：
海陸絲路歷史悠久，道里漫長，資料繁多，著作亦汗牛充棟。這次講座從中國歷史的角度，探索絲路沿線一些值得我們注意的實物訊息。這些訊息不限一時一地，因此不免零散，但有助我們認識絲路、補充中國歷史，甚至起到促進思考的作用。
講座以粵語講述。歡迎聽講，免費入場。歡迎參加者親臨現場或以網上連結聽講。
如有查詢，請與新亞書院院務室聯絡（電話︰3943-7609；電郵︰
nac@cuhk.edu.hk
）。
New Asia College Cultural Talks 202

There are two to three talks in each academic year. The first talk will be held on 19 September 2026. It is our honour to invite Dr. CHEUNG Shin Yee as our speaker. Details are as follows:

Moderator: Dr. Parker CHAN (Member of Committee on New Asia College Cultural Talks, Lecturer of CUHK Independent Learning Centre)
Date: 19 September 2026 (Saturday)
Time: 4:00pm
Venue: School hall, New Asia Middle School (through the school entrance at Hop Yat Road), 6 Farm Road, Tokwawan, Kowloon, Hong Kong
Deadline: 16 September,2026 (Wed)
Online Application:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13740249

講座以粵語講述。歡迎聽講，免費入場。歡迎參加者親臨現場或以網上連結聽講。

From: Learning and Cultural Enhancement Section

The International Connection Programme (ICP) is a cross-cultural peer mentorship programme organized by the Office of Student Affairs, which offers a unique opportunity for students from diverse backgrounds to connect and enhance cultural understanding. We warmly invite you to join us as a mentee, where you will have the chance to:
Build intercultural mentoring networks by connecting with senior students
Facilitate your transition and adjustment to the university life
Engage in enriching cross-cultural interactions and contribute to a more culturally inclusive and diverse campus
Eligibility
Year 1 non-local undergraduate students who will be studying at CUHK in both terms of 2026-27.
Matching
In each group, two mentors will be matched up with approximately four mentees.
Content
1.
Training Day Camp
All participants will be required to attend the training day camp. Free of charge.
Date: 4 October 2026 (Sunday)
Time: 9:00am – 4:00pm (Round-trip transportation will be arranged)
Location: Tai Po
Content: Ice-breaking, team building, cross-cultural communication skills, global leadership development
2. Bonding and cultural activities initiated by your group
3. Engaging cultural events organized by the Office of Student Affairs
4. Visit to CUHK (Shenzhen)
5. Leadership and Cultural tour
Certification and Prize
Student Development Portfolio (SDP) record update
Certificate of Appreciation (Requirement: attendance in the training day camp, one LCES-endorsed activity, completion of self-initiated cultural activity and submission of report)
(For selected teams)
Leadership and cultural tour in 2027
Apply now to be part of this enriching initiative!

Master of Arts in Japanese Studies (2027-2028 intake) is now open for application!
We are pleased to announce that applications are now open for the 2027–28 Master of Arts in Japanese Studies (MAJS) Programme.
Our MAJS Programme offers comprehensive training in Japanese society, culture, history, and language. Designed for those seeking deeper academic engagement or professional opportunities related to Japan, the programme equips students with the knowledge and skills essential for careers in Japan-related fields or further academic pursuits.
Whether you're passionate about Japanese studies or planning a career with a Japan focus, this programme is your gateway to meaningful growth and development.
For more information about the programme, please visit:
https://www.jas.cuhk.edu.hk/tc/programmes/ma-in-japanese-studies/
Application deadline:
1st round: 30 September 2026
2nd round: 30 November 2026

中大迎新與開學的季節又到來，位於山腰的中大出版社小書店很想跟大家打招呼！
為了鼓勵大家坐 3 分鐘校巴，或爬 5 分鐘山路走到「何東夫人堂」，看看出版社的書與一系列文創產品，我們在 9 月 7 日至 9 月 25 日期間，特別準備了「中大人限定」的開Sem見面禮三重奏：

精神福袋（免費拎）
•
來了就送
：$30 現金券 + 小書店探訪指南 + 隨機好禮（如 Reading Trail 運動毛巾）
•
打卡再送
：於 IG / Threads / 小紅書 / 朋友圈打卡，再送香港作家西西「朋友的貓」系列襟章（蹲貓、懶貓、企貓、睡貓）
2⃣
一籃子 75 折選書
• 特別優惠
：中大人平日享 8 折，活動期間 12 本精選好書加碼至
75 折
！（把握 add-drop period 的歡樂時光⋯⋯）
•
精選書單
：《我這一代人》、《尋找國家中的婦女》、《灣區變形》、《新家庭主義興衰》、《Hong Kong Art Deco Architecture》、《供水香港》、《大學的讀法》、《種植生活》、《從彼島到此島》、《清音與破曉》、《歷史學的訓練》、《虛擬親密》

小書店印章放題
• 歷年「她的現代史」、「小王子的領悟」、「香港原生植物」、「小書店/何東夫人堂」、「閱讀不用等待」、「香港街市」等全套紀念印章一次過登場，歡迎帶手帳來蓋好蓋滿！

Seminars / Forums / Programmes / Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre (ILC) offers a wide range of workshops and activities to support learning of language and communication skills. Visit our website for more information: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ (20260907)  - ILC
From: ILC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ilc-counsel@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【Weekly Highlights - English Section 】
A. Communication, Study Skills and Job Preparation Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre offers English workshops 7 September to 11 September: (1) Discussion Skills and Current Affairs - Speaking with Confidence, (2) Listening to Learn: Academic Listening and Note-taking Skills, (3) Study Skills in English at University Level, and (4) Saying What You Mean - English Pronunciation for Cantonese and Mandarin Speakers. These workshops are now available for registration at: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in English
Consultation service is available during the following time:
7 September (Mon): 14:30 – 16:30
9 September (Wed): 10:30 – 12:30
11 September (Fri): 14:30 – 16:30
Online Booking:
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
More Timeslot please check our website：
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EH/consultation.aspx
====================================
【Weekly Highlights - Chinese Section 】中文部本週活動
A. Chinese Workshops 中文工作坊
The Independent Learning Centre offers Chinese workshops 7 September to 11 September: (1) CRE Vocabulary and the Use of Idioms, (2) JRE Argumentative Writing II, and (3) BLNST Basic Law Test. These workshops are now available for registration at: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
自學中心九月七日至九月十一日舉辦 (1) 公務員綜合招聘試系列(CRE)：現代漢語詞匯與成語的運用, (2) 公務員綜合招聘考試系列(CRE)：能力傾向測試, (3) CRE中文運用應試實戰班：閱讀理解 (粵), (4) JRE 議論文寫作(II), 及 (5) BLNST基本法及香港國安法測試 (國安法部份)等工作坊，歡迎報名。
登記連結： https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in Chinese 自學中心中文輔導服務
Consultation service is available during the following time:
自學中心於九月七日至九月十一日提供以下中文輔導時段。
7 September (Mon): 10:30 – 12:30 and 14:30 – 16:30
8 September (Tue): 10:30 – 12:30
9 September (Wed): 10:30 – 12:30
10 September (Thu): 10:30 – 12:30 and 14:30 – 16:30
網上預約：
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
更多中文輔導時段。
====================================
C. “The Power of Words” 「書寫力量」
This is a reading and writing event organized by the ILC, Hong Kong Literature Research Centre, the Office of Arts Administrator (OAA) and Tolopoem. Activities we have this semester include Blackboard / Glass Wall Poems, Talks of Dialogue in the Arts and Workshops.
自學中心、香港文學研究中心、藝術行政主任辦公室及吐露詩社合辦的大型閱讀及寫作活動。這個學期的活動，除黑板詩及玻璃詩外，還有藝文縱談及各式工作坊。各項活動的資料可以參看：https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/Event/thepowerofwords.aspx
====================================
【Independent Online Learning Resources】自學中心網上自學資源
A. Independent Online Learning Resources in English
- Academic Writing
Visit this link on academic writing skills and convention for different citation styles:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Writing.aspx
- Vocabulary
Visit this link for both General Vocabulary and Specific Vocabulary (e.g. For Business and Medical Professionals) lists and practices:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Vocab.aspx
- Job Search and Interviews
Visit this link to identify your capabilities and personality types, learn how to prepare job search documents and personal statements, and how to get ready for job interviews:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx
B. Independent Online Learning Resources in Chinese中文網上自學材料
- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html
- Argumentative Writing議論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on the structure, the content and the language of argumentative writing.
介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html
- Cantonese Pronunciation粵語拼音速遞
This guide is designed for mainland students as an effective way to learn Cantonese pronunciation. Basic knowledge of Cantonese syllables is introduced with exercises. Comparison of Cantonese and Putonghua pronunciation is also highlighted
協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html
- Cantonese Express港式粵語速遞
An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx
- Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) 中國語言及文化自學資源網
Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.
中國語言及文化自學資源網(OPSCL)為一推薦自學資源之網上平台。平台為有意學習普通話、粵語、漢字、中國文化或香港文化等五大範疇的人士提供中文及英文雙語之學習資源，以推動自主學習與終身學習。平台內推薦的資源均附有簡介及評語，使用者可按自身需要搜尋學習資源，並在使用後給予評分或評論，以備其他使用者參考。此外，平台設有「自評系統」，使用者可通過完成自評，確定自身的學習起步點，從而尋找適合自己程度的學習資源。
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/EN/index.aspx
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/TC/index.aspx
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/SC/index.aspx

This is a reading and writing event organized by the ILC, Hong Kong Literature Research Centre, the Office of Arts Administrator (OAA) and Tolopoem. Activities we have this semester include Blackboard / Glass Wall Poems, Talks of Dialogue in the Arts and Workshops.
自學中心、香港文學研究中心、藝術行政主任辦公室及吐露詩社合辦的大型閱讀及寫作活動。這個學期的活動，除黑板詩及玻璃詩外，還有藝文縱談及各式工作坊。各項活動的資料可以參看：https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/Event/thepowerofwords.aspx
====================================
【Independent Online Learning Resources】自學中心網上自學資源
A. Independent Online Learning Resources in English
- Academic Writing
Visit this link on academic writing skills and convention for different citation styles:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Writing.aspx
- Vocabulary
Visit this link for both General Vocabulary and Specific Vocabulary (e.g. For Business and Medical Professionals) lists and practices:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Vocab.aspx
- Job Search and Interviews
Visit this link to identify your capabilities and personality types, learn how to prepare job search documents and personal statements, and how to get ready for job interviews:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx
B. Independent Online Learning Resources in Chinese中文網上自學材料
- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html
- Argumentative Writing議論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on the structure, the content and the language of argumentative writing.
介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html
- Cantonese Pronunciation粵語拼音速遞
This guide is designed for mainland students as an effective way to learn Cantonese pronunciation. Basic knowledge of Cantonese syllables is introduced with exercises. Comparison of Cantonese and Putonghua pronunciation is also highlighted
協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html
- Cantonese Express港式粵語速遞
An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx

Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. title: Invitation to participate in "Study on Cultural Diversity and Adaptation among University Students in Hong Kong" 誠邀您參與「香港大學生的文化多樣性與適應研究 」
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/09/04
»
Announcements
Invitation to participate in "Study on Cultural Diversity and Adaptation among University Students in Hong Kong" 誠邀您參與「香港大學生的文化多樣性與適應研究 」 - Psychology
From: Alan Tong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
alantong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
您好！心理學系與香港理工大學應用社會科學系研究團隊正合作進行一項香港大學生的文化多樣性與適應研究 ，誠邀您參與。
研究目的是探討香港高等院校學生的文化背景對學業、社會適應等方面的影響，為政策及支援提出發展建議。本研究已獲得香港理工大學倫理委員會的批准（參考編號：HSEARS20250122009）。
參與條件如下：
18歲或以上
現就讀於教資會資助大學（即香港八大其中之一）
本科的全日制學生*，本地與非本地生皆可
能以中文或英文進行閱讀、書寫與交流
*兼讀制學生、交換生和副學位課程的學生不符合參與條
件
研究活動：
網上問卷調查（2026年9月10日截止報名）
問卷包含有關文化取向與認同、語言能力、心理與社會適應、政策態度、健康狀況等方面的問題，完成需時約45分鐘，可於方便的時間自行填寫。完成後可獲得津貼HKD100，將以轉數快或Payme派發。
若有興趣參與，請填寫報名表：
https://hkpuhealthandsocial.au1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_ctN4pvNb9g8jGyq
如有查詢，請聯絡心理學系湯俊逸教授(
alantong@cuhk.edu.hk
) 或 理工大學研究人員陸依晴博士(電郵：
erin.lu@polyu.edu.hk
)。
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hello! Department of Psychology is collaborating with the Department of Applied Social Sciences at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU) on a study on Cultural Diversity and Adaptation among University Students in Hong Kong. We sincerely invites you to participate in this study.
The study aims to examine how university students’ cultural backgrounds influence their academic and social adaptation at Hong Kong’s universities and to generate insights to inform the development of relevant policies and support measures. This study has been approved by the Human Subjects Ethics Application Review System (HSEARS) of PolyU (Reference No.: HSEARS20250122009).
Eligibility criteria:
Aged 18 or above
Currently studying at a UGC‑funded university (i.e., one of Hong Kong’s eight public universities)
Full‑time undergraduate student*, either local or non-local
Able to read, write, and communicate in Chinese or English
*Part‑time students, exchange students, and students of sub-degree programs are not eligible.
Research activity:
Online Survey (Registration Closes on 10 September 2026)
The survey includes questions about cultural orientation and identity, language proficiency, psychological and social adaptation, policy attitudes, health conditions, etc. It takes about 45 minutes to complete, and participants can complete in their own time. Upon completion, you will receive an HKD 100 allowance, which will be distributed via FPS or PayMe.
If you are interested in participating, please fill in the registration form:
https://hkpuhealthandsocial.au1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_ctN4pvNb9g8jGyq
For inquiries, please contact Prof. Alan Tong at Department of Psychology (
alantong@cuhk.edu.hk
) or Dr Erin Lu (
erin.lu@polyu.edu.hk
) at PolyU.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

From: Jockey Club Museum of Climate Change (MoCC)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jaysonchan@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
［現正接受報名］
賽馬會氣候變化博物館大使
2026/27
（上學期）
Calling for CUHK Students: MoCC Ambassadorship 2026/27 (1st-semester Cohort)
(See the English version after the Chinese version)
►
觀看博物館大使影片
◄
2026/27年度
賽馬會氣候變化博物館大使計劃
（上學期）現正接受申請。
賽馬會氣候變化博物館
誠邀所有中大全日制學生報名，一起推動氣候行動。
賽馬會氣候變化博物館大使
與博物館教育活動和日常運作息息相關，更是未來在社會推動可持續發展的領袖。入選的學生將會接受培訓，參與博物館的日常運作，例如接待訪客和帶領導賞團等，亦有機會協助籌辦博物館活動，如工作坊和外展教育活動。
此外，你亦
：
可以獲得免費培訓及專業發展；
有機會獲得旅費資助，出席COP31及其他國際會議；
有機會接受電台及其他媒體的訪問。
如果你：
就讀中大全日制課程（任何學科）；
享受與不同年齡和背景的人交流，並希望加強溝通和交流技巧；
期望擁有充實的大學生活和豐富的履歷表；或
希望為地球出一分力，倡導和推動氣候行動，
請即填妥
網上報名表
，成為我們的一分子！
截止報名日期：2026年9月23日（星期三）晚上11時59分
計劃詳情：
https://www.mocc.cuhk.edu.hk/mocc-ambassadorship
如有查詢，請致電3943 0817或電郵至
jaysonchan@cuhk.edu.hk
與陳先生聯絡。
►
Watch the MoCC Ambassadorship Video
◄
Applications for the 1st-semester cohort of the MoCC Ambassadorship 2026/27 are now open.  All full-time students of CUHK, regardless of academic background(s), are eligible to apply for promoting climate action.
MoCC Ambassadors are an integral part of the education and operations of the
Jockey Club Museum of Climate Change
(MoCC), and they are the future sustainability leaders of the society.  Selected students are given effective and engaging training and all-rounded service-learning opportunities.  For example, they will guide visitors on MoCC tours, assist in the MoCC’s outreach activities, workshops and climate education projects.
As an ambassador, you will also:
Receive free training and professional development;
Have the opportunity to receive a travel grant to attend COP31 and other international conferences;
Have the opportunity to be interviewed by radio and other media outlets.
Join us if you:
are a full-time CUHK student;
enjoy interacting with diverse audiences, from kindergarten children to senior citizens, and wish to develop your interpersonal and communication skills;
look forward to enriching your university experience and enhancing your CV; or
are committed to climate leadership and action.
Deadline: 11:59 pm, 23 September 2026 (Wednesday)
Online application
and details:
https://www.mocc.cuhk.edu.hk/mocc-ambassadorship
You are welcome to contact Mr Jayson Chan at 3943 0817 or
jaysonchan@cuhk.edu.hk
if you have any questions.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

bodyText:

Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/09/04
»
Announcements
[30-min Online Study - Organ Donation] Earn HKD 100 Cash/gift voucher 【線上問卷/研究邀請】30 分鐘現賺 HKD 100 現金/等额礼品券補償 - Department of Educational Psychology
From: Mia Liang
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155106133@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
***請勿重複報名***
研究項目：
香港大學生器官捐贈意願實驗
Research Project:
Organ Donation Intentions in Hong Kong University Students
您好！我們誠邀香港中文大學的本科生（需為香港永久居民）參與一項關於器官捐贈意向的在線研究實驗。
Hello! We cordially invite
CUHK undergraduate students (must be Hong Kong permanent residents)
to participate in an online research study regarding organ donation intentions.
參與流程與重要說明：
為了確保研究數據的質量與您的填寫體驗，請務必閱讀以下細則：
設備建議：
為保證填寫的便利性與數據質量，
強烈建議使用電腦
完成本研究。
實驗組成：
本研究包含
兩個部分
。參與者必須完成全部兩個部分才能獲得現金補償。
特別注意：
完成第一部分後，需
間隔
24
小時
方可進行第二部分，請您預留充分的時間。
完成實驗總時長約為
30-40
分鐘
參與資格提示：
實驗系統設有篩選機制。如果在實驗過程中彈出「您無法參與本實驗」的提示，則證明您未通過篩選或喪失資格，屆時將無法獲得補償。
知情同意：
在填寫問卷前，您需要簽署一份知情同意書 。
Participation Process & Important Notes:
To ensure the quality of research data and a smooth experience, please read the following details carefully:
Device Recommendation:
To ensure ease of completion and data quality, it is
strongly recommended to use a computer
to complete this study.
Study Structure:
This study consists of
two parts
. Participants must complete both parts to be eligible for cash compensation.
Special Note:
There is a mandatory
24-hour interval
between the first and second parts. Please set aside sufficient time.
Total Duration:
The total time to complete the study is approximately
30-40 minutes
.
Participation Eligibility:
The system includes a screening mechanism. If a message stating
"You are not able to participant this study"
pops up during the process, it indicates that you have not passed the screening or have lost eligibility, and no compensation will be provided.
Informed Consent:
Before starting the questionnaire, you will be required to sign an
informed consent form
.
補償金額：
完成全部分兩階段的實驗後，您將獲得
100
港幣
的現金補償 。
備註：如您已參加過本實驗，請勿重複報名，重複報名將被視為無效 。
Compensation:
Upon completing both stages of the experiment, you will receive
HKD 100 in cash
as monetary compensation.
Note: If you have already participated in this experiment, please do not sign up again. Duplicate registrations will be considered invalid.
參與條件：
持有香港永久居民身份的香港中文大學在讀本科生 。
未報名成為一名器官捐贈者
無抑鬱症確診史
Requirements:
Current CUHK undergraduate students who are
Hong Kong permanent residents
.
Have
not
registered as an organ donor.
No clinical history of depression.
報名與查詢
(Registration and Inquiries)
：
如您對此研究感興趣，請點擊以下鏈接登記您的基本信息。我們將聯繫符合篩選標準的參與者，所有資料將嚴格保密 ：

登記鏈接：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9AeND44CLWQLaBM
如果您有任何疑問，請聯繫：
研究員：
梁菀洺女士 (Mia Liang)
1155106133@link.cuhk.edu.hk
導師：
謝志成教授 (Prof. Tse Chi-Shing)
cstse@cuhk.edu.hk
Registration and Inquiries:
If you are interested in this research project, please click the link below to register your basic information. We will contact participants who meet our selection criteria as soon as possible. All provided information will be kept strictly confidential:

Registration Link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9AeND44CLWQLaBM
If you have any questions or inquiries regarding this project, please contact:
Researcher:
Ms. Mia Liang
1155106133@link.cuhk.edu.hk
Supervisor:
Prof. Tse Chi-Shing
cstse@cuhk.edu.hk

為了確保研究數據的質量與您的填寫體驗，請務必閱讀以下細則：
設備建議：
為保證填寫的便利性與數據質量，
強烈建議使用電腦
完成本研究。
實驗組成：
本研究包含
兩個部分
。參與者必須完成全部兩個部分才能獲得現金補償。
特別注意：
完成第一部分後，需
間隔
24
小時
方可進行第二部分，請您預留充分的時間。
完成實驗總時長約為
30-40
分鐘
參與資格提示：
實驗系統設有篩選機制。如果在實驗過程中彈出「您無法參與本實驗」的提示，則證明您未通過篩選或喪失資格，屆時將無法獲得補償。
知情同意：
在填寫問卷前，您需要簽署一份知情同意書 。
Participation Process & Important Notes:
To ensure the quality of research data and a smooth experience, please read the following details carefully:
Device Recommendation:
To ensure ease of completion and data quality, it is
strongly recommended to use a computer
to complete this study.
Study Structure:
This study consists of
two parts
. Participants must complete both parts to be eligible for cash compensation.
Special Note:
There is a mandatory
24-hour interval
between the first and second parts. Please set aside sufficient time.
Total Duration:
The total time to complete the study is approximately
30-40 minutes
.
Participation Eligibility:
The system includes a screening mechanism. If a message stating
"You are not able to participant this study"
pops up during the process, it indicates that you have not passed the screening or have lost eligibility, and no compensation will be provided.
Informed Consent:
Before starting the questionnaire, you will be required to sign an
informed consent form
.
補償金額：
完成全部分兩階段的實驗後，您將獲得
100
港幣
的現金補償 。
備註：如您已參加過本實驗，請勿重複報名，重複報名將被視為無效 。
Compensation:
Upon completing both stages of the experiment, you will receive
HKD 100 in cash
as monetary compensation.
Note: If you have already participated in this experiment, please do not sign up again. Duplicate registrations will be considered invalid.
參與條件：
持有香港永久居民身份的香港中文大學在讀本科生 。
未報名成為一名器官捐贈者
無抑鬱症確診史
Requirements:
Current CUHK undergraduate students who are
Hong Kong permanent residents
.
Have
not
registered as an organ donor.
No clinical history of depression.

Announcements
Student Helper Recruitment 學生助理招募 - Curriculum and Instruction
From: Zhoutiao LI
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
zhoutiaoli@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Support University Research on Student Well-being & Resilience
We are recruiting
Student Helpers
to support two university research projects focusing on
student well-being, resilience, and university experiences
.
As a Student Helper, you will assist the research team in collecting questionnaire responses from university students and contribute to meaningful academic research.
Your Responsibilities
You will:
Invite eligible students to participate in online surveys
Share survey invitations through your student networks
Encourage students to complete questionnaires and collect valid responses
Who Can Apply?
We welcome:
CUHK undergraduate students
CUHK postgraduate students
Students with good communication skills and access to student networks
No previous research experience is required.
Reward

HK$20 for every valid response collected
Example:
40 valid responses = HK$800 reward
There is
no upper limit
. The more valid responses you help collect, the more you can earn.
Certificate Recognition
Students who successfully collect
40+ valid responses
will receive:

Official Certificate of Academic Research Participation
Why Join?
By joining as a Student Helper, you can:
⭐ Gain experience in university research and data collection
⭐ Develop communication and organizational skills
⭐ Strengthen your CV with research experience
⭐ Contribute to improving student support and university education

Interested students are welcome to apply now.
支援大學研究，累積研究經驗
我們現正招募
Student Helpers
（學生助理），協助兩項關於學生身心健康、抗逆力及大學學習經歷的大學研究項目。
作為 Student Helper，你將協助研究團隊收集學生問卷數據，參與具意義的大學研究，並了解實際學術研究及資料收集流程。
工作內容
你將協助：
邀請合資格學生參與網上問卷調查
通過個人學生網絡分享研究邀請
鼓勵學生完成問卷，並收集有效數據
申請資格
歡迎以下同學申請：
香港中文大學本科生（優先考慮）
香港中文大學研究生
具備良好溝通能力及學生網絡
對教育、心理學、學生發展或研究工作有興趣的同學
無需相關研究經驗。
研究貢獻獎勵
每份有效問卷可獲 HK$20 獎勵
例如：
40 份有效問卷 = HK$800 獎勵
沒有最高限制。協助收集越多有效問卷，獲得的獎勵越多。
證書認可
成功收集
40
份或以上有效問卷
的學生，將獲頒：
學術研究參與證書
以表彰你對大學研究的貢獻。
參與價值
加入 Student Helper 團隊，你可以：
⭐ 累積大學研究及數據收集經驗
⭐ 提升溝通及組織能力
⭐ 豐富個人履歷
⭐ 參與改善學生支持及大學教育的重要研究
有興趣參與的同學，歡迎立即申請。
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

From: Gender Research Centre

grcentre@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear all,
We warmly invite you to a book talk celebrating the launch of Professor Susanne Choi's new book,
Queer Resistance: Contesting State, Family, and Inequality in Post-Socialist China
.
Drawing on a decade of research, the book explores how LGBTQ+ individuals in post-socialist China navigate state governance, family expectations, gender norms, and social inequalities while seeking intimacy, dignity, and belonging.
Event Details
Speaker:
Professor Susanne Choi (Co-Director of Gender Research Centre; Professor of Department of Sociology, The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
Discussants:
Professor Travis Kong (Professor of the Department of Sociology, The University of Hong Kong);
Professor Lucetta Kam (Associate Professor in the Department of Humanities and Creative Writing, Hong Kong Baptist University)
Moderator:
Professor Lynne Nakano (Co-Director of Gender Research Centre; Professor and Chair of the Department of Japanese Studies, The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
Date:
9 October 2026
Time:
4:00 pm to 5:30 pm
Venue:
Room 422 (Conference Room), Department of Sociology, 4/F, Sino Building, CUHK
Format:
Onsite only

grcentre@cuhk.edu.hk
| (852) 3943 8775
Best regards,

From: Reimagining Yung Shue Au
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ysa-cuhk@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
「重塑榕樹凹：共創山海村落」—
地方營造大使招募
中文大學建築學院現正推動一項以「鄉郊地方營造（Rural Placemaking）」為核心的鄉村學堂及暑期工作坊，誠邀熱愛香港鄉郊文化、樂於親身參與實作的你，一同走進榕樹凹，參與村落景觀的復育與共創行動。
計劃期間，我們將邀請香港建造學院團隊擔任導師，帶領參加者學習傳統建造工藝及鄉郊實踐技術。參加者可自選出席一天或多天工作坊。若完成九天的工作坊後，參加者將獲頒由中文大學建築學院及香港建造學院簽發之服務證書，以作嘉許。
榕樹凹介紹：
榕樹凹位於新界東北端，於三百多年前開基立村，是一條歷史悠久的客家溫姓村落，村落鼎盛時期曾有逾三百名居民。由於地理位置接近邊境，榕樹凹在1980年代曾設有英軍軍營，留下了一段獨特而鮮為人知的歷史印記。雖然村落現已無人居住，但村民近年積極推動復村工作，透過修復祖屋、整理村史、舉辦村宴及傳統儀式，如籌辦麒麟隊；重建社群連結與文化記憶，展現出對深厚的鄉土感情與文化傳承精神。
****************************************
願景
共創鄉郊地方營造：以低碳修復與地方記憶，重塑山海景觀。
空間實作：以小型建設改善路徑與休憩空間。
感官敘事：將歷史轉化為具體的景觀導覽。
​共創行動：透過行動連結設計思考與鄉村振興。
****************************************
活動地點： 新界沙頭角榕樹凹村
****************************************
工作坊形式及階段:
鄉村導賞：認識榕樹凹村落歷史，了解鄉郊地方營造與文化地景。
物資收集：在山海與村落之間收集可用材料。
景觀實踐*：進行場地清理及空間建設實作，由香港建造學院導師帶領鄉村學堂，教授鄉郊景觀實踐技藝與傳統建造方法。
（ *
代表當日將由建造學院導師帶領鄉村學堂及景觀實踐活動。）
9
月
8日（二）、15日（二）、16日（三）*、17日（四）*、22日（二）
實際工作坊日期將視乎報名人數、天氣及工作人員情況作適當調整，包括增加或減少工作坊次數，屈時會通知相關參加者及在宣傳平台上公布。
- 參加者可因應自身時間安排，選擇參與單日或多日工作坊。
- 請參加者選擇所有可出席日期，以便主辦單位安排及分組。
- 導賞活動日期將稍後公布，會安排在平日和假日或工作坊期間舉行。
- 實際工作坊日期將視乎報名人數、天氣及現場情況作適當調整，並另行通知相關參加者。
- 如出席一節鄉村導賞、八節工作坊可獲中大建築學院及香港建造學院之義工服務證書。
*************************************
活動時間：早上 09:00 至 下午 04:00
名額：每節12人。
*************************************
對象：
* 身體狀況良好，能應付長時間戶外活動人士
* 對建築、景觀設計、保育等感興趣的人士
****************************************
報名連結：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733829
- 如出席一節鄉村導賞、八日工作坊可獲中大建築學院及香港建造學院之義工服務證書。
****************************************
計劃名稱：
「重塑榕樹凹故事：透過實驗式社區場地及自然文化徑共創鄉郊地方營造」
合辦機構：
中文大學建築學院
香港建造學院
榕樹凹村
資助：
環境及生態局環境科 鄉郊保育辦公室「鄉郊保育資助計劃」
****************************************
備註：
1. 榕樹凹屬禁區範圍，參加者需預先申請禁區許可證方可前往。
2. 在項目進行期間，所有與工作坊相關的船程費用將由計劃負責安排及資助。參加者需要自行安排陸路交通，並準備足夠食物（午餐）和飲用水。
3. 工作坊將以粵語進行。
4. 工作坊內容或會因天氣、路況、項目進度，以及參加者或工作人員身體狀況而作臨時調整，恕不另行通知，敬請留意。
5. 工作坊涉及一定體力勞動及長時間戶外活動。如參加者有身體不適、舊患或其他健康狀況，請預先通知主辦單位。
6. 村內沒有士多或補給設施，請預先準備足夠飲用水、午餐、乾糧、防曬及防蚊用品，並按個人需要攜帶雨具。
7. 工作坊地點蚊蟲較多，建議穿著淺色長袖衣物及長褲，並按需要攜帶蚊怕水。
8. 工作坊已包括基本第三者責任保險，參加者可按需要自行購買其他保險。
9. 鄉郊地區路面或有高低不平、濕滑、碎石情況，參加者須小心步行。
10. 如參加者未有遵守安全指引或工作人員安排，主辦單位有權終止其參與工作坊。
11. 活動期間我們可能會拍攝或／及錄影以作記錄、報告、宣傳及推廣用途。如你不欲被攝入鏡，請在活動開始前告知工作人員，以便我們作出適當安排。
12. 如有查詢，請電郵至
ysa-cuhk@cuhk.edu.hk
或致電 3943 6520 /3943 6518.

“Reimagining Yung Shue Au: Co-creating a Mountain-Sea Village”
— Recruitment for Rural-placemaking Ambassadors
Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story: Co-creating Rural Place
The School of Architecture at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently organising a rural school and summer workshop centred on the concept of
rural placemaking
. We invite individuals who are passionate about Hong Kong’s rural culture and interested in hands-on practice to join us in Yung Shue Au and participate in the revitalisation and co-creation of the village landscape.
During the programme, instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction will lead participants in learning traditional construction crafts and rural practical skills. Participants may choose to attend one or multiple workshop sessions according to their availability. Those who complete nine workshop days will receive a service certificate jointly issued by the School of Architecture, CUHK and the Hong Kong Institute of Construction in recognition of their participation and contribution.
Introduction to Yung Shue Au
Located in the northeastern New Territories, Yung Shue Au is a historic Hakka village established over 300 years ago by the Wan clan. At its peak, the village was home to more than 300 residents. Owing to its proximity to the border, a British military camp was stationed in the village during the 1980s, leaving behind a unique yet little-known historical legacy.
Although the village is currently uninhabited, villagers have actively promoted village revitalisation in recent years through repairing ancestral houses, documenting village history, organising village banquets and traditional rituals, as well as reviving the Qilin dance team. These efforts reflect a deep attachment to the village and a strong commitment to cultural inheritance and community reconnection.
Vision
Co-creating Rural Placemaking
Reimagining the mountain-sea landscape through low-carbon restoration and local memories.
Spatial Practice
Improving pathways and communal resting spaces through small-scale construction.
Sensory Narratives
Transforming local history into tangible landscape interpretation experiences.
Collective Action
Connecting design thinking with rural revitalisation through practical engagement.
Venue:
Yung Shue Au, Sha Tau Kok, New Territories
Programme Format and Phases
Village Guided Tour
Understanding the history of Yung Shue Au and learning about rural placemaking and cultural landscapes.
Material Collection
Collecting usable materials from the surrounding mountain, coastal, and village environment.
Landscape Practice
Participating in site clearing and spatial construction workshops led by instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction, focusing on rural landscape practices and traditional building techniques.
(* Stars indicate days when Hong Kong Institute of Construction instructors will lead the Landscape workshop.)
September
8 September (Tue), 15 September (Tue), 16 September (Wed)*, 17 September (Thur)*, 22 September (Tue)
Please note that actual workshop dates are subject to adjustment based on enrollment numbers, weather conditions, and staff availability. This includes the potential to increase or decrease the number of sessions. Registered participants will be notified directly of any changes, and updates will be posted across our promotional platforms.
- Participants may choose to join single-day or multiple-day workshops according to their availability.
​- Participants are encouraged to select all available dates to facilitate scheduling and grouping arrangements.
- Indicates dates on which the landscape practice workshops will be led by instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction.
- Dates for the guided tours will be announced later and will be arranged on both weekdays and weekends.
- Actual workshop dates may be adjusted according to registration numbers, weather conditions, and site situations. Relevant participants will be notified separately.
Workshop Time
09:00 am – 04:00 pm
Capacity
12 participants per session
Target Participants
Individuals in good physical condition who are able to participate in long hours of outdoor activities
Individuals interested in architecture, landscape design, conservation, and related fields
Registration Link
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733829
Participants who attend one village guided tour and eight workshop sessions will receive a volunteer service certificate jointly issued by the School of Architecture, CUHK and the Hong Kong Institute of Construction.
Project Title
“Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story: Co-creating Rural Place with Experimental Communal Hub and Eco-Cultural Trail”
Organisers
School of Architecture, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Hong Kong Institute of Construction
Yung Shue Au Village
Funding Support
Countryside Conservation Office
Environment Branch, Environment and Ecology Bureau
Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme
Remarks
1. Yung Shue Au is located within a restricted area. Participants are required to apply for a Closed Area Permit in advance.
2. During the project period, all boat transportation costs related to the workshops will be arranged and subsidised by the project. Participants are responsible for their own land transportation and should prepare sufficient food and drinking water.
3. The workshops will be conducted in Cantonese.
4. Workshop arrangements may be adjusted due to weather, road conditions, project progress, or the physical conditions of participants and staff without prior notice.
5. The workshops involve physical labour and extended outdoor activities. Participants with health conditions, previous injuries, or physical discomfort are advised to inform the organisers in advance.
6. There are no shops or supply facilities in the village. Participants should prepare sufficient drinking water, sun protection, mosquito repellent, and rain gear if necessary.
7. Mosquitoes and insects are common at the workshop site. Participants are advised to wear light-coloured long-sleeved clothing and long trousers, and bring insect repellent if needed.
8. Basic third-party liability insurance is included. Participants may arrange additional insurance at their own discretion.
9. Rural paths may be uneven, slippery, or covered with loose gravel. Participants should walk carefully.
10. The organisers reserve the right to terminate participation if safety instructions or staff arrangements are not followed.
11. Photographs and/or video recordings may be taken during the activities for documentation, reporting, publicity, and promotional purposes. Participants who do not wish to appear in photographs or recordings should inform staff before the activity begins.
12. For enquiries, please contact
ysa-cuhk@cuhk.edu.hk
or call 3943 6520 / 3943 6518.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

From: Wendy LI
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hkiimresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正進行一項為期8周，以內服中藥(沖劑)或西藥改善長新冠患者症狀的臨床研究，以下是研究安排：
研究對象：
年齡介乎6至80歲；
願意接受中醫或西醫治療4星期；
每星期一次覆診跟進病程；
目的         : 比較中藥與西藥對治療長新冠患者在改善生活質量、臨床症狀和生活社等治療效果和安全性。
研究內容：中/西醫評估*、問卷評估、抽血檢查、服用中藥或西藥等。
*注意: 本研究會隨機分「中藥組」或「西藥組」
研究地點： (a)中藥組: 沙田威爾斯親王醫院; (b)西藥組: 指定西醫診所 (中環)。
參與方式： 若有興趣，歡迎
1.透過以下方式報名：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13670048
2.亦歡迎您致電或WhatsApp我們6082-2583/ 2873-3245了解詳情。
Research Introduction:
The novel coronavirus has caused a global pandemic since the end of 2019. People are increasingly paying attention to the long-term effects of COVID-19 infection.People whose symptoms last for more than four weeks after COVID-19 infection are called [Long COVID]. The main symptoms include severe fatigue, shortness of breath, heart damage (such as myocarditis), cognitive impairment, sleep disorders, post-traumatic stress disorder syndrome, Muscle pain, decreased concentration, headache, impaired taste and smell, etc. affect the respiratory system, cardiovascular system, digestive system, urinary system, immune system, etc.
The Hong Kong Institute of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine at the Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting an 8-week clinical study on the improvement of symptoms of patients with COVID-19 by taking Chinese medicine (infusion) or Western medicine.
Target
: Age 6-80 who have recovered from COVID-19 infection.
Purpose
: To compare the therapeutic effects and safety of traditional Chinese medicine and Western medicine on improving the quality of life, clinical symptoms and social functions of long-term COVID-19 patients.
Research Content
: Visits, questionnaire assessment, blood draw before and after taking medicine,taking research Chinese medicine or Western medicine, etc.
Study Location
:(a) Chinese medicine group: Prince of Wales Hospital, Shatin;
(b) Western medicine group: designated western medicine clinic.

**This study is supervised by Prof. Karim Bettache (email: karimbettache@cuhk.edu.hk)**
Dear Potential Participants,
We are a research team from the School of Governance and Policy Science at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. This study is funded by the Research Grants Council (RGC) and led by a leading scholar in political psychology. The findings are expected to be published in top-tier international journals.
We sincerely invite South Asian permanent residents of Hong Kong (e.g., Indian, Pakistani, Nepalese, Bangladeshi, Sri Lankan, etc.) to participate in a focus group interview on the long-term psychological impact of colonialism on post-colonial societies.
Target participants:
South Asian ethnicity (e.g., Indian, Pakistani, Nepalese, Bangladeshi, Sri Lankan, etc.)
Holders of Hong Kong Permanent Resident status
Able to communicate in Mandarin, Cantonese, or English
Procedures and details of this study:
Research Consent
Focus Group Interview: A group discussion led by professional researchers, lasting approximately 1.5 hours
Flexible Location: In-person at CUHK campus or online participation available
A $100 HKD token of appreciation will be provided upon completion. All personal information and discussion content will be kept strictly confidential and used for academic research purposes only.
Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential.
If you are interested in participating, please contact us via:
WeChat: 13809899482
WhatsApp: 69409544
Email: 1155220689@link.cuhk.edu.hk
We will contact you afterwards to arrange further details.
For inquiries, please feel free to reach out through the above channels.

南亞裔人士（如印度、巴基斯坦、尼泊爾、孟加拉、斯里蘭卡等裔）
持有香港永久居民身份
能以普通話 / 廣東話 / 英文進行溝通

完成研究後，參加者可獲得$100港幣酬謝。訪談內容將全程嚴格保密，所有個人信息及對話內容僅用於學術研究用途。
本研究屬自願參與性質，期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如有意參與此項研究，歡迎透過以下方式聯絡我們：
微信：13809899482
WhatsApp：69409544
Email: 1155220689@link.cuhk.edu.hk
收到聯絡後，我們會再與合適參加者溝通後續安排。
如果對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過上述方式與我們聯絡。

From: Tim Lau
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學泌尿外科研究招募
:
香港中文大學泌尿外科現正進行一項男性特定群體的尿液及生物樣本HPV和病例對照研究。人類乳頭瘤病毒（HPV） 是全球最常見的性傳染病毒之一，能影響男性並導致多種疾病，包括生殖器疣（椰菜花）、陰莖癌、肛門癌 及 口咽癌。然而，男性 HPV 的感染情況一直缺乏研究，而你的參與將有助填補這個重要的知識空白。
本研究旨在了解HPV感染率、患者人口統計特徵、臨床特徵以及被診斷患有HPV相關惡性腫瘤的男性患者的疾病負擔。以評估男性尿液 HPV 測試的準確性，並更深入了解男性感染 HPV的風險因素，以及幫助未來預防及治療策略。
-如初步檢測確診為HPV陽性的患者，或將安排進一步行檢查 (例如:軟式膀胱鏡檢查等等)及跟進複檢。
參加者條件（男性，18歲或以上）：
1) 陰莖癌，肛⾨癌，或咽喉癌患者
2) 曾患性傳染病
3) 曾有同性性⾏為
4) 慢性前列腺炎患者
地點：沙⽥威爾斯親王醫院
樣本收集： 尿液及尿道拭子、口咽拭子、肛門拭子、冠狀溝拭子
-填寫簡單問卷
-根據情況也可能採集 20 毫升血液
[費用全免]
-完成整個研究計劃後可獲得港幣
$400
津貼
參加者的資料將會以專業方式絕對保密!!
所收集的資料僅用於學術研究用途
名額有限，先到先得!
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名：
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
-如果評估合適參與研究，將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如有查詢，歡迎電郵: timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk，與研究人員劉先生聯絡。
________________________________________________________________________
Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!]
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Division of Urology Research Recruitment
The Department of Surgery (Urology), The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants for a hybrid cohort and case-control study on male urinary HPV.
Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted viruses worldwide. It can affect men and lead to serious conditions including genital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. However, HPV infection in men remains under-studied. Your cooperation is highly solicited.
This research aims to determine HPV prevalence, patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease burden in men. It will also evaluate the accuracy of a new urine-based HPV DNA test and explore risk factors to support future prevention and treatment strategies.
Participants who test positive for HPV in the initial urine test may be invited for further investigations (e.g. flexible cystoscopy) and regular follow-up re-testing.
Eligibility (Males aged 18 or above)
Patients diagnosed with penile cancer, anal cancer, or oropharyngeal cancer
Men with a history of sexually transmitted diseases (STD)
Men who have sex with men (MSM)
Patients with chronic prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CPPS)
Study Location: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin
Narrative description
Urine sample + swabs (urethral, oropharyngeal, anal, coronal sulcus)
Complete a simple questionnaire
Optional: 20 ml blood sample (if required)
Free of Charge in HPV test !!
Upon successful completion of the study, participants will receive a
HKD 400
travel subsidy
Your Privacy is Fully Protected.
Data will only be used for academic research purposes.
If you are interested, please register via the link below:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
Suitable applicants will be contacted shortly.
For inquiries, please email:  timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk

The Department of Surgery (Urology), The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants for a hybrid cohort and case-control study on male urinary HPV.
Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted viruses worldwide. It can affect men and lead to serious conditions including genital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. However, HPV infection in men remains under-studied. Your cooperation is highly solicited.
This research aims to determine HPV prevalence, patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease burden in men. It will also evaluate the accuracy of a new urine-based HPV DNA test and explore risk factors to support future prevention and treatment strategies.
Participants who test positive for HPV in the initial urine test may be invited for further investigations (e.g. flexible cystoscopy) and regular follow-up re-testing.
Eligibility (Males aged 18 or above)
Patients diagnosed with penile cancer, anal cancer, or oropharyngeal cancer
Men with a history of sexually transmitted diseases (STD)
Men who have sex with men (MSM)
Patients with chronic prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CPPS)
Study Location: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin
Narrative description
Urine sample + swabs (urethral, oropharyngeal, anal, coronal sulcus)
Complete a simple questionnaire
Optional: 20 ml blood sample (if required)
Free of Charge in HPV test !!
Upon successful completion of the study, participants will receive a
HKD 400
travel subsidy
Your Privacy is Fully Protected.
Data will only be used for academic research purposes.
If you are interested, please register via the link below:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
Suitable applicants will be contacted shortly.
For inquiries, please email:  timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk

We are recruiting adults aged 18 or above for a 90-minute online study on visual perception and judgement. The study includes two computer-based visual tasks and a set of questionnaires containing 115 questions. Participants must have normal or corrected-to-normal vision and use a desktop or laptop computer with a physical keyboard. One of the questionnaires is available in English only. Detailed instructions, practice trials and rest breaks will be provided. Participants who complete the study will receive HKD 300 as a cash participation payment.
現正招募年滿18歲人士參與一項約90分鐘的網上視覺知覺及判斷研究。研究包括兩項電腦視覺任務及一套合共115題的問卷。參加者須視力正常或經矯正後正常，並使用配備實體鍵盤的桌上電腦或手提電腦。其中一份問卷只提供英文版本。研究會提供詳細說明、練習及休息時間。完成整項研究的參加者將獲得港幣300元現金參與報酬。
Please use Google Chrome to open the study link below. Safari is not supported.
請使用 Google Chrome 開啟以下研究連結；Safari 瀏覽器不支援本研究。

歡迎申請
2026 傑出學生獎，與大家分享你的成就和故事！
除了追求學術成就外，香港中文大學(中大)學生亦積極在非學術範疇發揮所長。為表揚在不同領域有傑出表現，並持續為大學社群及社會作出積極貢獻的學生，中大設立「傑出學生獎」，以肯定其成就與貢獻，並鼓勵同學追求卓越、勇於突破自我。

藝術
創新與發明
社會服務
體育
特別表現

在2025–26學年就讀於香港中文大學的全日制本科生或研究生，如於有關學年在上述其中一個範疇取得卓越成就或作出重大貢獻，均符合申請資格。
【截止日期】
2026年9月18日（星期五）中午12時正。

Research Paper CompetitionLingnan Culture Studies Research Paper Competition 2026-27 論文獎「嶺南文化研究論文獎」2026-27 - Institute of Chinese Studies
From: Joanne HUI
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ics-lingnan@cuhk.edu.hk

[The English version follows the Chinese one.]
嶺南文化研究計劃「嶺南文化研究論文獎」
2026-27
「嶺南文化研究論文獎」旨在推動國際嶺南文化學術研究，以鼓勵海內外在讀博士生及青年研究員在嶺南文化領域進行深入研究。
參獎資格：
本論文獎接受在讀博士生及青年研究員提交嶺南文化研究領域的優秀論文。論文內容可與古今文學、歷史、哲學、宗教、藝術、語言學、人類學等範疇相關。論文必須從未發表或出版，字數在三萬以內，中、英文皆可。
注意事項：
提交日期：2026年8月1日至2026年12月31日
參獎者須填妥申請表，並連同論文以電郵附件方式一併發送至：
ics-lingnan@cuhk.edu.hk
，郵件標題為「嶺南文化研究論文獎2026-27（申請人全名）」。
報名表格
：
按此
查　　詢：
地　　址: 香港沙田香港中文大學中國文化研究所105室
電　　話: (852) 3943 7393
傳　　真: (852) 2603 5149
電　　郵:
ics-lingnan@cuhk.edu.hk
Lingnan Culture Studies Research Paper Competition 2026-27
Organized by the Research Programme for Lingnan Culture, Institute of Chinese Studies, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
The Competition aims to promote international academic research on Lingnan culture, as well as to encourage local and overseas doctoral students and young research fellows who are aspiring to conduct in-depth research in the field.
Eligibility:
1. Eligibility is limited to doctoral students and young research fellows.
2. Submissions must be papers of original research on Lingnan culture, in the areas of literature, history, philosophy, religion, arts, linguistics, anthropology, or other humanities disciplines.
3. Submission papers should be either in Chinese or English of no more than 30,000 words. The papers should never have been published.
Submissions:
Submission period: 1 August 2026 – 31 December 2026
Applicants should submit the application form along with the research paper by email to:
ics-lingnan@cuhk.edu.hk
, with “Lingnan Culture Studies Research Paper Competition 2026-27 (Full name of applicant)” in the subject line.

title: Call for Rural Conservation! Free Training・Paid Internship! Join Us as a Project Ambassador at Yim Tin Tsai 第二屆【智遊自在鹽田梓】項目大使現正接受報名！生態文化導賞實習機會！
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/09/04
»
Announcements
Call for Rural Conservation! Free Training・Paid Internship! Join Us as a Project Ambassador at Yim Tin Tsai  第二屆【智遊自在鹽田梓】項目大使現正接受報名！生態文化導賞實習機會！ - Department of Geography and Resource Management
From: Cherry Lau
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cherrylau123@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【智遊自在鹽田梓】現正招募 第二屆項目大使！
Call for Project Ambassador to work in Yim Tin Tsai, Sai Kung!
熱愛大自然？或是對客家文化與天主教深感興趣？機會來了！
「智遊自在鹽田梓」現正招募第二屆項目大使，計劃費用全免，完成後可獲頒證書，一同參與生態保育與社區導賞工作。
成為項目大使，你可以在遠離煩囂的西貢鹽田梓島上工作，將生態知識、AR科技和社區導賞結合，親身參與鄉郊保育，更可優先報名參加項目活動！
工作體驗包括帶領生態文化導賞，以及協助活動進行
Love nature? Curious about Hakka culture and Catholicism? This is your opportunity!
"Exploring YTT Nature ARchive" is now recruiting for its second cohort (2026/2027) of Project Ambassadors. The programme is free to join, and you will receive free training and a certificate upon completion. Be part of our ecological conservation and community guiding efforts.
As a Project Ambassador, you will work on the Yim Tin Tsai island in Sai Kung, combining ecological knowledge, AR technology, and guided tours. You will also get priority access to project activities. Your role will include leading eco-cultural tours and supporting event operations.
參與資格 Eligibility
：
• 必須為香港中文大學在讀學生（本科生及碩士生均可）Current CUHK student (both undergraduate and postgraduate students are welcome)
• 對生態、客家文化、導賞或保育有興趣 Interest in ecology, Hakka culture, guided tours, or conservation
• 粵語流利，具英語能力更佳 Fluent in Cantonese (English proficiency is an advantage)
• 不怕坐船，熱愛戶外活動 Comfortable with outdoor activities
計劃日程 Programme Schedule
：
• 面試 Interview：Late September to early October 2026 (via Zoom)
• 網上理論課 Online Training：October - November 2026
• 實地考察 Field Visit：Early November 2026 (Yim Tin Tsai Island)
• 實地導賞考核 Tour Examination：November–December 2026 (Optional 如選擇參與導賞工作)
截止報名 Application Deadline: 20 September 2026 (Sunday) 23:59
報名表格 Join Us Now
：
https://forms.gle/wocifws9ndFh9tqV7
Enquiries: Cherry Lau (Project Manager)
cherrylau123@cuhk.edu.hk
══════════
關於我們 About the Project
本項目【智遊自在鹽田梓 Exploring YTT Nature ARchive】（全稱：「西貢鹽田梓生態保育應用研究：擴增模型與智能體驗式參與」）於2024年9月正式開始，為期三年，旨在運用擴增實境技術展示鹽田梓的生物多樣性，將智能科技融入島上自然保育與鄉郊復育工作。
"Exploring YTT Nature ARchive" is a three‑year project (2024–2027) that integrates Augmented Reality (AR) technology with nature conservation and rural revitalisation on Yim Tin Tsai Island. It aims to enhance public awareness and interest in the island's biodiversity through innovative technology and experiential learning.
資助單位 Funders: 鄉郊保育資助計劃、鄉郊保育辦公室 Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme (CCFS), Countryside Conservation Office (CCO)
主辦單位 Organiser: 香港中文大學地理與資源管理學系 Department of Geography and Resource Management
協辦/支持單位 Partners：香港科技大學綜合系統與設計學部、香港戶外生態教育協會、鹽田梓村委會、鹽光保育中心 HKUST Division of Integrative Systems and Design, Outdoor Wildlife Learning Hong Kong (OWLHK), Yim Tin Tsai Village Committee, Salt and Light Preservation Centre
Website:
http://www.yttnaturearchive.org
Facebook: 智遊自在鹽田梓 Exploring YTT Nature ARchive
Instagram: @yttnaturearchive
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

身處香港這座繁囂的都市，你正被焦慮、壓力、失眠或情緒內耗所困嗎？
緊湊的學業與工作節奏、對未來的不確定，是否讓你常感受慮與不安？
誠邀你參加自學中心首次開辦的呼吸禪修班，一起學習佛陀所教導——簡單、有效的呼吸方法。
這套練習將有助你緩解壓力、放鬆身心、培養覺察力，重新找回輕安與自在。


講者：
Karen, Chuen, Faye
畢業於香港大學佛法輔導碩士課程，現正於港大進修專業佛法輔導文憑課程。致力將佛法、心理輔導與現代科學融合，幫助我們守護健康快樂的心。

日期：
10月15日(四) 及 22日(四)
11月12日(四) 及 19日(四)
⏰
時間：
晚上7:30至9:00

地點：
香港中文大學聯合書院胡忠圖書館1樓研討室

對象：
中大學生及教職員

語言：
廣東話
成功完成 3 堂或以上課堂者，可獲贈冥想凳乙張
名額有限，先到先得。現已開放報名：
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/workshop/MTE2026/
In the hustle and bustle of Hong Kong, is anxiety, stress, sleeplessness, or emotional fatigue weighing you down?
Amidst demanding schedules and future uncertainties, do you feel anxious and uneasy sometimes?
We warmly invite you to join the Independent Learning Centre’s inaugural Breathing Meditation Class, where we explore simple but profound breathing methods rooted in Buddhist teachings together.
This practice is designed to ease your stress, unwind your body and mind, nurture self-awareness, and help you find your inner peace and tranquillity.


Facilitators:
Karen, Chuen, Faye
Graduated with Master of Buddhist Counselling from The University of Hong Kong, and currently pursuing Postgraduate Diploma in Professional Practice of Buddhist Counselling at HKU, they are dedicated to integrating Buddhist wisdom, psychological counselling, and modern science to help us nurture a healthy and joyful mind.

Date:
15, 22 Oct & 12, 19 Nov (Thursdays)
⏰
Time:
7:30 pm – 9:00 pm

Venue:
Seminar Room, 1/F, Wu Chung Library, United College

Target Audience:
CUHK Students and Staff

Language:
Cantonese

Complete 3 or more sessions to receive a FREE meditation stool
Seats are limited. Register Now at:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/workshop/MTE2026/

:

The new 2026 TOEFL format

Announcements
AI+Music!! Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research AI+Music!! 招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Xiuyang Meng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究
我們正在尋找熱愛音樂的你，參與人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究，用你的聽感為 AI 模型注入真實的青年情緒視角。
研究目的
本研究旨在運用人工智能技術，從青年視角對粵語流行歌曲進行情緒分類標註，評估青年群體對音樂情緒的主觀感知特徵，並為個性化音樂推薦系統及情緒調節相關研究提供數據支持。
招募條件
18 至 24 歲，熱愛音樂且經常聆聽流行音樂，能流暢使用粵語及英語進行溝通與表達的青年。
參與內容
聆聽 50 首粵語流行歌曲，並完整聽畢每首參與標註的曲目，依據自身主觀體驗與即時情緒感受，將歌曲進行情緒分類。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理陳小姐 或 蒙先生聯絡。
Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research
We are looking for music lovers like you to participate in our research on AI and popular song emotion categorization, contributing your listening experience to inject authentic youth emotional perspectives into our AI model.
Purpose of the Study
This study aims to use artificial intelligence technology to annotate the emotion categories of Cantopop songs from a youth perspective, evaluate the subjective emotional perception characteristics of young people towards music, and provide data support for personalized music recommendation systems and emotion regulation-related research.
Eligibility Criteria
Young people aged 18 to 24 who love music, listen to popular music regularly, and are able to communicate fluently in Cantonese and English.
Participation Content
Listen to 50 Cantopop songs in full, and categorize each song according to your subjective experience and immediate emotional feelings.
How to Join?
Please click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact eligible participants to explain the study details in full:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
Contact Us
If you have any questions, please call 6115-0322 during office hours to speak with our research assistants Ms. Chan or Mr. Meng.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

CUriosity
is CUHK’s campus magazine – made by students, for students. For 10 years, we published our thoughts and stories to students in CUHK through magazine publications, which are kindly supported by the General Education Foundation Programme of the Office of University General Education. Our latest issue, Issue 9, will come out soon! (For all of our issues, please go to our instagram @curiositycuhk).

for

Administrative coordinator
Core members
Writers

Designers

Dear Students,
3rd edition of the HK Express Gotta GO! Sustainable Explorer Challenge is back and now open for applications!
Love travel? Want to turn your ideas into a real adventure?
The
3rd HK Express Gotta GO! Sustainable Explorer Challenge
is now open for applications. Team up in pairs, design a
4D3N
lower-carbon travel itinerary
, and compete for the chance to bring your trip to life flying with HK Express!
Prizes & Opportunities
If your team is selected as one of the
5 finalist teams

Round-Trip flight tickets by HK Express
HK$4,000 travel fund per person
The chance to carry out your proposed trip in January 2027
And if your team wins the
Champion

Why join?
You’ll get the chance to:
Learn more about sustainable travel and carbon footprint awareness
Build skills in itinerary design, storytelling and pitching
