Gain hands-on experience through a real travel challenge
Meet students from universities across Hong Kong, Macau and other parts of the Greater Bay Area

3rd edition of the HK Express Gotta GO! Sustainable Explorer Challenge is back and now open for applications!
Love travel? Want to turn your ideas into a real adventure?
The
3rd HK Express Gotta GO! Sustainable Explorer Challenge
is now open for applications. Team up in pairs, design a

Announcements
[ RECRUITING! ] Student Helpers in Sleep and Circadian Medicine   - Department of Psychiatry
From: Circadian Lab
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
circadianlab@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
We are recruiting student helpers to support our ongoing clinical research projects on circadian rhythms and mental health at our lab in Shatin Hospital. You will be working collaboratively as a member of the research team. This is a great opportunity to gain hands-on exposure to clinical research workflows in a hospital setting.
Responsibilities:
Student helpers will play an important role in supporting the research team, with responsibilities mainly involving:
Data entry and data cleaning
Administer neurocognitive tests, questionnaires, and pupillometry assessments
Prepare study materials
Assist with the handling and processing of biological samples
Other ad hoc administrative tasks assigned
Requirements:
Open to students from all disciplines and year levels; a background in psychology, healthcare, or related fields is advantageous.
Fluency in Cantonese is required; proficiency in English is preferred.
Good interpersonal skills and strong attention to detail.
Motivated to gain research experience with a demonstrated strong work ethic.
Experience in data management and familiarity with SPSS or R are preferred.
Working Hours:
We are flexible with your work schedule. Generally, students are expected to commit to 2–4 regular sessions per week, with each session lasting at least 3 hours.
How to apply:
If you are interested in joining us as a student helper, please send your application to us at
circadianlab@cuhk.edu.hk
and include your CV, transcript, and a brief reason for applying. Shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further consideration.

bodyText:

Free Prostate Health Screening‼‼‼ 免費前列腺健康篩查－誠邀合資格男士參加 - S.H. Ho Urology Centre, Department of Surgery
From: Yellow Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yellowwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
根據衛生署數據，前列腺癌是本港男性常見的癌症之一。透過及早篩查，可以有效降低相關的健康風險。本次活動由中大何善衡泌尿中心舉辦，為合資格人士提供免費的前列腺特異抗原 (PSA) 檢測服務。
活動地點： 沙田區（詳細地址將於成功報名後通知）
活動內容：(所需時間約一小時)
1. 影片講解：深入淺出地介紹前列腺增生及前列腺癌的檢查與治療知識。
2. 前列腺篩查：合資格人士可獲免費前列腺特異抗原（PSA）測試乙次.
• 測試方式：我們將以指尖採血方式為參加者抽取血液樣本，並透過PSA檢測機進行現場測試，約十分鐘即可得知結果。
參加資格：
• 性別：男性
• 年齡：50-75歲
• 從未接受前列腺相關檢查
如有興趣參加活動，請填妥以下表格。
https://forms.office.com/r/HRJspBWSW6
如想了解更多關於前列腺癌風險的評估, 可瀏覽以下網址;
https://urologycentre.com.hk/zh-hant/diseases/detail/how-to-investigate-and-make-diagnosis-for-prostate-cance
r
參加者提供的所有資料將會被保密。如有任何查詢，請與我們聯絡 （Whatsapp: 5160 6904；電郵：yellowwong@cuhk.edu.hk）。
According to data from the Department of Health, prostate cancer is one of the most common cancers among men in Hong Kong. Early screening can effectively reduce related health risks. This event is organized by the S.H. Ho Urology Centre of CUHK, providing free Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) testing services for eligible individuals.
Event Venue: Shatin District (the exact address will be provided after successful registration)
Event Details: (Estimated duration: about one hour)
Video Presentation: An easy-to-understand introduction to the examination and treatment of prostate cancer and benign prostatic hyperplasia
Prostate Screening: Eligible participants will receive one free Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) test.
Testing Method: We will collect blood samples from participants via a fingertip blood test and conduct an on-site PSA test using a PSA testing device. Results will be available in about ten minutes.
Eligibility:
Gender: Male
Age: 50-75 years old
Have never undergone any prostate-related examination
If you are interested in participating, please fill in the online form below;
https://forms.office.com/r/HRJspBWSW6
For more information about the assessment of prostate cancer risk, please visit the following website:
https://urologycentre.com.hk/zh-hant/diseases/detail/how-to-investigate-and-make-diagnosis-for-prostate-cancer
All information provided by participants will be kept confidential. For any enquiries, please contact us (WhatsApp: 5160 6904; Email: yellowwong@cuhk.edu.hk)

title: HK$300Brain Health Study HK$300中大醫學院邀您參與腦部健康研究
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/09/04
»
Announcements
HK$300Brain Health Study  HK$300中大醫學院邀您參與腦部健康研究 - CUHK Psychiatry Sleep Assessment Unit
From: Wong Yuen Tung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yuentungwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
便秘？嗅覺變差？睡覺拳打腳踢？有腦退化家族史？
這些看似平常的小毛病，其實可能是柏金遜症等大腦退化的早期先兆！
提早了解大腦健康，預防神經退化！
中大醫學院睡眠研究小組推出全新手機篩查App，誠邀您參與醫學研究！
研究對象：
年齡介乎
50 至 65 歲
的華人
未確診
任何腦神經退化疾病（如柏金遜症、阿爾茲海默症/失智症等）
參加者需完成以下程序：
參與研究
費用全免
，成功完成相關研究程序者最多可獲
HK$300元超市禮券
作為津貼
階段一：
下載手機程式並完成問卷 （約需 15–20 分鐘）
完成後可獲得早期柏金遜病風險分數
符合資格並完成問卷者可獲 HK$100元超市禮券
階段二：
部分參加者將獲邀進一步參與臨床評估
包括身體檢查、臨床訪談、居家睡眠測試及神經認知測試
符合資格並完成階段二者，可額外獲 HK$200元超市禮券
立刻掃描海報右下方
二維碼 (QR Code)
或
點擊連結
下載程式「柏健通」參與研究
IOS用戶：
https://apps.apple.com/hk/app/%E6%9F%8F%E5%81%A5%E9%80%9A/id1626241589
Android用戶：
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2
查詢（致電或WhatsApp）：3919 7792 / 5282 5786（研究助理 黃小姐）
Constipated？Weakened sense of smell？Acting out dream during sleep (punching and kicking) ？Having a family history of neurodegenerative disease？
Common issues like these can actually be early warning signs of brain degeneration, including neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease.
Understand your brain health early to prevent neurodegeneration.
Sleep Assessment Unit - Psychiatry, CUHK has launched a brand-new screening App, and we sincerely invite you to join our medical research study.
Target participants：
Chinese aged between 50 to 65 years old
Have NOT been diagnosed
with any neurodegenerative disease (e.g. Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease/ Dementia, etc.)
What you will need to do:
Participation is completely free. Those who successfully complete the study procedure can receive up to HK$300 in supermarket voucher as an allowance.
Phase 1:
Download the mobile app "柏健通" and complete the questionnaires (take approximately 15-20 minutes)
An early Parkinson’s disease risk score will be provided upon completion
Eligible participants who complete the questionnaires will receive HK$100 supermarket voucher
Phase 2:
Selected participants will be invited to undergo further clinical assessments
Assessments include physical examination, clinical interviews, sleep studies, and neurocognitive assessments
Eligible participants who complete Phase 2 will receive an additional HK$200 supermarket voucher
Interested parties are welcome to participate by
clicking the links below
or
scanning the QR Code
in the poster to download the "柏健通" mobile application:
IOS users:
https://apps.apple.com/hk/app/%E6%9F%8F%E5%81%A5%E9%80%9A/id1626241589
Android users:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2
For details and registration enquiries, please contact our hotline: 39197792 or 5282 5786 (WhatsApp) (Research Assistant, Ms Wong)
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

Are you a Self-Critical person? Male Cantonese Speakers Participant Recruitment[Free of Charge] Magic Chair Experiment 想跳出自責的循環？「魔法椅子」自我關懷對話實驗 男性參與者招募【費用全免】 識廣東話【完成後可獲一份心理問卷報告】 - Department of Psychology
From: Chu Long Yiu
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155211898@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
「魔法椅子」自我關懷對話實驗 參與者招募 
心裡一直有把聲音告訴你不夠好？因此感到困擾，並想要減少批評自己？
香港中文大學心理學系 臨床心理科學實驗室 誠邀你參與有趣嘅心理學研究！
我們希望研究人們在受挫時，內心會如何與自己對話，而這些聲音會如何影響心理健康。
完成研究流程可獲一份心理問卷報告
招募對象：
年滿 18 歲
識廣東話
男性
生活受自我批評困擾者
研究內容：
線上前測問卷
約 1.5 小時實驗室實驗
2 星期後線上後測問卷
地點：香港中文大學 王福元樓102室
有興趣參加？請透過以下連結報名：
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_eJcE6LGxl0xhfW6
此研究已通過香港中文大學調查和行為研究倫理的審核。
如有任何疑問，歡迎聯絡我們！
電郵： ybxie@link.cuhk.edu.hk（研究負責人 Yanbin）
—————————————————————————————————————————
Magic Chair Experiment – Recruitment of participants 
Is there an inner voice keep telling you that you are good enough? You feel distressed about this and wish to stop criticizing yourself?
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory, Department of Psychology at CUHK, is inviting you to join this interesting study.
We would like to know more about how people’s inner voice and interaction within oneself when facing struggles, and how these inner voice affects individual’s mental health.
You will receive a personalized questionnaire report after finishing the study.

Eligible participants:
Aged 18 or above
Able to speak and understand Cantonese
Male
Distressed about self-criticism

Study Overview:
Online questionnaire before the experiment
In-person experiment at the laboratory (lasts for approximately 1.5 hour)
Follow-up online questionnaire at 2 weeks after the experiment
 Location: Room 102, Wong Foo Yuan Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin, N.T., Hong Kong SAR
 If you are interested in this study, please click the link below for application.
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_eJcE6LGxl0xhfW6
This study is approved by the Survey and Behavioral Research Ethics (SBRE) of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
 For enquiries, please feel free to contact Yanbin Xie at
ybxie@link.cuhk.edu.hk
.

For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Consultation Sessions for PhD and MPhil in Communication Programmes
The 2027-2028 Research Postgraduate Programmes (PhD and MPhil) of the School of Journalism and Communication, the Chinese University of Hong Kong, are now open for application. The School will hold several consultation sessions 21-23 & 26 October 2026 via Zoom.
Each session will be hosted by one of our research faculty members and conducted in a focus group format. Participants will have the opportunity to discuss their research plans, explore the programme structure and financial support in detail, and ask any questions they may have about admissions, studying at CUHK, etc. Those who are planning to apply for PhD and MPhil programmes (2027 Intake) are strongly encouraged to attend one of the sessions before submitting their application.

Master of Arts in Journalism,

From: Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages

modernlang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

Learn a new language in Term 1: French, German, Korean &Spanish
Modern Language Minor Programmes at CUHK
In Term 1, 2026-27, don’t miss out on this great chance to:
* learn a language and its culture or advance existing language skills
* have fun with our interactive approach, and
* earn 3 credits per course on top of that!
The Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages at CUHK cordially invites you to join our Modern Languages courses from our Minor Programmes in the Term 1 of 2026-27.
Course Selection & On-line Registration
(via CUSIS) for the coming semester (Term 1, 2026-27) (Please check CUSIS for your designated registration period.)
E-add/drop period on CUSIS
14 – 20 September 2026
(Mon, 8:30 pm – Sun 8:30 pm)
For more information, please subscribe to our Instagram accounts:
French:
cuhk_french_programme
German:
cuhk_german
Korean:
cuhk_korean
Spanish:
elecafelito
Hong Kong Sign Language:
HKSL.CUHK
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages:
CUHK.LING.ML
There are many practical benefits and advantages in language learning, in particular, an increased competitiveness. Our graduate survey shows that a large proportion of our graduates found their language training in the ML programme useful for their current job. Some explicitly stated that they are currently working or have been working with a company from the country of their target language or even in the country of the target language.
From beginner to more advanced levels, come and enjoy learning:
French, German, Korean, and Spanish
Eligibility:
All CUHK full-time undergraduate and MPhil/PhD students
Instructor & Venue:
Please refer to the website of Registration and Examinations Section (
http://www.res.cuhk.edu.hk
) for the details of the teaching timetable of the year of 2026-27.
You can also contact our language coordinators for more information:
French: Mr. Benjamin Gaudet
benjamin.gaudet@cuhk.edu.hk
German: Mr. Bernd Esch
berndesch@cuhk.edu.hk
Korean: Ms. Sehee Park
sehee.park@cuhk.edu.hk
Spanish: Mr. Antonio Garcia Susperregui
antoniorgarciasusperregui@cuhk.edu.hk
For more details on our course details on our Department’s
website
.
Remarks:
The units earned will be counted towards fulfillment of requirements for your minor programme and graduation.
For questions, please contact our Department General Office at 3943 9836 or via email to modernlang@link.cuhk.edu.hk.
See you in our courses!

bodyText:

Announcements
參與「大」「部」行計劃成為「綠行者」 Join ‘Walk for Green’ programme to be a ‘Green Walker’  - Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Office
From: Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Office
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
srsdo@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
「大」「部」行獎勵計劃
已經展開，中大學生和教職員凡於2026年9月1日至2027年6月30日期間於
校園步道
起點和終點使用讀卡器記錄步行次數以累積120分或以上，即成為「綠行者」並於學年完結後獲頒發獎品。
齊來參與「大」「部」行，徒步穿梭校園，減少依賴交通工具，既可欣賞中大景色，亦能實踐低碳生活模式。
計劃詳情：
https://www.srsdo.cuhk.edu.hk/zh-hk/walk-for-green
The ‘
Walk for Green
’ programme has begun. CUHK students and staff who, between 1 September 2026 and 30 June 2027, record their walking trips at the start and end points of campus
walking trails
using card readers, and accumulate 120 points or more, will be recognized as ‘Green Walkers’ and receive a prize at the end of the academic year.
Join the ‘Walk for Green’ programme: stroll across campus, reduce reliance on transportation, enjoy the scenery of CUHK, and practice a low‑carbon lifestyle.
Programme details:
https://www.srsdo.cuhk.edu.hk/en-gb/walk-for-green

About Us
Happy Ageing Lab
(https://www.happyageinglab.com/) is a social innovation initiative based at The Chinese University of Hong Kong. We advocate revamping the design and management of our built environment for healthy ageing through participatory research, co-design workshops, and interdisciplinary collaborations to shape a supportive and inclusive community for older adults.
Who We Are Looking For:
We are currently recruiting passionate
undergraduate and postgraduate students from CUHK
to join our team as Student Helpers for upcoming projects.
Job
Responsibilities:
Selected helpers will assist with various
on-site / remote
tasks on an ad-hoc basis, including:
- Assisting in workshops and community activities
- Conducting interviews and community surveys
- Audio transcription and document translation
- Supporting desk research and literature reviews
- Multimedia production using Adobe Creative Suite and/or Canva (e.g., social media content, graphics, videos)
- On-site event helpers / workshop note-takers
Remuneration & Working Arrangement:
Hourly Rate: HK$64/hour
(Standard CUHK Student Helper rate)
Arrangement:
Upon successful recruitment, you will be added to our WhatsApp group, where helper opportunities and assignment details will be posted from time to time. You can opt for tasks that fit your availability.
Application & Deadline:
If you are interested in working with us, please complete the application by
13 September 2026
.
Google Form:

We will get in touch with you soon if you are selected. Thank you!

From: Yuxuan ZHENG
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
zhyx@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The Cognitive Psychology Lab is recruiting university students to participate in an experimental study about multilingual language production. This experiment is endorsed by Prof. HUANG Liqiang (
lqhuang@psy.cuhk.edu.hk
) from the Department of Psychology, CUHK.
Location: Sino Building, Chung Chi College
Tasks:
You will take part in the experiments in a lab on separate days. You will be presented with pictures of common objects, and you need to name these pictures one by one in a designated language (i.e., Cantonese, Mandarin, or English).
You will also complete a language background questionnaire, do some rating on the pictures (e.g., familiarity), and complete some cognitive tasks (e.g., working memory tasks).
Duration and Payment:
Day 1: 60-70 mins (HKD70)
Day 2: 50-60 mins (HKD65)
Day 3: 50-60 mins (HKD65)
Requirements:
18-30 years old, university students
Cantonese as your first language, Mandarin and English as your native or non-native languages
Grew up in Hong Kong
No history of uncorrected sensory impairments or neurological disorders
If you are interested, please sign up through this link:
https://forms.gle/AMGhYw31vKx9v4iMA
. You will be contacted by email for further instructions.
This study is in collaboration with Dr. WANG Jie of The Department of Psychology, Education University of Hong Kong. Please contact Miss WANG Ziyi Pearl <cogpsy339@gmail.com> for any enquiries.
Thank you for your interest!
On Behalf of WANG Ziyi, Pearl

Clinical Gerontology and End-of-life Care Programme
provides comprehensive knowledge and training for professionals involved in the
care of older people
and in
end-of-life care

healthcare professionals
and students from
social work
backgrounds.

****
中小學學生活動管理專業證書課程
2026–2027****
香港中文大學教育學院、香港教育研究所與香港課外活動主任協會於2026–2027學年舉辦兼讀制 「中小學學生活動管理專業證書課程」，以回應中、小學學生活動的發展情勢，並配合學員的專業需要。
課程對象
負責或協助籌辦及帶領學生活動的現職中、小學教師，尤以現任及新任課外活動主任、全方位學習統籌主任、新高中「其他學習經歷」統籌主任、「學生學習概覽」統籌主任及課程發展主任為合。需持有教師資歷及認可大學之學士學位。
課程內容
課程包括四個必修單元和一個選修單元，共126小時。
必修單元
選修單元
DSA0001學生活動的基礎知識與理論
DSA0002學生活動的管理
DSA0003學生活動的實踐
DSA0004學生活動專題探究
DSA0101小學學生活動的組織與運作
DSA0102中學學生活動的組織與運作
修讀日期
2026年11月至2027年6月（除實習單元外，上課時間暫定為星期二及四晚上）
截止報名日期
2026年9月21日（星期一）
請於網上填寫及提交申請表格：

電話：3943 6999
傳真：2603 6850
電郵：
hkier-training@cuhk.edu.hk
****Professional Certificate Programme in Management of Student Activities in Primary and Secondary Schools 2026-2027****
The Faculty of Education and the Hong Kong Institute of Educational Research (HKIER) of the Chinese University of Hong Kong, and the Hong Kong Extra-curricular Activities Masters’ Association collaborate in offering the one-year Professional Certificate Programme in Management of Student Activities in Primary and Secondary Schools in the 2026–2027 academic year. This programme is designed to respond to the development of student activities and to accommodate the needs of professional training of educators.
Target Participants
Serving teachers in primary or secondary schools who are responsible for or involved in organizing and managing student activities, and holders of teacher qualification and a Bachelor's degree from a recognized university.
Curriculum
The curriculum consists of four compulsory modules and one elective module, a total of 126 hours.
Study Period
November 2026 to June 2027 (mainly on Tuesday and Thursday)
Application Deadline
21 September 2026
Please submit your application online:

  [Online experiment] Looking for native English speakers
Prof. Haerim Hwang (Department of English, CUHK) is looking for participants for a study on language production.
Which participants are we looking for?
- English is your first/native and dominant language
- Your graduate degree is not in the field of linguistics
- Can use your laptop/computer and have access to stable internet (no smartphones, laptops, or hotspot)
- Can participate in an experiment on Zoom in a quiet environment
- Have Chrome on your laptop/computer
How do I participate?
1. Fill out this questionnaire
-- English speakers: https://forms.gle/ttuhGGCwRx2n95kBA
2. Our research team will reach out to you, confirming your availability.
3. It will take approximately 2 hours to complete these tasks.
What do I get out of the study?
You will get HK$250 in cash upon the completion of the task.
Your participation will enhance our understanding of how people process English sentences.
Questions?
Contact Prof. Haerim Hwang at haerimhwang@cuhk.edu.hk
Ethics Approval
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics Committee SBREC (fssc02@cuhk.edu.hk) has vetted the study (Approval ID: SBRE-22-0026D). If you have any concerns regarding ethics, please contact them.

From: Winifred Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
winifredtywong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，旨在評估手機應用程式網上自助心理健康療程對改善青年睡眠及情緒健康的成效。現招募年齡介乎15歲至24歲青年研究。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
1. 15歲至24歲青年
2. 有失眠及情緒症狀
3. 過去三個月沒有接受失眠及情緒心理治療或藥物治療
您需要做什麼？
參與為期6週的手機App自助療程
每週觀看20分鐘左右的網上療程
完成四次網上問卷及七天睡眠日記，包括治療前、治療後、三個月跟進及六個月跟進
全部評估及治療皆在電話或網上進行，無需面見！
如有興趣，請即登記並填寫簡單的網上篩查問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_domAhEzzCmdV2sK
研究小組將會聯絡適合參與本研究的人士並進一步解釋研究詳情。閣下登記時留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
winifredtywong@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp: (+852- 47544464 黃小姐)查詢。
The Department of Psychiatry at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a research study to evaluate the effectiveness of an online self-help mobile app program for improving sleep and emotional well-being among youths. We would like to invite participants aged between 15 and 24 to join the study. Details are as follows:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Youths aged between 15-24 years
2. Experience symptoms of insomnia and emotional distress
3. Have not received psychological or medication treatment for these issues in the past 3 months
What will you do?
Join a 6-week self-help treatment via mobile app
Attend 20 minutes of online therapy weekly
Complete four online surveys and seven-day sleep diary: before treatment, after treatment, at 3-month follow-up, and at 6-month follow-up during the study
All assessments and treatments are conducted via phone or online — no in-person visits required!
If you are interested, please register and complete a short screening questionnaire here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_domAhEzzCmdV2sK
The research team will contact eligible participants and further explain the details of the study. Information collected will be only used for research purpose and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
winifredtywong@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852- 47544464 Miss Wong).

For enquiries, please write to:

bodyText:

Announcements
【$100 Coupon 】CUHK Allergy Team is Recruiting Healthy Children for Immune Testing  中大過敏科團隊誠邀非食物過敏兒童參與兒童免疫多組學圖譜研究 - Department of Paediatrics
From: Ann Au
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
annwsau@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
疾病與腸道微生態息息相關，中大兒科過敏科團隊正在研究兒童食物過敏的成因及治療方案。您的孩子的血液及糞便樣本有助我們科研團隊更了解兒童食物過敏與腸道微生態等多組學的關係，更對濕疹、哮喘、鼻敏感等其他免疫系統疾病提供寶貴的參考，對未來的科研發展作出巨大的貢獻。
以下表格將會收集基本資料，以便研究團隊評核您／您的孩子是否合適參與此研究。如果您／您的孩子被選中，研究團隊將會聯絡您，並安排到威爾斯親王醫院 (Prince of Wales Hospital) 再詳細解釋研究流程及簽署同意書。 研究團隊會為參加者抽取血液及糞便樣本。參加者在完成該研究後可獲港幣$100餐飲券、血液報告乙份及腸道微生態報告乙份。
研究團隊會在閣下填妥表格一個月內聯絡合資格的申請者，假如申請一個月後團隊未有聯絡閣下，代表閣下未能通過初步篩選。
您所提供的資料會用作日後聯絡之用，只有獲本研究團隊授權人員方可查閱。如果您／您的孩子對填寫申請表格或研究詳情有任何疑問，請於辦公時間聯絡 9671 1756 查詢。
申請表格連結：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3yNko4UyWrBHCJg
==================================================================
As many diseases are closely related to the gut microbiome, the CUHK Paediatric Allergy team is currently investigating the causes of paediatric food allergy and its treatments. Your child’s blood and stool samples could enable our team to understand more about the relationship between food allergy and multi-omics fields, such as the gut microbiome. It would also serve as a valuable reference for other immunological diseases such as eczema, asthma, and allergic rhinitis, contributing greatly to future scientific research.
The team will assess if you/your child’s eligibility to participate in this study with the form linked below. The team will contact you if you/your child is eligible, and arrange a session at the Prince of Wales Hospital for detailed study explanation and signature of consent forms.
The team will collect blood and stool samples from participants in this study. Participants will receive HK$100 food voucher, a blood test report, and a gut microbiome report after completion of the study.
The team will contact eligible participants within one month of receiving your form submission. You have not been selected to participate in the study if the team has not contacted you in a month.
All information collected will be used for contact purposes only and will only be accessible to authorised personnel. Should you/your child have any questions regarding form submission or study details, please call 9671 1756 within office hours.
Registration form link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3yNko4UyWrBHCJg
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

title: HK$300!! Brain Health Study HK$300!! 中大醫學院邀您參與腦部健康研究
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/09/04
»
Announcements
HK$300!! Brain Health Study  HK$300!! 中大醫學院邀您參與腦部健康研究 - CUHK Psychiatry Sleep Assessment Unit
From: Wong Yuen Tung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yuentungwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
便秘？嗅覺變差？睡覺拳打腳踢？有腦退化家族史？
這些看似平常的小毛病，其實可能是柏金遜症等大腦退化的早期先兆！
提早了解大腦健康，預防神經退化！
中大醫學院睡眠研究小組推出全新手機篩查App，誠邀您參與醫學研究！
研究對象：
年齡介乎
50 至 65 歲
的華人
未確診
任何腦神經退化疾病（如柏金遜症、阿爾茲海默症/失智症等）
參加者需完成以下程序：
參與研究
費用全免
，成功完成相關研究程序者最多可獲
HK$300元超市禮券
作為津貼
階段一：
下載手機程式並完成問卷 （約需 15–20 分鐘）
完成後可獲得早期柏金遜病風險分數
符合資格並完成問卷者可獲 HK$100元超市禮券
階段二：
部分參加者將獲邀進一步參與臨床評估
包括身體檢查、臨床訪談、居家睡眠測試及神經認知測試
符合資格並完成階段二者，可額外獲 HK$200元超市禮券
立刻掃描海報右下方
二維碼 (QR Code)
或
點擊連結
下載程式「柏健通」參與研究
IOS用戶：
https://apps.apple.com/hk/app/%E6%9F%8F%E5%81%A5%E9%80%9A/id1626241589
Android用戶：
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2
查詢（致電或WhatsApp）：3919 7792 / 5282 5786（研究助理 黃小姐）
Constipated？Weakened sense of smell？Acting out dream during sleep (punching and kicking) ？Having a family history of neurodegenerative disease？
Common issues like these can actually be early warning signs of brain degeneration, including neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease.
Understand your brain health early to prevent neurodegeneration.
Sleep Assessment Unit - Psychiatry, CUHK has launched a brand-new screening App, and we sincerely invite you to join our medical research study.
Target participants：
Chinese aged between 50 to 65 years old
Have NOT been diagnosed
with any neurodegenerative disease (e.g. Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease/ Dementia, etc.)
What you will need to do:
Participation is completely free. Those who successfully complete the study procedure can receive up to HK$300 in supermarket voucher as an allowance.
Phase 1:
Download the mobile app "柏健通" and complete the questionnaires (take approximately 15-20 minutes)
An early Parkinson’s disease risk score will be provided upon completion
Eligible participants who complete the questionnaires will receive HK$100 supermarket voucher
Phase 2:
Selected participants will be invited to undergo further clinical assessments
Assessments include physical examination, clinical interviews, sleep studies, and neurocognitive assessments
Eligible participants who complete Phase 2 will receive an additional HK$200 supermarket voucher
Interested parties are welcome to participate by
clicking the links below
or
scanning the QR Code
in the poster to download the "柏健通" mobile application:
IOS users:
https://apps.apple.com/hk/app/%E6%9F%8F%E5%81%A5%E9%80%9A/id1626241589
Android users:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2
For details and registration enquiries, please contact our hotline: 39197792 or 5282 5786 (WhatsApp) (Research Assistant, Ms Wong)
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

Announcements
Brief Psychological Training Programme for Social Anxiety  [社交焦慮短期訓練計劃] 誠邀符合條件的廣東話使用者參與 - Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory, Department of Psychology
From: Yanbin, XIE
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ybxie@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募參與者：社交焦慮短期介入訓練計劃
六週指導式自助練習，處理社會評價與自我批評
打破自我批評的惡性循環
找回自我肯定的正向情緒

香港中文大學校園內，全程免費
香港中文大學臨床心理科學實驗室團隊現正推行一項針對社交焦慮問題的短期介入訓練計劃，誠邀符合資格的人士參與。
社交焦慮不止影響我們如何應對社交場合，亦關乎我們如何看待自己，以及如何與他人建立聯繫。目前，社交焦慮問題的治療多採用認知行為取向，研究證實能有效改善個人在社交情境中的功能表現。本計劃則是團隊基於實證研究開發的新訓練方案，採用社會情緒取向，聚焦於處理個人與自我及他人的關係。本項目遵循階梯式照護模式 (stepped-care model)，定位為指導式自助 (guided self-help) 短期介入方案，旨在以較少的時間投入及心理負擔，為參加者提供有效支援。
訓練為期6週，包括「每週1次實體會面 + 自助練習 + 線上心理評估訪談及問卷」 ； 訓練完成後1個月和六個月進行隨訪評估
 「招募要求」
年滿18歲或以上；廣東話流利；
在社交焦慮方面感到困擾，例如在社交或公開場合強烈緊張焦慮、擔心自己被負面評價、迴避社交場合，並明顯影響工作或學習；
現時並未接受其他形式的心理治療或精神科藥物治療；
能夠親身前往香港中文大學校園參與訓練。

「參與流程」
報名後，我們將聯絡您安排篩選問卷及訪談，以確認是否適合參加本計劃，並邀請符合條件者參與訓練。

「報名連結」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eDNm9u2HOUkR302
如有疑問，歡迎聯絡研究團隊：cdclabcuhk@gmail.com
本計劃已獲香港中文大學–新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會審批（CUHK-NTEC CREC 2025.796）。
所有個人資料僅用作研究篩選及介入用途，並會嚴格保密。
香港中文大學臨床心理科學實驗室團隊
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory
Recruiting Participants: Brief Psychological Training Programme for Social Anxiety
The Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a brief intervention programme for individuals experiencing social anxiety difficulties. We invite eligible individuals to participate.
Social anxiety not only affects how we cope in social situations but also involves how we view ourselves and relate to others. While cognitive-behavioural approaches are widely used and evidence-based for treating social anxiety, our team has developed a novel training protocol grounded in empirical research that adopts a social-emotional approach, focusing on improving individuals’ relationships with themselves and with others. Following the stepped-care model, this programme is designed as a brief guided self-help intervention, aiming to provide effective support with minimal time commitment and psychological burden.
The training programme spans 6 weeks and includes:
Weekly in-person sessions (once per week)
Self-help practice exercises
Questionnaire assessments
Follow-up evaluations will be conducted one month and six months after the training.
「Eligibility Criteria」
Aged 18 or above
Fluent in Cantonese
Experiencing significant social anxiety-related distress (e.g., intense anxiety in social or public settings, fear of negative evaluation, avoidance of social situations, with noticeable impact on work or study)
Not currently receiving other forms of psychological therapy or psychiatric medication
Able to attend in-person sessions on the CUHK campus
「Procedures」
After registration, we will contact you to arrange a screening questionnaire and an interview to determine your suitability for the programme. Eligible participants will then be invited to join the training.
「Registration Link」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eDNm9u2HOUkR302
For enquiries, please contact our research team at: cdclabcuhk@gmail.com
This study has been approved by the Joint CUHK-NTEC Clinical Research Ethics Committee (CUHK-NTEC CREC 2025.796).
All personal data collected will be used solely for research screening and intervention purposes and will be kept strictly confidential.
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Announcements
【$200 Coupon】Recruiting Children (aged 4 or under) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study 誠意邀請5歲以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hatch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀5歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 4歲或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿5歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
4) 小朋友18歲以下的兄弟姊妹
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書
2) 網上問卷調查：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is 4 years old or under (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 5 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
4) Children’s brothers and sisters under 18 years old are also welcome to join
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent
2) Online Questionnaire : A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire: Recording children's eating habits
You will receive a $200 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.
For inquiries, please contact 2607-6057 or WhatsApp 6099-3064.

Announcements
Better Gut, Better Sleep? Gut-Brain Study | Earn up to HKD 500  「腸」通無阻，瞓得更好？「腸·腦」研究 | 最高可獲 HKD 500 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Michael Ng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
tsztsunng@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
近年醫學界發現，我們的腸道健康與大腦息息相關！原來「便秘」和「睡眠質素」的改變，可能是腦部退化的早期信號。為了深入了解這條神奇的「腸腦連線」，香港中文大學精神科學系睡眠研究組現正招募研究參加者。
研究對象:
年齡介乎 50 至 80 歲
關注腸道健康或者受便秘問題困擾（如排便困難、次數較少等）
沒有腦退化、精神疾病史
參加者需完成以下簡單程序：
填寫問卷 及 進行簡單面談
進行一次非入侵性睡眠檢測
記錄連續兩星期「大便日記」
進行一次結腸運輸試驗
收集一次大便樣本
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者最多可獲 HKD 500 超市禮券的津貼
如對本研究有興趣，請透過以下連結報名參加：
[網址連結:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eeTcY6hrKILNwhg
]
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電 3919 7792 / 9568 9006 或 WhatsApp 9568 9006與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。謝謝
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Recent research suggests that gut health is closely linked to brain function. Changes in bowel habits (e.g. constipation) and sleep quality may even be early signs of neurodegeneration.
To better understand this “gut–brain axis, we sincerely invite you to take part in our research study.
Who can join:
Aged 50–80
Concerned about gut health or bothered by constipation
No history of dementia or psychiatric disorders
What you will do:

 研究對象：18至70歲華人

超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史

[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 70 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes
If you are unsure whether you have diabetes, a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) will be arranged for you.

Study Procedures Include:
Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.

Announcements
#Recruiting vocally healthy participants aged 18 and above to participate in an acoustic analysis study to explore the quality and characteristics of the voice (HK$150 coupon) 誠意邀請18歲或以上沒有聲線障礙的人士參與探索聲線質量和特徵的聲學分析研究 (HK$150 coupon) - Department of Otorhinolarynogology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: Rina To
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rinato@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學耳鼻咽喉 頭頸外科學系現正招募十八歲或以上沒有聲線障礙的人士參與一項聲學分析的研究，旨在探究平滑化倒頻譜突出峰值 (CPPS) 的臨界值和其診斷準確性。
CPPS是一種可應用於日常對話的聲線聲學分析參數。CPPS相對於其他常用的聲學參數具有更高的診斷準確性。但是，根據文獻的報告顯示，使用不同的語言，聲線樣本類型，和軟件，都會影響到CPPS的結果。我們希望這項研究的結果能夠為臨床醫生和研究人員對聲線障礙患者進行客觀測量並為聲線評估的量化結果提供明確的參考。
招募對象：
年滿十八歲或以上
沒有聲線問題的人士
以廣東話為母語
費用：全免
評估與檢查地點：威爾斯親王醫院
研究程序及内容：
1）參加者將填寫聲線問卷， 並親臨威爾斯親王醫院接受喉纖維內視鏡檢查和聲線錄製。
2）喉纖維內視鏡檢查時能清楚看見咽喉，每次檢查需時約三十分鐘，是屬於低風險的檢查，一般只會感到輕微不適。
報名連結﹕
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4267989
參與研究，獲得獎勵：
完成聲線評估後，您可獲得港幣150元的超市現金券。
名額有限，先到先得。收到報名後，我們會再與合資格的參加者聯絡。
歡迎將此招募信息推薦給身邊有需要的家人以及朋友。
如有查詢，請與研究人員王先生（Mr. Wang）聯絡。
電郵：
zikaiwang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
The Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, is currently recruiting vocally healthy participants aged 18 and above for a study investigating the cut-off score and diagnostic accuracy of the smoothed cepstral peak prominence (CPPS) for Cantonese speakers with dysphonia.
CPPS is a parameter for acoustic analysis of voice that can be used in everyday conversation to provide a more comprehensive and realistic picture of an individual's vocal characteristics in natural communication situations. CPPS has a higher diagnostic accuracy than other commonly used acoustic parameters. However, reports in the literature indicate that the use of different languages, different types of voice samples, and different software can affect the results of the CPPS. We hope that the results of this study will provide clinicians and researchers with a clear reference for the quantitative results of objective measurement and voice assessment in patients with voice disorders.
Recruitment target:
Age 18 or above
People who do not have voice problems
Fluent in Cantonese as a native language or proficient in Cantonese
Cost: Free of charge
Location: Prince of Wales Hospital
Procedures and details of this Study:
Participants will undergo a laryngeal videostroboscopy examination and a comprehensive voice assessment at Prince of Wales Hospital.
A videostroboscopy examination can clearly observe the throat to detect whether it has structural or functional problem for speaking. Each examination takes approximately thirty minutes. It is a low-risk procedure, and participants typically only experience mild discomfort.
Registration link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4267989
Participate in the study and receive a reward:
After completing the voice assessment, you will receive a HK$ 150 supermarket gift card.
Limited seats available on a first-come first-served basis. We will contact you afterwards if you are suitable to join this study.
Welcome to recommend this recruitment information to your family and friends in need.
If you have any inquiries, please contact Mr. Wang.
Email:
zikaiwang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

【Call for Participation】 Smart Logistics Datathon 2026   【報名從速! 】智慧物流數據建模馬拉松比賽2026 - Asian Institute of Supply Chains & Logistics (AISCL)
From: Tammy Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
aiscl@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The Asian Institute of Supply Chains & Logistics of The Chinese University of Hong Kong will host the “
Smart Logistics
Datathon 2026
”, taking place from
October 30 to November 1, 2026
at the Hong Kong International Aviation Academy campus.
Full-time university students in Asia are welcome to sign up as a team of two to three members.  At most 20 teams will be selected and invited to compete on-site in Hong Kong. The Smart Logistics Datathon aims to inspire and empower young talents to explore innovative solutions and deepen their understanding of modern logistics challenges and opportunities.  Building on current AI trends, this year’s Datathon centers on the theme “
AI-Driven Horizons for Logistics Intelligence
”, placing particular emphasis on leveraging AI to facilitate data analysis and drive innovative insights.
Throughout the 35-hour competition, participating teams will work on real-world transport and logistics datasets, applying their analytical and creative thinking to generate innovative insights that can drive value for the logistics industry. The competition offers an excellent platform for students to strengthen skills in analytics, teamwork, problem-solving, time management, and public speaking. At the end of the event, each team will have 10 minutes to present their results to a panel of expert judges. Scholarships will be awarded to the winning teams.
Don’t miss this exciting opportunity to connect with talents from across Asia and compete for a scholarship prize!
********************************************************************************************
More details about the Datathon, can be found at the event website (
https://aiscl.cuhk.edu.hk/datathon2026/
).

title: Invitation to Participate in the CFA Research Challenge 2026–27
bodyText:

Events / Activities
Invitation to Participate in the CFA Research Challenge 2026–27  - Department of Finance
From: Quantitative Finance Programme
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
qfin@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
We are pleased to announce the recruitment of representative teams for CUHK in the CFA Research Challenge 2026–27. This global case competition offers valuable opportunities to:
Enhance your investment analysis skills
Strengthen your resume
Expand your professional network
The CFA Research Challenge cultivates best practices in equity research through hands-on mentoring and intensive training in company analysis.
Learn more:
https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/events/research-challenge
Eligibility
All undergraduate and postgraduate students (full-time or part-time) from any discipline are eligible to apply, except those who already hold the CFA designation.
Our school has achieved excellent results in recent years:
2022: Champion and Finalist
2023: 1st Runner-up and 2nd Runner-up
2024: Two Finalists
Assessment & Selection
As places in this year's Challenge are limited, we will be conducting an internal selection process to identify
two teams
to represent CUHK.
We will assess teams based on their slide deck and Excel submissions.
Closely matched candidates may be invited to a presentation selection round on the morning of September 16 (Wed), after which the two representative teams will be confirmed.
Application Process
Deadline: September 12, 23:59 HKT
Team Composition: 4 to 5 students
Submission Requirements
Prepare a slide deck (maximum 8 slides) for the equity research report on UBTECH (9880), TAIHING (6811), or MINIMAX (0100).
Use data to support your views.
Clearly list the data sources and approach used for analysis.
Submit both:
A single PDF file (consolidating team CVs and the slide deck).
The supporting Excel file with your analysis.
Upload here:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13740099
Best regards,
Edwin Mok, CFA
Associate Director, MSc Programme in Finance
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

⭐ [CUHK Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences] Invitation for Thyroid Disease Patients for Free Thyroid Eye Screening ⭐⭐【中大眼科】招募甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費甲狀腺眼篩檢 - Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences (OVS)
From: Hanson Wong (OVS)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yiumanwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
⭐⭐
【中大眼科】招募甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢
【香港中文大學眼科研究】招募甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢及臨床研究
香港中文大學醫學院眼科及視覺科學學系現正進行一項臨床研究，誠邀已確診或懷疑患有甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢，以評估是否患有甲狀腺眼病（Thyroid Eye Disease, TED），以及是否適合參與後續臨床研究。
什麼是甲狀腺眼病？
甲狀腺眼病是常見於甲狀腺疾病（如格里夫氏症）的眼部併發症，可引致以下情況：
眼乾、刺痛或流淚
眼皮腫脹或向上收縮
眼球突出（俗稱「眼凸」）
外觀改變，甚至影響視力
及早發現及治療，有助減低病情惡化的風險。
招募對象
符合以下條件人士歡迎參加：
年齡介乎
18
至
80
歲
已確診或懷疑患有甲狀腺疾病（包括甲亢或甲減）
輕至中度甲狀腺眼病患者（已確診或懷疑）
未曾接受甲狀腺眼病相關治療
非懷孕或非哺乳人士
能理解粵語、普通話或英語，並能閱讀中文或英文
即使未確定是否患有甲狀腺眼病，只要曾患甲狀腺疾病，亦歡迎參加篩檢。
研究內容及安排
免費全面眼科檢查
由專業眼科醫生評估及跟進
所有研究相關檢查及評估費用全免
符合資格者將獲邀參與為期約
12
個月
的臨床藥物研究
地點（由研究團隊安排）：
香港中文大學眼科中心（九龍）
或 香港中文大學醫院（沙田）
（最終是否符合研究資格將由研究團隊作進一步評估）
報名及詳情
請透過以下連結登記參與甲狀腺眼病篩檢：

立即登記篩檢
研究團隊將與合資格人士聯絡，安排進一步篩查。
查詢
香港中文大學醫學院眼科及視覺科學學系
電話：3943 0790（何小姐）
WhatsApp：5642 7952
請註明：「查詢 SAVEMORETED 甲狀腺眼疾藥物臨床研究」
您的參與不僅有助及早了解自身眼睛健康狀況，亦有助推動甲狀腺眼病的醫學研究，為未來患者帶來更多治療可能。
The Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) is currently conducting a clinical study on Thyroid Eye Disease (TED). We warmly invite individuals with confirmed or suspected thyroid disorders to participate in a
free comprehensive eye screening
to assess for TED and potential eligibility for further clinical research.
What is Thyroid Eye Disease (TED)?
Thyroid Eye Disease is a condition commonly associated with thyroid disorders such as Graves’ disease. It may lead to:
Dryness, irritation, or excessive tearing
Eyelid swelling or retraction
Protrusion of the eyes (proptosis)
Changes in appearance and, in some cases, vision impairment
Early detection and appropriate management are important to reduce the risk of disease progression.
Eligibility Criteria
Individuals who meet the following criteria are welcome to participate:
Aged
18 to 80 years
Diagnosed with or suspected of having thyroid disorders (hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism)
Diagnosed with or suspected of having
mild to moderate Thyroid Eye Disease
Have
not received prior treatment
specifically for Thyroid Eye Disease
Not pregnant or breastfeeding
Able to understand Cantonese, Mandarin, or English, and read Chinese or English
Individuals who are unsure whether they have Thyroid Eye Disease are also encouraged to join the screening if they have a history of thyroid conditions.
Study Details
Participants will receive:
Free comprehensive ophthalmic examination
Professional assessment and follow-up by ophthalmologists
All study-related examinations at no cost
Eligible participants may be invited to join a
12-month clinical drug study
, subject to further screening and eligibility assessment.

Study locations (by arrangement):
CUHK Eye Centre (Kowloon)
CUHK Medical Centre (Sha Tin)
Registration and Further Information
To register for the Thyroid Eye Disease screening, please visit:

Register for TED Screening
Our research team will contact eligible applicants to arrange further screening.
Enquiries
Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences
Faculty of Medicine, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Tel: 3943 0790 (Ms. Ho)
WhatsApp: 5642 7952
Please specify: “SAVEMORETED Clinical Study Enquiry”
Participation in this study not only helps you better understand your eye health, but also contributes to advancing research and improving treatment options for patients with Thyroid Eye Disease.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

Eligibility Criteria Individuals who meet the following criteria are welcome to participate: Aged 18 to 80 years Diagnosed with or suspected of having thyroid disorders (hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism) Diagnosed with or suspected of having mild to moderate Thyroid Eye Disease Have not received prior treatment specifically for Thyroid Eye Disease Not pregnant or breastfeeding Able to understand Cantonese, Mandarin, or English, and read Chinese or English Individuals who are unsure whether they have Thyroid Eye Disease are also encouraged to join the screening if they have a history of thyroid conditions.

Announcements
Curbing Central Obesity [$200 coupon] 招攬 中央肥胖改善計劃誠邀40-64歲合資格人士參與運動及飲食介入（$200港幣現金券） - Department of Sports Science and Physical Education
From: MA Chun hin
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ericaaama@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
邀請參加本項研究
初步證據顯示, 間歇性飲食（INTD）和高強度間歇運動（HIIE）在改善心血管代謝健康和減重方面存在協同作用。本研究旨在探討INTD和HIIE對體力活動不足的中央肥胖成人的心血管健康影響。
受試者招募
本研究的目標人群為香港體力活動不足的中年成年人（年齡40至64歲），並且具有中央肥胖。中央肥胖將定義為男性腰圍達90厘米（cm）或以上，女性腰圍達80厘米或以上。如果您對任何列出的條件有疑問，請諮詢研究人員。
https://forms.gle/FmCFdyFgdEyudP8k8
如您有任何疑問，可通過以下渠道聯絡這項研究的相關人員：
馬先生
WhatsApp: 39436085
電郵:
sspe.project0716@gmail.com
Invitation to Participate in Research Study
Preliminary evidence has suggested a synergistic interaction effect of intermittent dieting (INTD) and high intensity interval exercise (HIIE) on cardio-metabolic health and weight loss. This study aims to examine the effects of INTD and HIIE and intermittent dieting for cardiometabolic and cardiovascular fitness in physically inactive adults with central obesity.
Participant Recruitment
The target population of the proposed study will be physically inactive middle-aged adults (aged 40–64 years) with central obesity in Hong Kong. Central obesity will be defined as having a waist circumference 90 centimeters (cm) or above for men and 80 cm or above for women. If you are unsure about any of the listed conditions, then you should consult with the researchers.
https://forms.gle/FmCFdyFgdEyudP8k8
Contact Us
If you are interested and have any inquiries, please feel free to contact us:
Mr. MA
WhatsApp: 39436085
Email: sspe.project0716@gmail.com

We are hiring Reviewers for Explanatory Reading Comprehension Tasks!
We are seeking detail-oriented reviewers to evaluate our explanatory reading comprehension questions. This position involves taking the tests using your background knowledge and providing feedback on item difficulty.
Task Requirements & Workflow
Zero-Text Answering:
You will complete reading comprehension questions based on your existing general knowledge without reading the source passage first.
Difficulty Rating:
After completing each question, you will rate its difficulty based on your testing experience.
Batch Structure:
Tasks are organized into parts, with each part containing 6 question sets.
Time Commitment & Compensation
Time:
Approximately 50–60 minutes per part.
Allowance:
HKD 30 per completed part.
If you are interested in joining us, please feel free to contact me at
[1155191602@link.cuhk.edu.hk]

[Co-op@CUHK Student Stories: The Beginning of Their Co-op Journey]
Every Co-op journey begins with a reason. Some students seek clarity about their career aspirations, while others hope to gain real-world experience, develop essential workplace skills, or build professional networks. Through Co-op@CUHK, students take a meaningful step towards discovering their potential, enhancing their work readiness and preparing for their future careers.
Driven by curiosity, ambition, and a desire to learn beyond the classroom, Co-op students chose to step outside their comfort zones and embrace new opportunities. Please check out their stories and motivations for joining the Co-op programme.
Co-op is a space to explore possibilities before making career decisions.
Co-op empowers students to grow, discover, and succeed.
Co-op helps students build confidence and strengthen their career readiness.
Looking back, these students’ motivations for joining Co-op have evolved into precious learning experiences and lasting career insights. Their transformative journeys with Co-op@CUHK unlocked new opportunities, strengthened professional capabilities, and prepared them to navigate the future of work with confidence.
Application for the 6th cohort is now open. Apply
here
and seize the opportunity to explore, learn, and grow through Co-op@CUHK! Year 2 or above students from all disciplines, both local and non-local, are eligible to apply!
To stay updated with the latest information, follow our Programme on
LinkedIn
and
IG
.
If you have any questions, feel free to reach out to our team at
coop@cuhk.edu.hk
or call 3943 5674 / 3943 1422.
Best regards,

bodyText:

Microsoft Copilot Chat Tips Ace Your Data Assignments — Instant Analysis!  - ITSC
From: ITSC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
itsc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Got an Excel file and no idea what to do with it? Whether it's a stats class or lab report —
Copilot
can
analyze your data, generate charts, and explain the results
like a personal data scientist.
Prompt 1 — copy & paste it!

Upload & explore
"I've uploaded my dataset. Give me: 1) A summary of what this data contains 2) Key statistics for numeric columns 3) Interesting patterns or outliers 4) 3 questions this data could answer."
Prompt 2 — keep the conversation going!

Visualize it
"Create a bar chart comparing [column A] across [column B]. Also create a line chart showing the trend over time. Use clear labels, a legend, and a title. Explain what each chart reveals."
Prompt 3 — go advanced!

Advanced analysis
"Run a correlation analysis between [variable 1] and [variable 2]. Create a scatter plot with a trend line. Is the correlation significant? What does this mean? How would I report this in a paper?"
Why this works:
Copilot doesn't just crunch numbers — it explains results in language you can actually use in your assignments!

Bonus tip:
Try:
"Create a heatmap of correlations between all numeric variables and highlight the 3 most interesting relationships"
— instant extra credit vibes!
Looking for more ways to level up your Copilot game? Check out previous
All IT - Microsoft Copilot Chat Usage Tips
for even more helpful guidance and best practices.

Dear Students,
3rd edition of the HK Express Gotta GO! Sustainable Explorer Challenge is back and now open for applications!
Love travel? Want to turn your ideas into a real adventure?
The
3rd HK Express Gotta GO! Sustainable Explorer Challenge
is now open for applications. Team up in pairs, design a
4D3N
lower-carbon travel itinerary
, and compete for the chance to bring your trip to life flying with HK Express!
Prizes & Opportunities
If your team is selected as one of the
5 finalist teams
, you’ll receive:
Round-Trip flight tickets by HK Express
HK$4,000 travel fund per person
The chance to carry out your proposed trip in January 2027
And if your team wins the
Champion
title, each member will also receive an extra set of round-trip tickets to any HK Express destination.
Why join?
You’ll get the chance to:
Learn more about sustainable travel and carbon footprint awareness
Build skills in itinerary design, storytelling and pitching
Present your idea to a judging panel
Gain hands-on experience through a real travel challenge
Meet students from universities across Hong Kong, Macau and other parts of the Greater Bay Area
Who can join?
You must apply in a team of 2 undergraduate students (local or non-local) currently enrolled at one of the following institutions (arranged alphabetically):
Hong Kong Baptist University (HKBU)
Lingnan University (Lingnan)
Macao Polytechnic University (MPU)
Macao University of Tourism (UTM)
The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)
The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen (CUHK SZ)
The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU)
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST)
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou) (HKUST GZ)
Students from different universities may form a team together. Individuals may need to obtain relevant visas or travel permits for entering Hong Kong where applicable.
Interested? How it works:
Fill in the
Programme Briefing Registration
F
orm
and register your preferred
Programme Briefing
session
(Compulsory).
Attend the Programme Briefing to learn about the programme and get exclusive tips from previous winners.
Form a team of 2
and complete the
Application Form
to enroll into the programme and indicate your preferred workshop sessions.
Learn about sustainable tourism, carbon accounting and social media skills through
hands-on workshops
.
Draft your 4D3N
sustainable travel itinerary
following the principles of sustainable tourism and submit your proposal for screening.
Top 30 teams will be invited to a
Pitching Presentation.
Five finalist teams
will be selected from the pitching presentation to execute their itineraries with
sponsor
ship
.
Finalists to compete in
Final Battle
after bringing their itinerary to life, sharing their experience and learnings from the trip with
the
public and judging panel
.
Key dates

Dear Students,
3rd edition of the HK Express Gotta GO! Sustainable Explorer Challenge is back and now open for applications!
Love travel? Want to turn your ideas into a real adventure?
The
3rd HK Express Gotta GO! Sustainable Explorer Challenge
is now open for applications. Team up in pairs, design a
4D3N
lower-carbon travel itinerary
, and compete for the chance to bring your trip to life flying with HK Express!
Prizes & Opportunities
If your team is selected as one of the
5 finalist teams
, you’ll receive:
Round-Trip flight tickets by HK Express
HK$4,000 travel fund per person
The chance to carry out your proposed trip in January 2027
And if your team wins the
Champion
title, each member will also receive an extra set of round-trip tickets to any HK Express destination.
Why join?
You’ll get the chance to:
Learn more about sustainable travel and carbon footprint awareness
Build skills in itinerary design, storytelling and pitching
Present your idea to a judging panel
Gain hands-on experience through a real travel challenge
Meet students from universities across Hong Kong, Macau and other parts of the Greater Bay Area
Who can join?
You must apply in a team of 2 undergraduate students (local or non-local) currently enrolled at one of the following institutions (arranged alphabetically):
Hong Kong Baptist University (HKBU)
Lingnan University (Lingnan)
Macao Polytechnic University (MPU)
Macao University of Tourism (UTM)
The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)
The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen (CUHK SZ)
The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU)
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST)
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou) (HKUST GZ)
Students from different universities may form a team together. Individuals may need to obtain relevant visas or travel permits for entering Hong Kong where applicable.
Interested? How it works:
Fill in the
Programme Briefing Registration
F
orm
and register your preferred
Programme Briefing
session
(Compulsory).

Form a team of 2
and complete the
Application Form
to enroll into the programme and indicate your preferred workshop sessions.
Learn about sustainable tourism, carbon accounting and social media skills through
hands-on workshops
.
Draft your 4D3N
sustainable travel itinerary
following the principles of sustainable tourism and submit your proposal for screening.
Top 30 teams will be invited to a
Pitching Presentation.
Five finalist teams
will be selected from the pitching presentation to execute their itineraries with
sponsor
ship
.
Finalists to compete in
Final Battle
after bringing their itinerary to life, sharing their experience and learnings from the trip with
the
public and judging panel
.

From: Zhou Zhenyi
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155198832@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【香港中文大學研究邀約｜招募母語為廣東話的中大本科生參與線上訪談】
香港中文大學教育心理學系 LEaPP Lab 現正進行一項研究，旨在了解大學生的學習經驗與相關心理歷程。我們誠邀母語為廣東話的香港中文大學本科生參與本研究訪談。
參與資格
年滿18歲；
目前為香港中文大學本科生；
母語為廣東話。
參與流程與回報
有興趣參與的同學首先需要完成一份約5分鐘的背景資料調查，以確認是否符合研究要求。
研究團隊將根據背景調查結果聯絡符合資格的參與者，並邀請其參與一次約20–30分鐘的線上訪談。
完成訪談後，參與者將獲得HKD $50報酬，以感謝您的支持。
參與方式
請點擊以下連結完成背景資料調查：

https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_bE4IovsqrgWaTfo
研究團隊將根據您的回答確認是否符合訪談資格，並透過電郵與合資格參與者聯絡。
研究聲明：
所有收集的資料將嚴格保密，僅供學術研究用途。參與純屬自願性質，參與者可隨時退出研究。
聯絡我們：
如有任何查詢，歡迎聯絡研究小組：
xinjiechen@cuhk.edu.hk
zhenyizhou@cuhk.edu.hk
感謝您的參與與貢獻。
香港中文大學教育心理學系 LEaPP Lab 敬啟
English Version
【CUHK Research Invitation | Native Cantonese-speaking Undergraduate Students Wanted for an Online Interview】
The LEaPP Lab at the Department of Educational Psychology, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), is currently conducting a research project to understand university students’ learning experiences and related psychological processes. We invite native Cantonese-speaking CUHK undergraduate students to participate in this research interview.
Eligibility

Telephone Survey Research Laboratory of Hong Kong Institute of Asia-Pacific Studies will recruit undergraduate student helpers for conducting telephone surveys. The telephone surveys are normally carried out from 6:15 p.m.to 10:15 p.m. (4 hours). The working dates are irregular. The hourly rate for telephone interviewers will be HK64/hr. Those who can conduct telephone interviews by fluent Cantonese is prerequisite. If you are interested in this job, please apply via the online application system by the following link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13724138
Those who have submitted the online application will be put into the pool of waiting list. We will hold a briefing session for fresh interviewers irregularly and will select the applicants from the waiting list. Those who are selected will be informed by email and are required to attend a briefing session before formal fieldwork.

Invited Talk | The Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University Practice of Education + AI (Wednesday, 2 September 2026)  - Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research
From: Andy WONG
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
andy.wong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
How do universities move from AI strategy to a tangible, sustainable reality?
Join us for an insightful virtual talk, "From Strategy to Ecosystem: The XJTLU Practice of Education + AI".
We are thrilled to welcome
Dr Xin BI
from Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University (XJTLU), who will share how XJTLU is building an AI-driven educational ecosystem. Drawing on two practices both recognised by the IIOE Higher Education Digitalisation Pioneer Case Award, the talk will explore three interconnected dimensions of AI integration:
Leadership: How university leadership aligns strategy, governance, and resource allocation to drive the AI vision.
Pedagogy: How faculty translate AI into classroom practice, supported by professional development to foster AI literacy and personalised learning.
Technology: How strategic intent is converted into working platforms, including the
XIPU AI Agent
and the
Learning Mall
ecosystem.
Whether you are an educator, institutional leader, or ed-tech enthusiast, this talk will offer practical, transferable insights into reshaping the educational paradigm.

Time: 2:45 pm – 4:00 pm (UTC+8)
Venue: Online via Zoom

title: Recruitment of Student Helpers for CUHK VR Open Session HK$80/hour
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/28
»
Announcements
Recruitment of Student Helpers for CUHK VR Open Session HK$80/hour   - Department of English
From: Prof. Wilkinson Daniel Wong Gonzales
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
wdwonggonzales@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Get hands-on experience with VR technology while supporting a CUHK research and learning event!
We are recruiting enthusiastic, responsible, and proactive CUHK students to support our upcoming CUHK VR Open Session, where participants will have the opportunity to experience VR-based learning simulations and explore immersive technologies for learning and communication.
Event Details
Dates: 17–18 November 2026
Time: 9:00 AM–6:00 PM
Venue: Yasumoto International Academic Park, CUHK
Application Deadline: 15 September 2026
Student Helper Payment: HK$80/hour
The expected working period is 9:00 AM–6:00 PM (up to 9 hours), equivalent to HK$720 for a full day.
The 9-hour period includes appropriate breaks and lunch time. Please note that lunch and snacks will not be provided.
We expect to recruit approximately 4–5 Student Helpers per day. Applicants may indicate which day(s) and hours they are available, although priority will be given to students who can commit to a full day.
Who Can Apply?
Applicants must:
be currently registered CUHK students with active student status;
be eligible to receive payment under CUHK Student Helper arrangements;
be proactive, responsible, approachable, and willing to assist participants;
be comfortable communicating and working with people from different backgrounds;
be able to communicate in English; and
preferably be able to communicate in Cantonese and Mandarin/Putonghua
Students interested in Virtual Reality (VR), EdTech, AI, games, immersive learning, or emerging technologies are especially encouraged to apply.
No previous VR experience is required. Instructions and guidance on the equipment and assigned duties will be provided.
What Will Student Helpers Do?
Student Helpers will:
welcome and guide participants during the Open Session;
help participants put on and use VR headsets;
explain basic VR controls and procedures;
support participants while they experience the VR simulations;
proactively approach participants who may need assistance;
assist the organising team with session coordination and participant flow; and
help with other basic event-support duties as needed.
Physical Requirements
The role involves active event support. Student Helpers may need to:
stand for periods of time;
move around the venue regularly;
assist participants with putting on and adjusting VR headsets; and
handle and help organise VR equipment.
Payment and Selection
Payment will be processed through CUHK. Applicants must therefore be eligible for appointment and payment as CUHK Student Helpers.
Selected applicants will be contacted by email.
As only approximately 4–5 helpers are required per day, submission of the application form does not guarantee selection.
Before You Apply
Please make sure that you are genuinely available for the time slots you indicate.
Priority may be given to applicants who can commit to longer shifts or a full day.
Selected Student Helpers will receive further information about their duties, payment arrangements, and event-day procedures by email.
About the Project
This event forms part of the CUHK research project:
“Speak Up, Skill Up: VR Microinterventions for Bias Response Training with Evolutionary Computation”
CUHK Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics approval: SBRE-26-0023
Student Helpers are being recruited to support event operations and are not being recruited as research participants through this advertisement.
Apply
Application deadline: 15 September 2026
Application form:
https://forms.gle/JqStBJQca71uzxur7
Enquiries
For questions about the Student Helper role or the VR Open Session, please contact:
Wilkinson Daniel Wong Gonzales (PI)
wdwonggonzales@cuhk.edu.hk
Aru Nurgissayeva (Assistant)
arunurgissayeva@cuhk.edu.hk
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

Library Orientation for Undergraduate Students 2026 (3 - 15 Sep)
Welcome from the CUHK Library! As you begin your university journey, there is much to explore, and the CUHK Library is always here to support you.
Come and explore both physical and electronic library that can support your academic success!
Library Tours & Briefings
Date:
3 – 15 Sep 2026
Language:
English / Cantonese / Putonghua
What you will discover:
Study spaces and room booking services
Computers, printing, and other facilities
How to find books, e-books, journals, and databases
Course readings and past exam papers
Using AI Responsibly at University
And much more…

Students who attend the briefing session will receive
a welcome gift
and
have a chance to win a coupon
on the spot. Be sure to
sign up
!

https://www.lib.cuhk.edu.hk/en/learning/orientation/#UG

初到中大？參加圖書館迎新活動（導賞及簡介會），領取迎新禮品！
歡迎來到中文大學圖書館！當你展開大學生活的新篇章，校園內有許多資源等待你發掘，而中文大學圖書館將一直為你的學習旅程提供支援。
誠邀你前來探索圖書館的實體及電子資源，助你提升學習成效，邁向學術成功！
圖書館導賞及簡介會
日期：2026年9月3日至9月15日
語言：英語／廣東話／普通話
你將會認識：
研習空間及研讀室預約服務
電腦、列印及其他設施
如何查找館藏書籍、電子書、期刊及資料庫
課程指定讀物及歷屆考試試卷
在大學中負責任地使用人工智能（AI）
以及更多精彩內容……
參加迎新簡介會的同學將會獲得一份小禮品，透過互動遊戲，還有機會獲得禮券。
立即
報名
吧！

From: Amber Lam
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
You are cordially invited to attend a public lecture organised by the Institute of Chinese Studies (ICS) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong on Thursday, 24 September 2026. It is our honour to welcome Dr. Jennifer Dorothy LEE, ICS Visiting Fellowship visiting scholar from the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, to deliver a talk on the topic:
“Shuttered Eyes, Kinship Threads: Tracing Music and Migration in the Family of Yo-Yo Ma”
.
Abstract:
What can a single photograph say? The black-and-white artefact featured in this talk, a product of the Nanjing Guanghua Photo Studio, shows a family like many others in 1946, caught between wars and continents. The figures pictured are musicians, primarily, but also teachers, scientists, and jacks-of-all-trades. They are the progenitors of the famed cellist Yo-Yo Ma, of his sister Yeou-Cheng, and of me. Drawing on lenses that range from music to art history to something akin to critical fabulation, I unfold the episodic, recursive process of unearthing my family history for the very first time. The process starts from initial encounters with a single photograph that cue a forensic exploration, compelling me to extract from handwritten letters, intimate anecdotes, musical manuscripts, and persistent memories. At certain points, through an historian's microscope, I reconstruct the spaces in which these familial figures lived and breathed. At other points, I activate imaginative techniques, such as the musical notations they leave behind, to piece together the facts and fabulations of the past.
Speaker:
Dr. Jennifer Dorothy Lee
is Associate Professor of Art History, Theory, & Criticism at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago. Trained in comparative literature, Lee brings literary frames and methodologies to work with visual and material objects. Lee's first book,
Anxiety Aesthetics: Maoist Legacies in China, 1978–1985
(University of California Press, 2024) offers a sustained study of aesthetics, art, and subjectivity redefined in the historical moment bridging the Mao era with Dengist reforms. Lee's current book project,
Diasporic Longing
, explores belonging, displacement, and music from Asia to Europe among her family of musicians. Tracking her progenitors' wartime migrations amid 20th-century upheavals, Lee weaves biography, storytelling, fragments of poetry, and musical notation to revisit the meanings of diaspora across three continents. Lee holds a PhD in East Asian Studies from New York University, an MA in Comparative Literature from the University of London, and a BA in English & Comparative Literature from Columbia University.

Participate in this study and earn 300 HKD! :) English learning from computer-mediated English reading  - Department of English
From: Jookyoung Jung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jookyoungjung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Participate in this study and earn 300 HKD! :)
English learning from computer-mediated English reading
Hello! I am Jookyoung Jung, Associate Professor at the Department of English. I'd like to invite you to a study that examines the relationship between computer-mediated English reading and English learning.
If you decide to participate, I will ask you to take part in three experimental sessions.
In Session 1, we will ask you to complete a brief questionnaire about yourself. Next, you will take English proficiency tests that measure your grammar and vocabulary.
In Session 2, you will read English texts while your eye movements are recorded using an eye-tracker.
In Session 3, you will take a series of memory tasks.
In return for your participation, I am able to offer you 300 HKD at the end of the 3rd session.
If you meet the criteria below, please join our study!
Your age is 18 years or older.
Chinese is your first language, and English is your second language.
Your English score (no lower, no higher!!): DSE English: 4-5; IELTS: 5.5-6.5; TOEFL iBT: 75-95; Cambridge English Scale: 160-180
If you want to participate in this study, please complete this online survey so that we can contact you and schedule your sessions.
Link:
https://forms.gle/9NyVzTHPBvW7wgHz6
If you have any queries about the study, please feel free to contact our team at tobiiproject2021@gmail.com begin_of_the_skype_highlighting. I would be very grateful if you would agree to take part! :-)

bodyText:
