Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/28
»
Announcements
Call for native Cantonese and Mandarin speakers for a short pronunciation study.（HKD 64 per hour) 招募廣東話及普通話母語者參與實驗材料錄音（每小時64元津貼） - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: LI Chunzi
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
chunzili@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學語言學及現代語言系現正籌備一項詞彙判斷實驗，現招募廣東話及普通話母語者擔任發音人，為實驗錄製語音刺激材料。
發音人資格：
年滿18歲；
母語為廣東話或普通話；
曾學習國際音標（IPA）或具備基本閱讀國際音標的能力；
沒有語言、言語或聽力障礙記錄。
如有興趣擔任發音人，請點擊以下連結填寫登記表格：
https://forms.gle/nAnGswT7jrBbTxh77
合資格的登記者將獲聯絡，進行簡短的發音篩選。通過篩選後，我們將與合適的發音人安排正式的錄製工作。
正式錄音工作的津貼按每小時港幣64元計算。
您在登記表格中提供的個人資料只會用於發音人招募、篩選及聯絡，並會嚴格保密。
如有任何查詢，請電郵
chunzili@cuhk.edu.hk
。
The Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is preparing a wordlikeness judgment experiment. We are recruiting native Cantonese and Mandarin speakers to record speech stimuli for the experiment.
Speaker eligibility:
Aged 18 or above;
Native speaker of Cantonese or Mandarin;
Have learned the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) or have basic familiarity with reading IPA;
No history of language, speech, or hearing disorders.
If you are interested in serving as a speaker, please register using the following Google Form:
https://forms.gle/nAnGswT7jrBbTxh77
Eligible registrants will be contacted to complete a brief pronunciation screening. Speakers who pass the screening will be contacted to arrange the formal recording of the experimental stimuli.
Compensation for the formal recording work will be calculated at a rate of HKD 64 per hour.
The personal information provided in the registration form will be used only for speaker recruitment, screening, and contact purposes and will be kept strictly confidential.
If you have any questions, please email
chunzili@cuhk.edu.hk
.

bodyText:

Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/28
»
Announcements
Enhancement to VeriGuide Assignment Submission Service from Academic Year 2026-27 VeriGuide作業提交服務將於2026-2027學年起進行增強 - The VeriGuide Team, Department of Computer Science and Engineering
From: Kevin Lam
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
veriguide@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
To provide additional support for academic integrity in assignment submissions, VeriGuide will be enhanced with Turnitin originality checking.
Turnitin is a widely used originality checking service adopted by universities worldwide to support academic integrity and good academic practices.
The enhancement is currently scheduled to take effect on
7 September 2026
, subject to final system validation.
Key Points
For
student course assignment submissions
made on or after
7 September 2026
, submissions through VeriGuide, including those submitted via the VeriGuide integration in Blackboard, will also be submitted to Turnitin for originality checking.
Teachers will be able to access the
Turnitin Originality Report
through the VeriGuide system.
The Turnitin report will complement the existing academic integrity checks available in VeriGuide and provide additional information to support the review of assignment submissions.
This enhancement applies to
student course assignment submissions
only. Other submission types and services supported by VeriGuide will continue to operate under their existing arrangements.
The existing VeriGuide submission workflow will remain largely unchanged to minimize disruption to teaching and learning activities.
Students will continue to submit assignments through VeriGuide as before.
During the submission process, students will be presented with a Turnitin consent statement regarding the processing of their submissions by Turnitin.
This enhancement is designed to provide teachers and students with additional tools and information to support academic integrity and good academic practices.
For enquiries regarding this enhancement, please contact
Mr Patrick Lau
(Email:
tplau@cuhk.edu.hk
; Tel:
3943 9457
).
為了進一步確保作業提交的學術誠信，VeriGuide 將新增 Turnitin 原創性檢測功能。
Turnitin 是一項廣為使用的原創性檢測服務，旨在維護學術誠信和良好的學術規範。
此增強功能目前計劃於
2026 年 9 月 7 日
生效，但需通過最終系統驗證。
重點
於
2026 年 9 月 7 日或之後
提交的
學生課程作業
，透過 VeriGuide 提交的作業（包括透過 Blackboard 中的 VeriGuide 整合提交的作業）也將提交給 Turnitin 進行原創性檢查。
教師將能夠透過 VeriGuide 系統查閱
Turnitin 的原創性報告
。
Turnitin 的報告將補充 VeriGuide 中現有的學術誠信檢查，並提供額外資訊以輔助作業提交的審查工作。
此項功能強化
僅適用於學生提交的課程作業
。VeriGuide 所支援的其他提交類型及服務，將繼續依照現有安排運作。
為盡量減少對教學活動的干擾，現有的 VeriGuide 提交工作流程將基本保持不變。
學生將一如既往地透過 VeriGuide 提交作業。
在提交作業的過程中，學生將看到一份關於 Turnitin 處理其提交內容的 Turnitin 同意聲明。
這項改進旨在為教師和學生提供額外的工具與資訊，以支持學術誠信與良好的學術規範。
有關此項改進的查詢，請聯絡
劉先生
（電子郵件：
tplau@cuhk.edu.hk
；電話：
3943 9457
）。
为了进一步保障作业提交的学术诚信，VeriGuide 将新增 Turnitin 原创性检测功能。
Turnitin 是一款被广泛采用的原创性检测服务，旨在维护学术诚信和良好的学术规范。
该功能增强目前计划于
2026年9月7日

要点

2026年9月7日及之后
提交的
学生课程作业
，通过VeriGuide提交的作业（包括通过Blackboard中VeriGuide集成提交的作业）也将同时提交至Turnitin进行原创性检查。
教师可通过VeriGuide系统访问
Turnitin原创性报告
。
Turnitin报告将补充VeriGuide现有的学术诚信检查功能，并提供更多信息以支持作业审核。
此项改进
仅适用于学生课程作业提交
。VeriGuide支持的其他提交类型和服务将继续按现有方式运行。
现有的VeriGuide提交流程将基本保持不变，以最大程度地减少对教学活动的影响。

在提交过程中，系统将向学生展示一份关于 Turnitin 处理其提交内容的 Turnitin 同意声明。
这项改进旨在为教师和学生提供更多工具和信息，以支持学术诚信和良好的学术规范。

The Independent Learning Centre (ILC) offers a wide range of workshops and activities to support learning of language and communication skills. Visit our website for more information: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ (20260831)  - ILC
From: ILC

【Weekly Highlights - English Section 】
A. Communication, Study Skills and Job Preparation Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre offers English workshops 31 August to 4 September: (1) Interview Practice and Self Reflection, (2) Study Skills in English at University Level, (3) Building a Bigger and Better Vocabulary, (4) Saying What You Mean - English Pronunciation for Cantonese and Mandarin Speakers, (5) Listening to Learn: Academic Listening and Note-taking Skills, and (6) Citation and Referencing Matters in Academic Writing. These workshops are now available for registration at: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in English
Consultation service is available during the following time:
31 August (Mon): 14:30 – 16:30
1 September (Tue): 10:30 – 12:30
2 September (Wed): 14:30 – 16:30
3 September (Thu): 10:30 – 12:30
4 September (Fri): 14:30 – 16:30
Online Booking:
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
More Timeslot please check our website：
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EH/consultation.aspx
====================================

Launch Day: Hong Kong Inter-University GenAI Hackathon for SDGs (Saturday, 19 September 2026)  - Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research
From: Andy WONG
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
andy.wong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Calling all CUHK students! Ready to use GenAI to make a real-world impact?
I highly encourage you to participate in the Hong Kong Inter-University GenAI Hackathon for SDGs 2026!
This month-long hackathon is an incredible opportunity to apply multimodal GenAI technologies towards the UN SDGs. You will get the chance to collaborate with peers across different universities, research pressing social issues, and prototype innovative, socially beneficial solutions.
Beyond coding, this hackathon is about building your 21st-century skills, expanding your network, and stepping into the world of social entrepreneurship and start-up incubation.
Kick-off / Launch Day Details:
Date: Saturday, 19 September 2026
Time: 9:30 am – 3:00 pm (HKT)
Venue: Lecture Hall II, Centennial Campus, HKU
Don't miss this chance to build tech for good!
Learn more:
https://www.hack4sdg.com/
Register now:

「中大文化徑」導賞員計劃

藝術行政主任辦公室現正招募學生助理為導賞員，負責帶領約150分鐘的「中大文化徑」導賞團，遊走中大校園，了解藝術及建築特色、校園歷史及相關的文化內容。
工作範疇

帶領「中大文化徑」導賞團；
向參加者介紹中大校園及文化景點；
回答參加者的提問；及
處理主管指定的任何臨時職責。
時薪

每小時77港幣（一次導賞團計最少4小時）
備註

經初步甄選後，初步入選申請者會收到通知參與簡介會及實習；
​獲選之報名者必須完成上述簡介會及實習，方能正式成為「中大文化徑」導賞員。
截止日期

2026年9月17日 (星期四) 12:00pm
報名及更多資訊

https://www.srrsh.cuhk.edu.hk/zh/node/546/
‘CUHK Culture Trail' Docent Programme

The Office of the Arts Administrator is recruiting student helpers as docents to lead 150-minute guided tours of the ‘CUHK Culture Trail’, and share information about the arts and architectural characteristics of the CUHK, as well as the culture and stories behind the campus.
Job Responsibilities

To lead ‘CUHK Culture Trail’ Guided Tours;
To introduce CUHK campus and cultural spots to participants;
To answer questions raised by participants during the tour; and
To handle any ad hoc duties as assigned by the supervisor.
Salary

HKD77/ hour (at least 4 hours for a tour)
Remarks

After initial screening, shortlisted applicants will be invited for introduction session and assessment;
Selected applicants must complete the introduction session and assessment to be formally admitted as a 'CUHK Culture Trail' docents.
Application deadline

17 September 2026 (Thursday) 12:00pm
Application and for more information

https://www.srrsh.cuhk.edu.hk/en/node/546/

⭐⭐⭐Parent and Child Participants Needed (Twins and Singletons)!! Maximum $550 allowance and a performance report! 誠邀家長和小朋友(包括單生兒和雙胞胎)參與研究！！最高可獲得共$550報酬和個人報告！！⭐⭐⭐  - Department of Psychology
From: Queenie Chow
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
literacy@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
誠邀閣下與子女參與一項關於華語兒童中英數能力的跨學科大型研究，詳情如下：
對象：
幼稚園高班至六年級單生兒和雙胞胎學生（包括同卵雙生和異卵雙生）
學童家長
學童需以廣東話為母語，並在香港居住 2.5 年以上
目的：
建立學童在中、英文讀寫和數學能力發展的多模態模型，以及設計能夠全面反映兒童在這三方面表現的網上測試工具
研究內容：
第一部分
學童：中英文和數學能力的測試
，分成網上測試和面對面測試兩部分。網上測試分為六個區域，各需時約40分鐘。網上測試毋須一次完成，參加者可自行安排時間分段執行，在四星期內完成所有項目即可。
面對面測試在網上測試完成後另約時間進行，約需45分鐘
家長：
在網上測試平台接受
約
15
分鐘的語文及數學測試
，及填寫關於學童學習情況與家庭語言環境的
問卷
*
現在報名的幼稚園高班至六年級學童只需完成今年一次測試
第二部分（可選擇是否參與）
學童：腦電圖測試（EEG），約2小時
報酬：每年測試完結後將收到：
(1) 測試結果的個人報告；(2) 港幣200元超級市場現金券；(3) 小禮物，
參與腦電圖 (EEG) 部份的學生另有250元超級市場現金券
研究詳情及報名請見以下網頁：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4OWk4Rmnmb0M20e
如對是項研究有任何疑問或查詢，歡迎聯絡本項目的首席研究員Urs Maurer教授（電郵: umaurer@cuhk.edu.hk）或研究小組（電話：3943-4379；電郵：
lifespandevlab.cuhk@gmail.com
）。

Calling all CUHK undergrads and postgrads! The Hong Kong Inter-University Generative AI Hackathon for SDGs 2026 is back for its 4th year. Whether you are a coding pro or completely non-technical, this is your chance to team up across Hong Kong universities and tackle real urban challenges—from Smart Mobility to Sustainable Northern Metropolis—and pitch for exciting prizes.
Launch Day Event
Date: 19 September 2026 (Sat)
Venue: Lecture Hall II, HKU Centennial Campus
You will be
Pitching ideas
Forming teams
Getting to know mentors and team members
Allocating tasks
Registration deadline: 14:00, 14 September 2026 (Mon)
Check out the timeline and rules:
https://www.hack4sdg.com/
Register:
https://www.hack4sdg.com/2025-event/registration/
第四屆香港大專院校聯校「GenAI Hackathon for SDGs」開始接受報名，歡迎所有 CUHK 本科生及研究生參與
不論你來自甚麼學術背景，是否具備技術知識，均可與全港八大同儕跨校組隊，利用生成式人工智能（generative AI）就綠色交通及可持續北部都會區等議題構思解決方案，達致聯合國可持續發展目標，為社會未來謀福祉。
啟動日
日期：2026年9月19日（六）
地點：香港大學百周年校園 Lecture Hall II

分享構思

Lecture Series in Honour of Professor Jao Tsung-i: Reflection and Truth in Jao’s Scholarship
Professor Jao Tsung-i (1917–2018), renowned for his profound erudition in both the artistic and humanistic spheres East and West, had pioneered numerous research innovations. To commemorate the 110th anniversary of his birth, the “Lecture Series in Honour of Professor Jao Tsung-i” is co-organized by the Institute of Chinese Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), Jao Tsung-I Petite Ecole at the University of Hong Kong (HKU), Jao Tsung-I Academy of Sinology at Hong Kong Baptist University, Fung Ping Shan Library at HKU, and Hok Hoi Library. The three upcoming lectures, themed “Reflection and Truth in Jao’s Scholarship” and hosted by the Institute of Chinese Studies, will be held at CUHK on 12 September, 19 September, and 3 October.

Events / Activities
Water Sports Training Course (Sep to Oct) - CUHK Water Sports Centre 水上活動訓練課程 (九至十月) - 中大水上活動中心 - Water Sports Centre / P E Unit
From: Kent Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
kentwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
(The English version follows the Chinese one)
============ 中大水上活動中心通訊 =============
***** 訓練課程 *****
(更多資料: http://www.facebook.com/WSC.CUHK)
獨木舟訓練班 (一天課程)
* 一星 (一天) : 9月26日 (六) (K11)、9月27日 (日) (K12)
** 二星 (一天) : 10月3日 (六) (K13)
*** 三星 (一天) : 10月4日 (日) (K14)
初級滑浪風帆訓練班 (兩天課程) (適合初學人仕參與)
* 9月19 (六)及20 (日) (W7)
* 9月26 (六)及27 (日) (W8)
風帆入門訓練班 (第一級) (兩天課程)
* 10月31 (六)及11月1 (日) (S6)
# 為提供更完善的服務給您、中大不同部門及其他學會對水上活動的需要，本中心現特設 "度身訂造" 服務，馬上致電2603 6776聯絡我們吧!
***** 報名方式 *****
(更多資料: https://tinyurl.com/kxp3dwm2 or http://www.facebook.com/WSC.CUHK)
網上報名日期：
Class K11、K12、W7及W8 - 由2026年8月28日 (星期五) 下午5:30至9月1日 (星期二) 下午3:00，先到先得，額滿即止。
Class K13及 K14 - 由2026年9月4日 (星期五) 下午5:30至9月8日 (星期二) 下午3:00，先到先得，額滿即止。
Class S6 - 由2026年9月18日 (星期五) 下午5:30至9月22日 (星期二) 下午3:00，先到先得，額滿即止。
網上報名網址：
https://webapp.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/ras/restricted/eventlist?id=73
# 查詢請致電2603 6776 (水上活動中心辦事處)。
***** 人數上限 *****
(更多資料: http://www.facebook.com/WSC.CUHK)
+ 獨木舟訓練班：上限8人
+ 滑浪風帆訓練班：上限5人
+ 風帆訓練班：上限6人
***** 收費 *****
(更多資料: http://www.facebook.com/WSC.CUHK)
+ 獨木舟訓練班：
** 初級課程 - 學生$210，職員 (及家屬) $270
+ 滑浪風帆訓練班：
** 初級課程 - 學生$630，職員 (及家屬) $700
+ 風帆入門訓練班：
** 第一級 - 學生$680，職員 (及家屬) $740
體育部將津貼獨木舟訓練班($90)，滑浪風帆及風帆訓練班($200)予全期出席之學生，退款將於課程後即時退回。
注意：
參加者須能穿著衣服及救生衣游泳50米。課程首日可能會安排游泳測試。
水上活動對體能有一定要求，參加者應確保身體狀況適合參與相關活動。
課程將以廣東話授課，並輔以英語說明。
報讀獨木舟二星證書課程或以上級別的參加者，必須於報名時出示相關資歷證明。未能提供有效證書者，本中心有權拒絕其報名申請。
參加者必須年滿14歲。18歲以下人士須取得家長、監護人或授權人士同意；16歲以下人士須由家長、監護人或授權人士陪同參與活動。陪同人士必須年滿 18歲。
課程費用僅包括教練費及器材使用費。成功完成課程並通過考核者，可申請相關證書。證書費用需另行支付：獨木舟$45、滑浪風帆$30及帆船$55 / $115
報名一經確認後，恕不接受退款、更改課程或更換參加者（包括因疾病而未能出席的情況）。惟因惡劣天氣、報名人數不足或本中心取消課程而導致的情況除外。
參加者須於課程當日自行前往水上活動中心集合。請自備泳衣、長袖上衣、適合下水使用且包趾包跟的運動鞋，以及午餐。
如報名人數不足，本中心保留取消課程的權利。受影響的參加者將獲個別電郵通知。
體育部將為出席率達 100% 的學生提供培訓津貼：獨木舟訓練($90)，滑浪風帆及帆船訓練($200)，津貼將於課程完成後發還。缺席或中途退出課程者將不獲發放津貼。
如有任何查詢，請聯絡：水上活動中心2603 6776 / 體育部：3943 6097
******* News for the Water Sports Training Course *******
Kayaking Training Course (1-day course):
* One Star: 26 Sep (Sat) (K11), 27 Sep (Sun) (K12)
** Two Star: 3 Oct (Sat) (K13)
*** Three Star: 4 Oct (Sun) (K14)
Basic Windsurfing Training Course (2-day course) (It also fit for Improver):
* 19-20 Sep (Sat & Sun) (W7)
* 26-27 Sep (Sat & Sun) (W8)
Introduction to Sailing Training Course (Level 1) (2-day course)
* 31 Oct to 1 Nov (Sat & Sun) (S6)
- The Centre offers a tailored package for all CUHK members (services include a fun day, a certificate course, and a special event); for more information, please call 2603 6776 (CUWSC Office).
******* Enrollment *******
Online enrollment will be accepted on a first-come, first-served basis until the course reaches its maximum capacity.
Class K11, K12, W7 & W8 - 5:30 pm on 28 Aug to 3:00 pm on 1 Sep 2026
Class K13 & K14 - 5:30 pm on 4 Sep to 3:00 pm on 8 Sep 2026
Class S6 - 5:30 pm on 18 Sep to 3:00 pm on 22 Sep 2026
Direct register link for user:
https://webapp.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/ras/restricted/eventlist?id=73
******* Max capacity *******
+ Kayaking Training Course: Max. 8 persons
+ Windsurfing Training Course: Max. 5 persons
+ Sailing Training Course: Max. 6 persons
******* Course fee *******
+ Kayaking Training Course:
- Student ($210), Staff & Family member ($270)
+ Windsurfing Training Course:
- Student ($630), Staff & Family member ($700)
+ Introduction to Sailing Training Course (Level 1):
- Student ($680), Staff & Family member ($740)
Physical Education Unit will subsidize STUDENT with 100% attendance in Kayaking Training Course ($90) and Windsurfing / Sailing Training Course ($200). Subsidize will be refunded after the course except for abstention.
******** Contact us **********
Further information will be posted to Water Sports Centre Website (https://tinyurl.com/kxp3dwm2 or http://www.facebook.com/WSC.CUHK), University Sports Centre notice board. We are welcome any inquiry kentwong@cuhk.edu.hk (email) & 2603 6776(OFFICE)
Remarks:
Participants should be able to swim 50 metres while wearing clothing and a life jacket. A swimming assessment may be conducted on the first day of the course.
Please note that water sports require a reasonable level of physical fitness. Participants should ensure they are physically fit to join the activity.
The course will be conducted primarily in Cantonese with supplementary instruction in English where necessary.
No refunds, program changes or participant substitutions will be permitted after enrollment, including cases of illness. Exceptions will only be made in the event of adverse weather conditions, insufficient enrollment or course cancellation by the Centre
.
Participants enrolling in the Kayak 2 Star Award course or above must present the relevant qualification certificate upon registration. Failure to provide valid certification may result in the Centre declining the enrollment.
Participants must be aged 14 or above. Those under 18 years of age must obtain consent from a parent, guardian or authorized person. Participants under 16 years of age must be accompanied by a parent, guardian or authorized person throughout the activity. The accompanying parent, guardian or authorized person must be at least 18 years old.
The course fee covers instructor fees and equipment use only. Participants who successfully complete and pass the course assessment will be eligible to apply for a certificate. Certificate fees are charged separately: Kayaking $45, Windsurfing $30 and Sailing $55 / $115.
Participants should report directly to the Water Sports Centre on the course day. Please bring your own swimsuit, long-sleeved shirt, enclosed sports shoes suitable for water activities (covering both toes and heels) and lunch.
The course may be cancelled if the minimum enrollment requirement is not met. Affected participants will be notified individually by email.
The Physical Education Unit will provide a training subsidy for students who achieve 100% attendance: Kayaking Training $90 and Windsurfing / Sailing $200. The subsidy will be reimbursed after course completion. Participants who withdraw or are absent from the course will not be eligible for the subsidy.
For enquiries, please contact Water Sports Centre 2603-6776 or Physical Education Unit 3943-6097.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

.
Participants enrolling in the Kayak 2 Star Award course or above must present the relevant qualification certificate upon registration. Failure to provide valid certification may result in the Centre declining the enrollment.
Participants must be aged 14 or above. Those under 18 years of age must obtain consent from a parent, guardian or authorized person. Participants under 16 years of age must be accompanied by a parent, guardian or authorized person throughout the activity. The accompanying parent, guardian or authorized person must be at least 18 years old.
The course fee covers instructor fees and equipment use only. Participants who successfully complete and pass the course assessment will be eligible to apply for a certificate. Certificate fees are charged separately: Kayaking $45, Windsurfing $30 and Sailing $55 / $115.
Participants should report directly to the Water Sports Centre on the course day. Please bring your own swimsuit, long-sleeved shirt, enclosed sports shoes suitable for water activities (covering both toes and heels) and lunch.
The course may be cancelled if the minimum enrollment requirement is not met. Affected participants will be notified individually by email.
The Physical Education Unit will provide a training subsidy for students who achieve 100% attendance: Kayaking Training $90 and Windsurfing / Sailing $200. The subsidy will be reimbursed after course completion. Participants who withdraw or are absent from the course will not be eligible for the subsidy.
For enquiries, please contact Water Sports Centre 2603-6776 or Physical Education Unit 3943-6097.

Announcements
[Research Invitation] Speech Intervention Study for Cantonese-speaking Children and Adolescents with Cleft Palate 【研究邀請】招募參與「唇顎裂兒童及青少年語音介入」之學術研究 - Department of Otorhinolarynogology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: Rina To
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rinato@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
各位香港中文大學成員：
我們誠邀閣下及其子女參與由香港中文大學耳鼻喉科、頭頸外科進行的學術研究 。
研究題目：
「探索針對唇顎裂兒童及青少年的語音介入框架：隨機對照試驗」
研究目的：
患有唇顎裂的兒童有較高風險出現語音/發音困難，這可能嚴重影響其說話清晰度。本研究旨在比較兩種不同的實證語音介入框架（線性與非線性語音介入）在改善這些語音錯誤方面的成效。
招募對象：
說廣東話的兒童及青少年 (4歲 – 17歲)；
4 至 17 歲，母語為廣東話嘅兒童及青少年。
患有唇顎裂，並有發音/語音問題。
於 24 個月大前已完成唇顎裂之修復手術；
無已知認知障礙，或任何會影響其獨立參與語音任務能力的醫療狀況。
研究程序：
全面評估：
參與者將經歷全面的語音評估程序，包括多項標準化語音測試及填寫問卷。
個別治療：
參與者將接受由專業言語治療師設計的語音治療方案。請注意，候補名單對照組的參與者將在主要研究觀察階段結束後接受治療。
錄影記錄：
參與者的語音將被錄影，以作進一步記錄和分析。所有語音數據及錄音將受密碼保護並嚴格保密 。
費用與報酬：
潛在益處：
參與者能透過治療方案提升整體說話清晰度，並為唇顎裂語音的臨床護理程序及機制提供貢獻。
參與費用：
參與本研究無需支付任何額外費用。
聯絡方式：
如有興趣參與或有任何疑問，請致電
3943 9609
聯絡首席研究員
何皓賢先生
。
感謝閣下對本研究計劃的興趣與支持。亦可以使用以下連結報名:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13736537
此研究項目已獲香港中文大學 – 新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會（Joint CUHK-NTEC-CREC）批准。
Dear Members of the CUHK Community,
We are cordially inviting children and adolescents with Cleft Palate ± Lip to participate in a research study conducted by the Division of Speech Therapy (Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Study Title:
Exploring Speech Intervention Frameworks for Cantonese-speaking Children and Adolescents with Cleft Palate +/- Lip: A Randomized-Controlled Trial.
Children born with Cleft Palate ±Lip (CP±L) are at high risk for speech difficulties, such as glottal stops or backing errors, which can significantly impact how well they produce speech sounds and are understood. This study investigates the effectiveness of two different evidence-based speech intervention frameworks (Linear vs. Non-linear phonological intervention) in improving these speech outcomes.
Who Can Participate?
Cantonese-speaking children and adolescents (aged 4 to 17) with CP±L
Individuals exhibiting cleft speech errors that require intervention;
Primary repair of the palate done prior to 24 months old;
No known cognitive or hearing impairment, or other medical conditions that prevent independent participation in speech tasks.
What is Involved?
Comprehensive Assessment:
Participants will undergo standardized speech assessments and questionnaires.
Treatment:
Participants will receive speech therapy protocols designed by professional speech therapists. Please note that participants in the waitlist group will receive treatment after the primary study observation phase.
Recording:
Speech sessions will be video-recorded for data analysis and will remain strictly confidential.
Benefits and Costs:
Potential Benefits:
Improvement in overall speech clarity and contribution to the clinical management of cleft palate speech.
Costs:
There is no additional cost to participate.
Contact Information:
If you are interested or have questions, please contact Mr. Choco Ho (何皓賢), Speech Therapist and Principal Investigator, at 3943 9609 or click the link below:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13736537
This study has been approved by the Joint CUHK-NTEC-CREC.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

From: Institute of Environment, Energy and Sustainability
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
iees@cuhk.edu.hk

Climate Change Beyond 1.5°C: Do We Still Have Hope? | 8 September at CUHK
Dear Colleagues and students,
You are warmly invited to a special public lecture, Climate Change Beyond 1.5°C: Do We Still Have Hope? From the Latest IPCC Science to Climate Action in Cities, taking place at CUHK as part of Hong Kong Green Week 2026.
The lecture will be delivered by Professor Debra Roberts, former Co-Chair of Working Group II for the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report, Coordinating Lead Author of the forthcoming IPCC Special Report on Climate Change and Cities, and a core team member of UNEP’s Overshoot Spotlight Report.
Professor Roberts will discuss what the latest climate science tells us about climate overshoot, why adaptation and resilience are becoming increasingly urgent, and how cities can translate scientific knowledge into practical action.
The programme will feature:
Welcoming remarks by Ms Wong Shuk-han, Diane, Under Secretary for Environment and Ecology
Public lecture by Professor Debra Roberts
A Hong Kong academic response by Professor Amos P. K. Tai of CUHK
A fireside conversation moderated by Ms Kitty Tam of Civic Exchange
Audience Q&A and closing reflection
Event details
Date:
Tuesday, 8 September 2026
Time:
4:00–5:30 pm
Venue:
Lecture Theatre 1, Yasumoto International Academic Park, CUHK (LT1, YIA)
Registration:
https://www.eventbrite.com/e/climate-change-beyond-15c-do-we-still-have-hope-tickets-1997662504326
The event is open to the public. Colleagues, students, researchers, policymakers, practitioners and anyone interested in climate action are warmly encouraged to attend.
Jointly organised by CUHK’s Institute of Environment, Energy and Sustainability, the Museum of Climate Change and Civic Exchange, with sponsorship from The Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation Hong Kong.
Please feel free to circulate this invitation within your department and relevant networks.
Best regards,
Institute of Environment, Energy and Sustainability

bodyText:

Free Training・Certificate・Paid Internship! Join Us as a Project Ambassador at Yim Tin Tsai  第二屆【智遊自在鹽田梓】項目大使現正接受報名！生態文化導賞實習機會！ - Department of Geography and Resource Management
From: Cherry Lau
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cherrylau123@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【智遊自在鹽田梓】現正招募 第二屆項目大使！
Call for Project Ambassador to work in Yim Tin Tsai, Sai Kung!
熱愛大自然？或是對客家文化與天主教深感興趣？機會來了！
「智遊自在鹽田梓」現正招募第二屆項目大使，計劃費用全免，完成後可獲頒證書，一同參與生態保育與社區導賞工作。
成為項目大使，你可以在遠離煩囂的西貢鹽田梓島上工作，將生態知識、AR科技和社區導賞結合，親身參與鄉郊保育，更可優先報名參加項目活動！
工作體驗包括帶領生態文化導賞，以及協助活動進行
Love nature? Curious about Hakka culture and Catholicism? This is your opportunity!
"Exploring YTT Nature ARchive" is now recruiting for its second cohort (2026/2027) of Project Ambassadors. The programme is free to join, and you will receive free training and a certificate upon completion. Be part of our ecological conservation and community guiding efforts.
As a Project Ambassador, you will work on the Yim Tin Tsai island in Sai Kung, combining ecological knowledge, AR technology, and guided tours. You will also get priority access to project activities. Your role will include leading eco-cultural tours and supporting event operations.
參與資格 Eligibility
：
• 必須為香港中文大學在讀學生（本科生及碩士生均可）Current CUHK student (both undergraduate and postgraduate students are welcome)
• 對生態、客家文化、導賞或保育有興趣 Interest in ecology, Hakka culture, guided tours, or conservation
• 粵語流利，具英語能力更佳 Fluent in Cantonese (English proficiency is an advantage)
• 不怕坐船，熱愛戶外活動 Comfortable with outdoor activities
計劃日程 Programme Schedule
：
• 面試 Interview：Late September to early October 2026 (via Zoom)
• 網上理論課 Online Training：October - November 2026
• 實地考察 Field Visit：Early November 2026 (Yim Tin Tsai Island)
• 實地導賞考核 Tour Examination：November–December 2026 (Optional 如選擇參與導賞工作)
截止報名 Application Deadline: 20 September 2026 (Sunday) 23:59
報名表格 Join Us Now
：
https://forms.gle/wocifws9ndFh9tqV7
Enquiries: Cherry Lau (Project Manager)
cherrylau123@cuhk.edu.hk
══════════
關於我們 About the Project
本項目【智遊自在鹽田梓 Exploring YTT Nature ARchive】（全稱：「西貢鹽田梓生態保育應用研究：擴增模型與智能體驗式參與」）於2024年9月正式開始，為期三年，旨在運用擴增實境技術展示鹽田梓的生物多樣性，將智能科技融入島上自然保育與鄉郊復育工作。
"Exploring YTT Nature ARchive" is a three‑year project (2024–2027) that integrates Augmented Reality (AR) technology with nature conservation and rural revitalisation on Yim Tin Tsai Island. It aims to enhance public awareness and interest in the island's biodiversity through innovative technology and experiential learning.
資助單位 Funders: 鄉郊保育資助計劃、鄉郊保育辦公室 Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme (CCFS), Countryside Conservation Office (CCO)
主辦單位 Organiser: 香港中文大學地理與資源管理學系 Department of Geography and Resource Management
協辦/支持單位 Partners：香港科技大學綜合系統與設計學部、香港戶外生態教育協會、鹽田梓村委會、鹽光保育中心 HKUST Division of Integrative Systems and Design, Outdoor Wildlife Learning Hong Kong (OWLHK), Yim Tin Tsai Village Committee, Salt and Light Preservation Centre
Website:
http://www.yttnaturearchive.org
Facebook: 智遊自在鹽田梓 Exploring YTT Nature ARchive
Instagram: @yttnaturearchive

广东话学习小组
我中大普通话恩桥团契现正举办广东话学习小组！
我们是一群基督徒，希望关心来港读书的普通话同学。为帮助普通话来港生适应香港及中大生活，我们特为大家预备了一系列迎新活动（广东话小组）。
时段：9月18日、10月2日、10月9 日、10月16日、10月23日、10月30日、11月6日
时间：逢星期五晚上七点半至九点半
地点：香港中文大学
内容：地道香港同学与你一起学习广东话
人数：每组大约6位参加者与2位香港人作为广东话小组导师
费用：$50（第一堂收按金$200，出席6堂$150）
课程完结后13/11请参加者免费吃加油饭庆祝）

https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfL6bgK8ppf4zsrOj0_kVqSBJHctLVwvBDXFFQCbtZxo87PGQ/viewform
报名及其他详情：
截止报名日期：2026年9月15日23:59
* 名额有限，额满即止
查詢：
cuhkmbridge@gmail.com
================================================================
Cantonese Learning Group (September to November 2026)
The CUHK Mandarin Bridge Fellowship is currently organizing a Cantonese Learning Group.
We are a group of Christians who care deeply about Mandarin-speaking students in CUHK. We wish helping every Mandarin-speaking students in CUHK adapt to life in Hong Kong. Thats the reason we have specially organized a series of orientation activities (Cantonese Learning Groups) for you.
Details are as follows:
Dates: ：18/9、2/10、9/10、16/10、23/10、30/10、6/11
Time: Fridays, 7:30 PM to 9:30 PM
Location: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Content: Learn Cantonese together with local Hong Kong people
Group Size: Each group will consist of approximately 6 participants and 2 Hong Kong tutors for the Cantonese Learning Group, or 3-4 participants and 1 Hong Kong tutor.
Cost: $50 ($200 will be collected on the 1st lesson, attend 80% for a $150 deposit refund)

bodyText:

»

Announcements
【Earn HK$500 coupon】 Recruiting adults (aged 18-65) to participate in research on online therapy for insomnia 【可獲得 500元現金券】招募成年人 (18-65歲)參與失眠的數碼化治療研究 - Psychiatry
From: Charis
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你是否經常在床上輾轉難眠，夜醒或早醒？你並不孤單——許多人都面臨著同樣的問題。我們誠邀您參與研究，讓專業數碼化治療助你改善睡眠！
研究目的
本研究旨在評估市民對數碼化失眠認知行為治療聊天機器人的遵從性，以及其對改善睡眠問題的效果。
治療方式
· 由專業臨床心理學家及精神科醫生設計的電子化治療
· 完全免費
參與資格
· 18至65歲能說廣東話流利溝通（能流利閱讀並理解廣東話）的香港居民
· 在過去一個月內，每週至少三晚出現睡眠困擾
· 最近四周或以上無需長期服藥
參與研究，獲得獎勵！
完成所有治療及後續測試後，您可獲得高達500港幣。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4UPFh054GtJGXX0
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理聯絡。
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do you often toss and turn in bed, wake up frequently at night, or wake up too early? You are not alone—many people experience the same challenges. We invite you to participate in our study and explore professional digital treatment to improve your sleep!
Purpose of the Study
This research aims to evaluate the public’s adherence to a digital insomnia cognitive behavioural therapy chatbot and assess its effectiveness in improving sleep problems.
Treatment Method
· A professionally designed digital therapy created by clinical psychologists and psychiatrists
· Completely free of charge
Eligibility Criteria
· Hong Kong residents aged 18 to 65 who can speak in Cantonese fluently, read and understand Cantonese
· Experienced sleep disturbances at least 3 nights per week in the past month
· No need for long-term medication for the past four weeks or more.
Receive Rewards for Participating!
Upon completion of all treatment sessions and follow-up assessments, participants will receive up to HKD 500.
How to Join?
Click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact suitable participants to provide further details:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4UPFh054GtJGXX0
Contact Us
If you have any questions, please call 6115-0322 during office hours to speak with our research assistants.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

From: Miss Manuela Wong

manuelawong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
International screening of the independent media collective
AsiaVisions' Migrante (1987)
to commemorate the 40th anniversary of Bethune House
This is the first international public exhibition of the digitized, English-subtitled version of 'Migrante,' a landmark documentary by the independent media collective AsiaVisions about Filipino domestic workers in Hong Kong during the global 1980s. Commemorating the 40th anniversary of Bethune House, the event is a part of a worldwide Migrant Workers Film Festival in different cities.
The speakers will talk about the legacy of the film and its filmmakers, including the archival and digitization process behind the re-release and the present conditions of domestic workers.
Date: September 11, 2026, Friday
Time: 15:30
Venue: YIA LT2 (G/F), Yasumoto International Academic Park, CUHK
Registration:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13737535
Speakers:
Rosemarie Roque, Polytechnic University of the Philippines
Lydia Catedral, Hong Kong Polytechnic University
Dolores Balladares Pelaez, United Filipinos in Hong Kong
Moderator:
Elmo Gonzaga, The Chinese University of Hong Kong

bodyText:

Announcements
Brief Low-intensity Training for Eating Disorders and Self-Criticism 「饮食问题低强度心理治疗」诚邀普通话女性使用者 - Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory, Department of Psychology
From: Yanbin, XIE
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ybxie@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募参与者：饮食问题低强度心理治疗
香港中文大学临床心理科学实验室团队现正推行一项针对饮食失调问题人群的短期训练计划，诚邀符合资格的人士参与。
六周指导式自助练习，处理与情绪和自我的关系
探索自我批评的恶性循环
开启看待自我的新视角
香港中文大学校园内，全程免费
饮食失调问题很多时候并非只是一个关于食物、身材偏好或者意志力的问题，而关乎我们如何看待自己，以及如何处理和他人的关系。目前，针对饮食失调的治疗多采用认知行为取向，研究证实能有效控制非适应性饮食失调行为的出现。本计划是团队基于实证研究开发的新训练方案，采用社会情绪取向，聚焦于处理自己与他人的关系。本项目遵循阶梯式照护模式，定位为指导式自助短期介入方案，旨在以较少的时间投入及心理负担为参加者提供支援。
训练为期6周，包括「每周1次实体会面 + 自助练习 + 线上心理评估访谈及问卷」；训练完成后1个月及6个月进行跟进评估。
「招募要求」
年满18岁或以上；女性；普通话流利（训练将主要使用普通话）；
受饮食失调问题困扰，例如，对饮食失调、体重或体型有过度的关注，饮食失调后感到强烈自责或羞愧，反复出现无法控制的暴食行为，或伴有反复出现的代偿行为（催吐、使用泻药或利尿剂、过度运动等）并因此影响日常生活或情绪；
目前并未接受其他形式的心理治疗或精神科药物治疗；
能够亲身前往香港中文大学校园参与训练。
「报名链接」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0pJvKNUXXEGYx4G
报名后，我们将联络您安排筛选问卷及访谈，以确认是否适合参加本计划，并邀请符合条件者参与训练。
如有疑问请联络研究团队：epplab.ed@cuhk.edu.hk。
所有个人资料仅用作研究用途，并会严格保密。
临床心理科学实验室团队
Recruiting Participants: Brief Training Programme for Eating Disorders
The Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory at CUHK is currently running a brief training programme for individuals struggling with eating disorders. We are now inviting eligible participants to join.
We all care about how we look. But eating disorders are often about much more than food, body shape, or willpower—they are deeply tied to how we see ourselves and how we relate to others. While cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT) is the most widely used and evidence-based treatment for eating disorders, our team has developed a new training protocol grounded in recent research, drawing on a socioemotional framework that focuses specifically on self-perception and interpersonal relationships. Following a stepped-care model, this programme is designed as a brief guided self-help intervention, offering meaningful support with a relatively low time commitment and psychological load.
  The programme runs for 6 weeks:
Weekly in-person sessions on campus
Guided self-help practice tasks to complete between sessions
Online assessment interviews and questionnaires
Follow-up evaluations will be conducted at 1 month and 6 months post-training.

Who We're Looking For
Female aged 18 or above;
Are fluent in Mandarin;
Are currently struggling with eating disorder symptoms, for example, excessive evaluation or concerns on food, weight, or body shape, intense guilt or shame after eating, recurrent episodes of binge eating that feel out of control, with compensatory behaviours such as self-induced vomiting, laxative or diuretic misuse, or excessive exercise;
Are not currently receiving any other form of psychological therapy or psychiatric medication;
Are able to attend in-person sessions on the CUHK campus

Sign Up Here
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0pJvKNUXXEGYx4G
After you sign up, we will contact you to complete a screening questionnaire and a brief interview to see if this programme is a good fit for you. If eligible, you will be invited to join the 6-week training.
 For any questions, feel free to reach out to us at:
epplab.ed@cuhk.edu.hk
All information you provide will be kept strictly confidential and used solely for research screening and intervention purposes.
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory

創意（30分）：視乎參賽者對主題的詮釋是否獨特及新穎。

Are you ready to strengthen your research data management skills? This is your opportunity to gain practical knowledge and hands-on experience that will help you manage research data more effectively and enhance the impact of your research.

CUHK Library
invites you to join our
Research Data Management Workshop Series
this term. Designed for researchers at all career stages, these sessions will equip you with essential skills, best practices, and tools for managing, sharing, and preserving research data throughout the research lifecycle.

Fri, 9 Oct, 2:30–4:00 pm
Understanding Research Data Management

Writing Data Management Plans with DMP Tool

Effective Use of The CUHK Research Data Repository

(Earn $200!! Recruiting teenagers (aged 18 to 24) to participate in depressive disorder study (welcome healthy people) (獲得 $200!!)誠邀18-24歲青少年參加與抑鬱症狀相關的研究(歡迎健康人士) - Department of Psychiatry
From: Phoebe Chan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，主要探討運用語音分析檢測青少年的憂鬱症狀。現招募年齡介乎18歲至24歲的青少年參與研究，歡迎所有健康人士、抑鬱和焦慮人士參加。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
18歲至24歲青少年,
除了抑鬱和焦慮外，沒有確診其他精神障礙
能說流利的廣東話
使用智慧型手機（附錄音機）並可持續存取互聯網
接受本研究所使用的即時通訊應用程式的服務條款和隱私權政策
您需要做什麼？
通過篩查訪談後，在手機
連續 7 天
使用指定的訊息應用程式
使用手機上的錄音功能進行數位語音錄音，包括（a）指定的段落閱讀和（b）引導音訊日記。
每天
早上
和
晚上
，在應用程式分別回答4個指導性問題
進行跟進訪談
完成實驗及跟進評估後，可以獲得$200現金津貼。
有興趣的參加者請按以下連結填寫問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_801s3xAKvKm1Uma
研究員將通過WhatsApp聯絡合適的參加者，並詳細解釋研究內容。
閣下留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp:(+852- 53202853)。

Announcements
A New Area A University General Education Course – “Understanding Modern China” (UGEA1555) 大學通識教育四範圍新科目：認識現代中國 （UGEA1555） - Office of University General Education
From: Office of University General Education
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ugcp@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Are you interested in gaining a deeper understanding of China’s remarkable transformation over the past century and its impact on today’s world?
The Office of University General Education is pleased to introduce UGEA1555 “Understanding Modern China,” a new 3-unit General Education course (Area A: Chinese Cultural Heritage) to be offered on a pilot basis in 2026-27.
Starting from the 2027-28 academic year, “Understanding Modern China” (UGCP1000) will replace “Understanding China” (UGCP1001) as a University Core requirement for all undergraduate students. As part of the University’s preparation for this transition, UGEA1555 will be offered as a pilot course, providing students with an opportunity to explore this important subject and enjoy special flexibility in meeting graduation requirements.
Why Take UGEA1555?
“Farewell to slogans. Read, discuss, and understand modern China as it is.”
The course introduces important ideas, events and agents that have shaped the historical process of modernization in China, with a view to providing a conceptual framework for a systematic and structured understanding of modern China.
Topics
Understanding the transition from imperial to modern China: the historical perspective
Economic transformation in modern China
Social change and cultural transformation in modern China
Chinese modernization: visions for the future
Special Pilot Arrangement
Students who complete UGEA1555 with a grade of D or above may choose to use the course to fulfil either:
Three units of the Area A General Education requirement, or
Both the UGCP1001 (1-unit) requirement and two units of the Area A General Education requirement
This special arrangement offers you greater flexibility in planning your studies.

To enrol in UGEA1555 Understanding Modern China, students must satisfy one of the following enrolment requirements:
Have completed UGFH1000 In Dialogue with Humanity or UGFN1000 In Dialogue with Nature and obtained at least a passing grade; or
Enrol in UGEA1555 concurrently with UGFH1000 In Dialogue with Humanity or UGFN1000 In Dialogue with Nature in either Term 1 or Term 2.
For more information about the course, please visit the following website:
https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/tc/learning/4-areas-of-ge/new-courses/ugea1555understanding-modern-china/
If you have any questions, please feel free to contact the General Education China Programme of the Office of University General Education at 3943 1902 or write to ugcp@cuhk.edu.hk.
Office of University General Education
你是否有興趣深入瞭解中國在過去一個世紀中的蛻變，及其對當今世界的影響？
自2027-28 學年起，「認識現代中國」（UGCP1000）將取代「認識中國」（UGCP1001），作為所有本科生必須修讀的大學核心課程。為全面推出該科目作相關準備，大學通識教育部於2026-27學年開設UGEA1555「認識現代中國」，作為大學通識教育四範圍的一門新的3學分的科目（範圍A︰中華文化傳承），進行試教，為同學提供探索現代中國的機會，並在滿足畢業要求方面享有特別的靈活性。
為何選修
UGEA1555
？
「用知識打破壁壘，以思考撥開迷霧。」
本科目介紹中國現代化歷史進程中的重要思想、事件和推動者，提供一個系統而有條理的概念性框架，以此理解現代中國。
涵蓋課題
理解中國從帝制到共和的轉變︰歷史背景
現代中國的經濟轉型
現代中國的社會變遷和文化轉型
中國式現代化︰朝向未來的願景
特別安排（只限
UGEA1555
）
修畢UGEA1555且成績達D級或以上的學生，可選擇以此科目滿足：
大學通識教育範圍A （3學分）的要求，或
UGCP1001（1學分）及大學通識教育範圍A（2學分）的要求 。

https://www.oge.cuhk.edu.hk/tc/learning/4-areas-of-ge/new-courses/ugea1555understanding-modern-china/
If you have any questions, please feel free to contact the General Education China Programme of the Office of University General Education at 3943 1902 or write to ugcp@cuhk.edu.hk.
Office of University General Education
你是否有興趣深入瞭解中國在過去一個世紀中的蛻變，及其對當今世界的影響？
自2027-28 學年起，「認識現代中國」（UGCP1000）將取代「認識中國」（UGCP1001），作為所有本科生必須修讀的大學核心課程。為全面推出該科目作相關準備，大學通識教育部於2026-27學年開設UGEA1555「認識現代中國」，作為大學通識教育四範圍的一門新的3學分的科目（範圍A︰中華文化傳承），進行試教，為同學提供探索現代中國的機會，並在滿足畢業要求方面享有特別的靈活性。
為何選修
UGEA1555
？
「用知識打破壁壘，以思考撥開迷霧。」
本科目介紹中國現代化歷史進程中的重要思想、事件和推動者，提供一個系統而有條理的概念性框架，以此理解現代中國。
涵蓋課題
理解中國從帝制到共和的轉變︰歷史背景
現代中國的經濟轉型
現代中國的社會變遷和文化轉型
中國式現代化︰朝向未來的願景
特別安排（只限
UGEA1555
）
修畢UGEA1555且成績達D級或以上的學生，可選擇以此科目滿足：
大學通識教育範圍A （3學分）的要求，或
UGCP1001（1學分）及大學通識教育範圍A（2學分）的要求 。

Announcements
[$500 coupon] Participant recruitment for an HKU intervention study 招攬40歲以上合資格人士參與健康指導及可穿戴裝置介入研究-可獲得[500超市禮券]  - Department of Sports Science and Physical Education
From: Hanwen Zhang
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ham.zhang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
參加者招募：健康指導及可穿戴裝置介入研究
香港大學（港大）Youngwon Kim教授正與香港中文大學（中大）楊懌健教授合作，招募中央肥胖的成年人士參與研究。本研究旨在探討可穿戴裝置功能及健康指導對活動行為與心臟代謝風險因素的影響。
參與研究包括甚麼？
前往實驗室三次。每次到訪包括約1小時的評估，例如收集人口統計資料、量度血壓、抽取血液樣本及填寫問卷。
在指定研究期間連續24小時佩戴研究級可穿戴裝置。
接受其中一種介入方案：僅使用Fitbit可穿戴裝置功能，或使用相同功能並在一年內接受至少22節健康指導課程。
在約20個月內完成整個研究方案。
參與研究可能帶來甚麼益處？
了解心臟代謝疾病，並提供建議的生活方式調整。
獲得有助了解個人健康及體適能狀況的報告，包括Fitbit數據及血脂分析。
完成整個研究方案後，可獲港幣500元超市禮券。
哪些人士可能符合參加資格？
如您符合以下全部條件，便可能具備參加資格：
東亞裔，年齡為40歲或以上。
腰圍達90厘米或以上（男性），或80厘米或以上（女性）。
現時的體能活動量未達世界衞生組織建議水平。
使用智能手機。
能以中文或英文溝通。
能夠進行一般日常生活活動。
現時並未參與其他改變生活方式的研究或運動計劃。
如何登記或查詢更多資料？
如您有興趣參加，請掃描下方的登記二維碼，或聯絡研究團隊。
掃描二維碼登記
電話／
WhatsApp
：
52447300
電郵：
pastudy@hku.hk
實驗室地址：
香港薄扶林沙宣道5號賽馬會跨學科研究大樓3樓305室運動生理學實驗室。
抽血注意事項：
抽血前須禁食8小時，即不可進食或飲用任何飲品，包括茶、咖啡及酒精；期間可以飲用清水。
如有查詢，請透過上述聯絡方法與Youngwon Kim教授及港大研究團隊聯絡。歡迎您將此招募資料轉發予可能符合參加資格的人士。
Participant Recruitment: Intervention Study on Health Coaching and Wearable Devices
Professor Youngwon Kim at The University of Hong Kong (HKU), in collaboration with Professor Yijian Yang at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), is recruiting adults with central obesity. The study will examine how wearable-device functions and health coaching affect movement behaviours and cardiometabolic risk factors.
What does participation involve?
Attend three laboratory visits. Each visit includes an approximately 1-hour assessment, such as collecting demographic information, measuring blood pressure, drawing blood, and administering questionnaires.
Wear a research-grade wearable device continuously for 24 hours during designated study periods.
Receive one of two interventions: Fitbit-based wearable functions alone, or the same wearable functions combined with at least 22 health-coaching sessions delivered over 1 year.
Complete the full study protocol over approximately 20 months.
What are the potential benefits?
Learn about cardiometabolic diseases and recommended lifestyle changes.
Receive reports that may help you understand your health and fitness status, including Fitbit data and a lipid profile.
Receive an HK$500 supermarket coupon after completing the full study protocol.
Who may be eligible?
You may be eligible if you meet all the following criteria:
Are East Asian and aged 40 years or above.
Have a waist circumference of at least 90 cm (men) or at least 80 cm (women).
Do not currently meet the World Health Organization-recommended levels of physical activity.
Use a smartphone.
Can communicate in Chinese or English.
Can perform usual activities of daily living.
Are not currently participating in another lifestyle-change research study or exercise programme.
How can I register or obtain more information?
If you are interested, please scan the registration QR code below or contact the research team.
Scan to register
Phone/WhatsApp:
52447300
E-mail:
pastudy@hku.hk
Laboratory address:
Exercise Physiology Lab (Room 305), 3/F, Jockey Club Building for Interdisciplinary Research, 5 Sassoon Road, Pokfulam, Hong Kong.
Important note for blood collection:
An 8-hour fast is required before the phlebotomy session. This means no food or drinks, including tea, coffee and alcohol. Water may be consumed freely.
For enquiries, please contact Professor Youngwon Kim and the HKU research team using the details above.You are welcome to share this invitation with people who may meet the eligibility criteria.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Announcements
[Recruiting Older Adult Caregivers] Effects of mindfulness-based intervention on the microbiome of older adult with chronic stress: A randomised controlled trial (Earn up to $300 supermarket vouchers ! )  【誠招年長照顧者】靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群成效研究 (完成最高獲$300現金券) - SPHPC
From: Donald Liu
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
donaldliu@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群成效研究: 隨機對照試驗
Effects of mindfulness-based training on the microbiome of older adults with chronic stress: A randomised controlled trial
現正誠邀合資格人士報名參加
We are now recruiting participants to join our programme.
賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院 現誠邀60歲以上人士參加一項靜觀課程研究
研究將會探討靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群的影響。
很多長者受慢性壓力困擾，如未能適當處理壓力，對他們的心理及生理皆有嚴重影響。研究發現慢性壓力會破壞腸道微生物群的平衡。靜觀證實可有效改善心理健康，卻甚少研究探究靜觀課程如何改善參與者的微生物群。這項研究將在社區招募138名年滿60歲人士，邀請他們參與為長者而設的靜觀課程與健康教育控制課程，比較兩者於改善壓力、負面情緒及腸道微生物的成效。
參加者將會被隨機分派入兩組其中一組：
a) 靜觀練習組：
分派入本組的參加者將接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的靜觀課程。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
b) 健康教育組：
分派入本組的參加者會接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的健康教育課程，課程內容包括營養，運動，維持生活習慣。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
招募對象:
i) 年齡60歲以上;
ii) 能聽講廣東話;
iii) 需要持續照顧有長期病患的親屬;
iv) 照顧者負荷指數達 7分或以上;
v)沒有經醫生診斷有精神病患或認知問題;
vi) 沒有嚴重的身體或精神問題;
vi)不是正接受心理治療;
vii) 兩年內沒有參加過正規的靜觀課程;
viii) 被照顧親屬並非剛離世;
ix) 三個月內沒有使用抗生素或益生菌
課堂詳情
時間：10月尾開始 星期三或四的 上午
地點：沙田瀝源健康院 - 本活動共8節, 每週1次, 每次1.5小時
兩組參加者均須在課程開始前、結束後，及結束後3個月填寫共次3問卷調查及提供3次糞便樣本。
*費用全免*
參與是次研究不需繳付任何費用。
每次提供樣本及填寫問卷將會獲得價值$100 的現金卷，最高可獲300元現金卷。
歡迎將以上資訊廣傳給親朋好友。
如需了解更多本研究資訊或查詢，請聯絡：
廖先生/魏先生 (研究助理)
電話：2252-8463  Whatsapp: 5264 6865
如有興趣參與研究，請使用以下連結報名。
報名：https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_8cu06nvBsZqwVBY

Calling all CUHK students Join COP31 as a Student Delegate through self-funded participation and gain first-hand insights into global climate action
Successful candidates will attend COP31 for at least four days, with guidance from Professor Amos Tai of the Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences and Professor Yuan Xu of the Department of Geography and Resource Management. Participants will have the chance to connect with global sustainability experts, gain exposure to international climate negotiations, and explore emerging solutions to climate challenges
COP31 dates: 9–20 November 2026
Location: Antalya, Türkiye
ℹ Details and Registration:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13736695
Registration Deadline: 18 September 2026
Should you have any questions, please contact the Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Office (
srsdo@cuhk.edu.hk
).
各位中大同學注意 歡迎報名成為 COP31中大學生代表，以自費形式參與會議，親身了解全球氣候議題
獲選的同學將有機會參與至少四天的會議，在地球與環境科學系戴沛權教授及地理與資源管理學系徐袁教授的指導下，與全球可持續發展專家交流，了解國際氣候談判，並探索應對氣候挑戰的方案

programme!
Training Session(s): to be arranged during the Sundays of Sept 2026 +/- Oct 2026

**Students should be able to participate in at least 16 days of research clinic (Sunday full day or occasionally Saturday half day/weekday night) during the membership period.
Major duties:
Conducting eye examinations
Operating eye investigation machines
Assisting doctor consultation
Delivering eye health education
Organizing outreach & screening activities
Come & help us if you are KEEN to...
Learn and operate different eye investigation/machines
Meet people with different backgrounds
Participate in outreach activities of our ongoing/future eye research projects

Conduct research

bodyText:

Announcements
Microsoft Copilot Chat Tips Rewrite Text for Any Tone  - ITSC
From: ITSC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
itsc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Ever wonder if your message sounds too formal? Too casual? Too blunt?
Copilot
can take
any text you paste
and instantly rewrite it in different tones. It’s like having a style consultant for your writing — just paste, pick your vibe, and go!
Try this prompt — copy & paste it!
"Rewrite the following message in 3 different tones: (1) formal and professional, (2) friendly and casual, (3) brief and direct. Here’s the original message: 'Hey team, just a reminder that the quarterly reports are due by end of day Friday. Please make sure your sections are completed and reviewed before submitting. Let me know if you need any help.'"
Why this works:
Asking for multiple versions in one go lets you compare and pick the best fit — or mix and match parts from each version. It’s faster than asking one at a time!

Bonus tip:
Great for when you’re unsure if your message sounds too harsh, too casual, or just right! Seeing side-by-side comparisons makes the choice easy.
More Tips & Resources
Looking for more ways to level up your Copilot game? Check out previous

for even more helpful guidance and best practices.

Invited Talk | The XJTLU Practice of Education + AI (Wednesday, 2 September 2026)  - Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research
From: Wikie Chan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
wik.chan@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
How do universities move from AI as a strategic aspiration to a tangible, sustainable reality?
Join us for an insightful online talk, "From Strategy to Ecosystem: The XJTLU Practice of Education + AI".
We are thrilled to welcome Dr Xin BI from Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University (XJTLU), who will share how XJTLU is building an AI-driven educational ecosystem. Drawing on practices recognised by the IIOE Higher Education Digitalisation Pioneer Case Awards, the talk will explore three interconnected dimensions of AI integration:
Leadership: How university leadership aligns strategy, governance, and resource allocation to drive the AI vision.
Pedagogy: How faculty translate AI into classroom practice, supported by professional development to foster AI literacy and personalised learning.
Technology: How strategic intent is converted into working platforms, including the XIPU AI Agent and the Learning Mall ecosystem.
Whether you are an educator, institutional leader, or ed-tech enthusiast, this talk will offer practical, transferable insights into reshaping the educational paradigm.

title: Recruiting households for participation in a serology study on RSV epidemiology 誠邀住戶參與呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)血清流行病學研究
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/28
»
Announcements
Recruiting households for participation in a serology study on RSV epidemiology 誠邀住戶參與呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)血清流行病學研究 - S.H. Ho Research Centre for Infectious Diseases
From: Dr. CHAN Chin Pok, Tony
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ceidstudy@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學何善衡傳染病研究中心現正進行一項全港性研究，旨在透過血清學檢測分析呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)於本港人口流行及傳播的模式。
我們現邀請本地住戶參與此研究。參與住戶及其成員需符合以下條件：
單位中有多於一人居住 (非獨居)；
住戶內需有多於一半成員參與此研究
(例：2-3人住戶需至少2名成員參加；4-5人住戶需至少3名成員參加)；
沒有接種RSV疫苗 或 參與相關臨床試驗研究；
現時沒有懷孕；及
於過去6個月通常居住於香港
研究內容:
參加者需於接下來的12個月合共抽血5次 ，並每月填答簡單問卷
未滿18歲參加者以「篤手指」方式進行
介乎2-5歲的參加者則無需抽血
本研究亦提供快速檢測包供參加者於出現呼吸道病徵時進行檢測 (費用全免)
地點:
沙田威爾斯親王醫院研究中心 (抽血/篤手指)
位於佐敦的私人診所 (抽血)
年滿6歲的參加者於完成所有抽血及問卷回合後可獲最多HK$250超市禮券。2-5歲的參加者則可於完成所有問卷回合後獲贈高達$100便利店禮券。名額有限，先到先得。如住戶有興趣參與研究，請登入
https://tinyurl.com/cuhkceid-rsv
填答網上表格。如符合參與資格，研究人員將會與你聯絡。
如有疑問，請於辦公時間致電2252-8862，WhatsApp 9244-8827 或傳送電郵至ceidstudy@cuhk.edu.hk 。
多謝支持！
S.H. Ho Research Centre for Infectious Diseases, The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a territory-wide serology study to analyse the population burden and epidemiology of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
All local households are invited to join the study. Participating households and members should fulfil the conditions below:
Not living alone;
More than half of the members in the household should participate in this study
(e.g. at least 2 participants for 2-3 persons-households; at least 3 participants for 4-5 persons-households);
No history of RSV vaccination nor participation in related clinical trials;
Not being pregnant; and
Normally residing in Hong Kong in the past 6 months
About the study:
Participants aged 6 years or above are asked to provide blood samples for totally 5 rounds and complete monthly surveys in the ensuing 12 months
Blood samples would be collected by “finger-prick” for those aged below 18 years
Participants aged 2-5 years are exempted from blood sampling
This study also offers rapid tests for self-testing by participants whenever presenting with respiratory symptoms (free of charge)
Venue:
Research clinic in the Prince of Wales Hospital (blood-taking / finger-prick)
Private clinic in Jordan (blood-taking only)
Participants aged 6 years or above would be offered up to HK$250 supermarket voucher after a total of 5 rounds of blood-taking. Participants aged 2-5 years would be offered up to HK$100 convenience store voucher after a total of 5 survey rounds. Limited quotas - first come first served! Interested households please log in to
https://tinyurl.com/cuhkceid-rsv
and fill in the online form. If you are eligible for the study, research staff will be in contact with you shortly.
Should you have any enquiries, please contact us at 2252-8862, via WhatsApp 9244-8827, or by email (
ceidstudy@cuhk.edu.hk
) during office hours.
Thank you for your support.

For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

Announcements
Recruiting Young Adults (18-29 years old) in Hong Kong for Participating a Bereavement Survey Study (receive up to HKD300 supermarket coupon upon completion!!) 誠邀18至29歲香港年輕成人參加問卷研究— 「關於年輕成人經歷親友/重要的人離世的哀傷」 (完成研究最多可獲價值港幣$300元正超市禮券) - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Ling Haofeng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
haofengling@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
誠邀18至29歲香港年輕成人參加問卷研究— 「關於年輕成人經歷親友/重要的人離世的哀傷」 (完成研究最多可獲價值港幣$300元正超市禮券)
參加者納入標準：
18
至
29
歲
在香港居住的本地年輕成人
在過去
18
個月內經歷過親友
/
重要的人離世
能閱懂中文和以廣東話溝通
研究程序：
1
）基線問卷
填妥同意書後，參加者將完成一份20分鐘基線問卷
問卷問題將與面對及經歷親友/重要的人離世時的哀傷過程及對死亡的觀念有關
完成基線問卷將會獲得
港幣一百元
正超市禮券作爲報酬
2
）第一輪跟進問卷
六個月後，我們會邀請參加者完成一份跟進問卷
完成第一輪跟進問卷的參加者將會獲得
港幣一百元
正超市禮券作爲報酬
3
）第二輪跟進問卷
在完成第一輪跟進問卷的六個月後，我們會邀請參加者再次完成一份跟進問卷
完成第二輪跟進問卷的參加者將會獲得
港幣一百元
正超市禮券作爲報酬
本研究均屬自願參與。研究資料會被保密，除研究人員外，任何人均不能獲取參與者所填寫的問卷資訊或錄音內容。本研究已通過香港中文大學–新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會(CREC-2025.748)及香港中文大學調查和行為研究倫理(SBRE‐24‐0378)審查。
參加方法:
請用以下連結填寫同意書及問卷，完成後可獲送贈港幣
一百元
正超市禮券
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4SbSwIIE6shc67I
歡迎將此招募信息推薦給身邊合資格的香港年輕成人。
如有查詢，請與博士後研究員凌皓峰博士聯絡。
電郵: haofengling@cuhk.edu.hk
WhatsApp：44643831 (凌皓峰博士)
We are now inviting Hong Kong young adults to participate in a bereavement survey, titled “Trajectories of grief outcomes and the associated psychosocial predictors among recently bereaved young adults in Hong Kong: A retrospective longitudinal mixed-methods approach”. Participants will receive up to HK$300 coupons upon completion.
Participant Inclusion Criteria:
Local young adults aged 18 to 29 residing in Hong Kong.
Have experienced the death of a close friend/relative or an important person within the past 18 months.
Able to read Chinese and communicate in Cantonese.
1) Baseline Questionnaire
- After signing the consent form, participants will complete a 20-minute baseline questionnaire.
- The questionnaire will include questions about grieving process in response to the death of a loved one or significant person, and attitudes toward death
- Participants will receive HK$100 coupons for completing the baseline questionnaire.
2) First Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months later, participants who have completed the baseline questionnaire will be invited to complete a follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the first follow-up questionnaire will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
3) Second Follow-up Questionnaire
- Six months after the first follow-up questionnaire, participants who have completed the first follow-up questionnaire will be invited to complete a second follow-up questionnaire.
- Participants who complete the second follow-up questionnaire after will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
Participation in this study is voluntary. The study data will be kept confidential and no one other than the researchers will have access to the questionnaire information or audio recordings completed by the participants. This study has been approved by The Joint CUHK-NTEC CREC (CREC-2025.748) and the Survey and Behavioral Research Ethics Committee of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (SBRE‐24‐0378).
Please use the following link to fill out the consent form and questionnaire. Upon completion, you will be rewarded with HK$100 coupons.
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4SbSwIIE6shc67I
You are welcome to recommend this recruitment information to qualified young adults in Hong Kong.
For enquiries, please contact Dr. Ling
E-mail: haofengling@cuhk.edu.hk
WhatsApp: 44643831

bodyText:

Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/28
»
Announcements
Latest Arrangements for School Bus Service (Effective from September 1, 2026) 校巴服務最新安排 (2026年9月1日起生效) - Transport Office
From: Transport Office
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
transport_office@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
2026年9月1日（星期二）起，校巴服務將作以下調整：
穿梭
校巴服務
1.
1A
線
將改為1線，開出時間為每小時逢10、25、40及55分，服務時間為上午7時40分至下午6時55分。
2.
1B
線
將會取消。
3. 新增
2S
線
，開出時間為每小時逢00及30分，服務時間為上午8時至下午6時30分。路線為
大學站廣場＞研究生宿舍一座＞大學體育中心＞邵逸夫堂＞馮景禧樓＞聯合書院（上行）＞新亞書院＞聯合書院（下行）＞大學行政樓＞善衡書院＞研究生宿舍一座＞大學站。
4.
2
線
將取消每小時逢00及30分班次，現有每小時逢15及45分班次則維持不變。
5.
8
線
將改由康本園開出，並停靠環迴東站（上行）及敬文書院（上行）站後，繼續按現有路線行車。康本園開出時間為每小時逢15、35及55分，服務時間為上午7時35分至下午6時35分。
6.
H
線
將取消停靠十苑站。
轉堂校巴服務
7.
7
線
開出時間將更改為每小時逢00及18分，服務時間為星期一至五上午8時18分至下午5時18分，星期六上午8時18分至下午1時18分
有關行車路線及時間表等資訊詳情，請瀏覽交通處網頁：
https://transport.cuhk.edu.hk/tc/
Starting from September 1, 2026 (Tuesday), there will be changes to the on-campus school bus service:
Shuttle School Bus Service
1.
Route 1A
will be renamed as Route 1.  The bus will depart at every 10, 25, 40 and 55 minutes each hour, with service hours from 7:40 a.m. to 6:55 p.m.
2.
Route 1B
will be cancelled.
3. A new
Route 2S
will be introduced.  The bus will depart at every 00 and 30 minutes each hour, with service hours from 8:00 a.m. to 6:30 p.m.  The routing is:
Station Piazza > Postgraduate Hall 1 > Univ. Sports Centre > Sir Run Run Shaw Hall > Fung King Hey Bldg. > United College (Upward) > New Asia College > United College (Downward) > Univ. Admin. Bldg. > S.H. Ho College > Postgraduate Hall 1 > Univ. Station
.
4. Departures of
Route 2
at every 00 and 30 minutes each hour will be cancelled, while the existing departures at every 15 and 45 minutes each hour will remain unchanged.
5.
Route 8
will start from Y.I.A.P., then stop at Campus Circuit East (Upward) and CW Chu College (Upward) before continuing along its existing route.  Departures from Y.I.A.P. will be at every 15, 35 and 55 minutes each hour, with service hours from 7:35 a.m. to 6:35 p.m.
6.
Route H
will no longer stop at Residence No. 10.
Meet-class School Bus Service
7. The departure times of
Route 7
will be changed to every 00 and 18 minutes each hour.  The service hours will be from 8:18 a.m. to 5:18 p.m. on Mondays to Fridays, and from 8:18 a.m. to 1:18 p.m. on Saturdays.
For details of the route map and timetable, please visit the Transport Office webpage:
https://transport.cuhk.edu.hk/
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

午間講座 - 慢性胃炎的中醫辨治與飲食宜忌
TCM Tips for Chronic Gastritis: How to Eat, Heal, and Protect Your Stomach
慢性胃炎屬中醫常見脾胃病範疇，胃脹胃痛令人困擾，甚至影響情緒。所謂「三分治、七分養」，講座分享如何識別脾胃問題、了解不同體質的飲食宜忌、示範簡易養胃穴位保健法，教大家以中醫方式應對這場保「胃」戰
Chronic gastritis is a super common pi-wei (spleen and stomach) issue in TCM. Dealing with a bloated or painful stomach is really frustrating and can easily ruin your mood. There is a famous saying in Chinese medicine: "Three parts treatment, seven parts nourishment." In this talk, you will learn how to spot pi-wei problems and find out what to eat (and what to avoid!) based on your unique body constitution. We will also show you some simple acupressure methods for stomach care to do at home. Come learn how to protect your stomach in TCM way!

TCM Tips for Chronic Gastritis: How to Eat, Heal, and Protect Your Stomach
慢性胃炎屬中醫常見脾胃病範疇，胃脹胃痛令人困擾，甚至影響情緒。所謂「三分治、七分養」，講座分享如何識別脾胃問題、了解不同體質的飲食宜忌、示範簡易養胃穴位保健法，教大家以中醫方式應對這場保「胃」戰
Chronic gastritis is a super common pi-wei (spleen and stomach) issue in TCM. Dealing with a bloated or painful stomach is really frustrating and can easily ruin your mood. There is a famous saying in Chinese medicine: "Three parts treatment, seven parts nourishment." In this talk, you will learn how to spot pi-wei problems and find out what to eat (and what to avoid!) based on your unique body constitution. We will also show you some simple acupressure methods for stomach care to do at home. Come learn how to protect your stomach in TCM way!

From: Reimagining Yung Shue Au
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
「重塑榕樹凹：共創山海村落」—
地方營造大使招募
中文大學建築學院現正推動一項以「鄉郊地方營造（Rural Placemaking）」為核心的鄉村學堂及暑期工作坊，誠邀熱愛香港鄉郊文化、樂於親身參與實作的你，一同走進榕樹凹，參與村落景觀的復育與共創行動。
計劃期間，我們將邀請香港建造學院團隊擔任導師，帶領參加者學習傳統建造工藝及鄉郊實踐技術。參加者可自選出席一天或多天工作坊。若完成九天的工作坊後，參加者將獲頒由中文大學建築學院及香港建造學院簽發之服務證書，以作嘉許。
榕樹凹介紹：
榕樹凹位於新界東北端，於三百多年前開基立村，是一條歷史悠久的客家溫姓村落，村落鼎盛時期曾有逾三百名居民。由於地理位置接近邊境，榕樹凹在1980年代曾設有英軍軍營，留下了一段獨特而鮮為人知的歷史印記。雖然村落現已無人居住，但村民近年積極推動復村工作，透過修復祖屋、整理村史、舉辦村宴及傳統儀式，如籌辦麒麟隊；重建社群連結與文化記憶，展現出對深厚的鄉土感情與文化傳承精神。
****************************************
願景
共創鄉郊地方營造：以低碳修復與地方記憶，重塑山海景觀。
空間實作：以小型建設改善路徑與休憩空間。
感官敘事：將歷史轉化為具體的景觀導覽。
​共創行動：透過行動連結設計思考與鄉村振興。
****************************************
活動地點： 新界沙頭角榕樹凹村
****************************************
工作坊形式及階段:
鄉村導賞：認識榕樹凹村落歷史，了解鄉郊地方營造與文化地景。
物資收集：在山海與村落之間收集可用材料。
景觀實踐*：進行場地清理及空間建設實作，由香港建造學院導師帶領鄉村學堂，教授鄉郊景觀實踐技藝與傳統建造方法。
（ *
代表當日將由建造學院導師帶領鄉村學堂及景觀實踐活動。）
9月
1日（二）、8日（二）、15日（二）、16日（三）*、17日（四）*、22日（二）
實際工作坊日期將視乎報名人數、天氣及工作人員情況作適當調整，包括增加或減少工作坊次數，屈時會通知相關參加者及在宣傳平台上公布。
- 參加者可因應自身時間安排，選擇參與單日或多日工作坊。
- 請參加者選擇所有可出席日期，以便主辦單位安排及分組。
- 導賞活動日期將稍後公布，會安排在平日和假日或工作坊期間舉行。
- 實際工作坊日期將視乎報名人數、天氣及現場情況作適當調整，並另行通知相關參加者。
- 如出席一節鄉村導賞、八節工作坊可獲中大建築學院及香港建造學院之義工服務證書。
*************************************
活動時間：早上 09:00 至 下午 04:00
名額：每節12人。
*************************************
對象：
* 身體狀況良好，能應付長時間戶外活動人士
* 對建築、景觀設計、保育等感興趣的人士
****************************************
報名連結：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733829
- 如出席一節鄉村導賞、八日工作坊可獲中大建築學院及香港建造學院之義工服務證書。
****************************************
計劃名稱：
「重塑榕樹凹故事：透過實驗式社區場地及自然文化徑共創鄉郊地方營造」
合辦機構：
中文大學建築學院
香港建造學院
榕樹凹村
資助：
環境及生態局環境科 鄉郊保育辦公室「鄉郊保育資助計劃」
****************************************
備註：
1. 榕樹凹屬禁區範圍，參加者需預先申請禁區許可證方可前往。
2. 在項目進行期間，所有與工作坊相關的船程費用將由計劃負責安排及資助。參加者需要自行安排陸路交通，並準備足夠食物（午餐）和飲用水。
3. 工作坊將以粵語進行。
4. 工作坊內容或會因天氣、路況、項目進度，以及參加者或工作人員身體狀況而作臨時調整，恕不另行通知，敬請留意。
5. 工作坊涉及一定體力勞動及長時間戶外活動。如參加者有身體不適、舊患或其他健康狀況，請預先通知主辦單位。
6. 村內沒有士多或補給設施，請預先準備足夠飲用水、午餐、乾糧、防曬及防蚊用品，並按個人需要攜帶雨具。
7. 工作坊地點蚊蟲較多，建議穿著淺色長袖衣物及長褲，並按需要攜帶蚊怕水。
8. 工作坊已包括基本第三者責任保險，參加者可按需要自行購買其他保險。
9. 鄉郊地區路面或有高低不平、濕滑、碎石情況，參加者須小心步行。
10. 如參加者未有遵守安全指引或工作人員安排，主辦單位有權終止其參與工作坊。
11. 活動期間我們可能會拍攝或／及錄影以作記錄、報告、宣傳及推廣用途。如你不欲被攝入鏡，請在活動開始前告知工作人員，以便我們作出適當安排。
12. 如有查詢，請電郵至
ysa-cuhk@cuhk.edu.hk
或致電 3943 6520 /3943 6518.

“Reimagining Yung Shue Au: Co-creating a Mountain-Sea Village”
— Recruitment for Rural-placemaking Ambassadors
Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story: Co-creating Rural Place
The School of Architecture at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently organising a rural school and summer workshop centred on the concept of
rural placemaking
. We invite individuals who are passionate about Hong Kong’s rural culture and interested in hands-on practice to join us in Yung Shue Au and participate in the revitalisation and co-creation of the village landscape.
During the programme, instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction will lead participants in learning traditional construction crafts and rural practical skills. Participants may choose to attend one or multiple workshop sessions according to their availability. Those who complete nine workshop days will receive a service certificate jointly issued by the School of Architecture, CUHK and the Hong Kong Institute of Construction in recognition of their participation and contribution.
Introduction to Yung Shue Au
Located in the northeastern New Territories, Yung Shue Au is a historic Hakka village established over 300 years ago by the Wan clan. At its peak, the village was home to more than 300 residents. Owing to its proximity to the border, a British military camp was stationed in the village during the 1980s, leaving behind a unique yet little-known historical legacy.
Although the village is currently uninhabited, villagers have actively promoted village revitalisation in recent years through repairing ancestral houses, documenting village history, organising village banquets and traditional rituals, as well as reviving the Qilin dance team. These efforts reflect a deep attachment to the village and a strong commitment to cultural inheritance and community reconnection.
Vision
Co-creating Rural Placemaking
Reimagining the mountain-sea landscape through low-carbon restoration and local memories.
Spatial Practice
Improving pathways and communal resting spaces through small-scale construction.
Sensory Narratives
Transforming local history into tangible landscape interpretation experiences.
Collective Action
Connecting design thinking with rural revitalisation through practical engagement.
Venue:
Yung Shue Au, Sha Tau Kok, New Territories
Programme Format and Phases
Village Guided Tour
Understanding the history of Yung Shue Au and learning about rural placemaking and cultural landscapes.
Material Collection
Collecting usable materials from the surrounding mountain, coastal, and village environment.
Landscape Practice
Participating in site clearing and spatial construction workshops led by instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction, focusing on rural landscape practices and traditional building techniques.
(* Stars indicate days when Hong Kong Institute of Construction instructors will lead the Landscape workshop.)
September
1 September (Tue), 8 September (Tue), 15 September (Tue), 16 September (Wed)*, 17 September (Thur)*, 22 September (Tue)
Please note that actual workshop dates are subject to adjustment based on enrollment numbers, weather conditions, and staff availability. This includes the potential to increase or decrease the number of sessions. Registered participants will be notified directly of any changes, and updates will be posted across our promotional platforms.
- Participants may choose to join single-day or multiple-day workshops according to their availability.
​- Participants are encouraged to select all available dates to facilitate scheduling and grouping arrangements.
- Indicates dates on which the landscape practice workshops will be led by instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction.
- Dates for the guided tours will be announced later and will be arranged on both weekdays and weekends.
- Actual workshop dates may be adjusted according to registration numbers, weather conditions, and site situations. Relevant participants will be notified separately.
Workshop Time
09:00 am – 04:00 pm
Capacity
12 participants per session
Target Participants
Individuals in good physical condition who are able to participate in long hours of outdoor activities
Individuals interested in architecture, landscape design, conservation, and related fields
Registration Link
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733829
Participants who attend one village guided tour and eight workshop sessions will receive a volunteer service certificate jointly issued by the School of Architecture, CUHK and the Hong Kong Institute of Construction.
Project Title
“Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story: Co-creating Rural Place with Experimental Communal Hub and Eco-Cultural Trail”
Organisers
School of Architecture, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Hong Kong Institute of Construction
Yung Shue Au Village
Funding Support
Countryside Conservation Office
Environment Branch, Environment and Ecology Bureau
Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme
Remarks
1. Yung Shue Au is located within a restricted area. Participants are required to apply for a Closed Area Permit in advance.
2. During the project period, all boat transportation costs related to the workshops will be arranged and subsidised by the project. Participants are responsible for their own land transportation and should prepare sufficient food and drinking water.
3. The workshops will be conducted in Cantonese.
4. Workshop arrangements may be adjusted due to weather, road conditions, project progress, or the physical conditions of participants and staff without prior notice.

6. There are no shops or supply facilities in the village. Participants should prepare sufficient drinking water, sun protection, mosquito repellent, and rain gear if necessary.

“Reimagining Yung Shue Au: Co-creating a Mountain-Sea Village”
— Recruitment for Rural-placemaking Ambassadors
Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story: Co-creating Rural Place
The School of Architecture at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently organising a rural school and summer workshop centred on the concept of
rural placemaking
. We invite individuals who are passionate about Hong Kong’s rural culture and interested in hands-on practice to join us in Yung Shue Au and participate in the revitalisation and co-creation of the village landscape.
During the programme, instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction will lead participants in learning traditional construction crafts and rural practical skills. Participants may choose to attend one or multiple workshop sessions according to their availability. Those who complete nine workshop days will receive a service certificate jointly issued by the School of Architecture, CUHK and the Hong Kong Institute of Construction in recognition of their participation and contribution.
Introduction to Yung Shue Au
Located in the northeastern New Territories, Yung Shue Au is a historic Hakka village established over 300 years ago by the Wan clan. At its peak, the village was home to more than 300 residents. Owing to its proximity to the border, a British military camp was stationed in the village during the 1980s, leaving behind a unique yet little-known historical legacy.
Although the village is currently uninhabited, villagers have actively promoted village revitalisation in recent years through repairing ancestral houses, documenting village history, organising village banquets and traditional rituals, as well as reviving the Qilin dance team. These efforts reflect a deep attachment to the village and a strong commitment to cultural inheritance and community reconnection.
Vision
Co-creating Rural Placemaking
Reimagining the mountain-sea landscape through low-carbon restoration and local memories.
Spatial Practice
Improving pathways and communal resting spaces through small-scale construction.
Sensory Narratives
Transforming local history into tangible landscape interpretation experiences.
Collective Action
Connecting design thinking with rural revitalisation through practical engagement.

Yung Shue Au, Sha Tau Kok, New Territories

Village Guided Tour
Understanding the history of Yung Shue Au and learning about rural placemaking and cultural landscapes.
Material Collection
Collecting usable materials from the surrounding mountain, coastal, and village environment.
Landscape Practice
Participating in site clearing and spatial construction workshops led by instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction, focusing on rural landscape practices and traditional building techniques.

Announcements
Leadership Study Participants Recruitment 【完成線上研究，可獲HKD100報酬】誠意邀請香港小學生及家長參與領導力相關心理學研究（尤其期盼小二、小五、小六學生參與！） - Gender Studies Programme
From: HE Chuting
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
conniehe@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你想了解孩子對於學校或日常生活裡的“領導”的看法嗎？想知道孩子對於“當領導”的意願嗎？不要錯過這次有趣又有意義的研究機會。簡單進行線上研究，還有報酬可領喔~~
招募對象
：
在香港就讀小1到小6的小學生以及其父親或母親
目前各個組別依舊在積極招募，尤其小2、小5、小6組別以及各個組別的女孩子組依舊席位多多！誠摯邀請合乎要求的小朋友同家長參與~~如果你們身邊有合乎要求的小朋友和家長，也懇請幫我們多多宣傳~~
研究項目：
小學生、家長及老師的領導認知與刻板印象
研究內容：
1.孩子：1對1線上訪談（需錄音），約需1小時。
2.家長：填寫1份網上問卷，約需1小時。
報酬：
家長和孩子完成各自的研究項目後，可獲得共100港幣報酬。
參與條件：
1.兒童參加者為在港就讀小1到小6的小學生，家長參加者為該兒童的父親或母親。
2.兒童能講流利廣東話或普通話，家長能閱讀和書寫中文。
3.兒童可使用有互聯網、視頻和音頻功能的電腦或平板參與研究。
4.兒童沒有主要的身體障礙（如：視障、四肢不健全）和未被診斷有任何有關精神健康或主要的發展障礙的狀況（如：自閉症、過度活躍）。
5.請留意參加者需在此前沒有參與過本研究的“預實驗”或“教師部分”（如不清楚是否參與過也可先留下聯繫方式，稍後我們的研究人員將與您聯繫進行確認）。
如對本實驗感興趣，請通過以下鏈接報名
，我們的研究人員將盡快聯繫您：https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KzWB6HhTtOhwou
參與純屬自願性質，所收集的資料只作研究用途及保密處理。如有任何疑問，請聯繫何小姐（conniehe@link.cuhk.edu.hk)。

Child:

Parent:

Participants will receive HKD 100 in total.

From: Haerim Hwang
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
haerimhwang@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
  [Online experiment] Looking for native English speakers
Prof. Haerim Hwang (Department of English, CUHK) is looking for participants for a study on language production.
Which participants are we looking for?
- English is your first/native and dominant language
- Your graduate degree is not in the field of linguistics
- Can use your laptop/computer and have access to stable internet (no smartphones, laptops, or hotspot)
- Can participate in an experiment on Zoom in a quiet environment
- Have Chrome on your laptop/computer
How do I participate?
1. Fill out this questionnaire
-- English speakers: https://forms.gle/ttuhGGCwRx2n95kBA
2. Our research team will reach out to you, confirming your availability.
3. It will take approximately 2 hours to complete these tasks.
What do I get out of the study?
You will get HK$250 in cash upon the completion of the task.
Your participation will enhance our understanding of how people process English sentences.
Questions?
Contact Prof. Haerim Hwang at haerimhwang@cuhk.edu.hk
Ethics Approval
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics Committee SBREC (fssc02@cuhk.edu.hk) has vetted the study (Approval ID: SBRE-22-0026D). If you have any concerns regarding ethics, please contact them.
